literature.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 研究发现,预先存在的免疫力会降低病毒载量并阻断 传播,从而导致对病毒多样性的强烈选择。不同的组织施加不同的选择压力,上呼吸道有利于与人类受体高亲和力结合的病毒,而下呼吸道有利于抗体逃逸病毒。 [10.1002/advs.78843]
两种 疫苗 均诱导 HI 反应,并在第 3-4 周达到峰值。rgH5N1 疫苗 引发针对 H5N8 的高交叉反应滴度 (9.2–9.4 log 2 ),而 rgH5N8 疫苗 引发针对 H5N1 的较低交叉反应滴度 (7.25 log 2 )。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11243811/v1]
该病毒引起 SPF 鸡的轻微临床疾病和 100% 存活率,但观察到显着的呼吸道组织病理学损伤。在 BALB/c 小鼠中,它表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明哺乳动物的适应潜力较低。 [10.1186/s13567-026-01862-3]
疫苗 诱导显着的血清体液反应,在 H5N1 攻击后,它为大多数鸡提供保护并防止病毒脱落。 [10.3390/v18111285]
该审查确定了疾病优先顺序的五个明确标准,并强调了基于这些因素的诊断有效性的可变性。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11737060/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study found that pre-existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, leading to strong selection on viral diversity. [10.1002/advs.78843]

Both vaccines induced HI responses that peaked at weeks 3–4. The rgH5N1 vaccine elicited high cross-reactive titers against H5N8 (9.2–9.4 log 2 ), whereas the rgH5N8 vaccine elicited lower cross-reactive titers against H5N1 (7.25 log 2 ). [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11243811/v1]

The virus caused mild clinical disease and 100% survival in SPF chickens, but significant respiratory tract histopathological damage was observed. In BALB/c mice, it showed limited nasal replication, suggesting low mammalian adaptation potential. [10.1186/s13567-026-01862-3]
The vaccine induced a significant serum humoral response, and after the H5N1 challenge, it provided protection and prevented virus shedding in most of the chickens. [10.3390/v18111285]
The review identified five explicit criteria for disease prioritization and highlighted the variability in diagnostic effectiveness based on these factors. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11737060/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
研究发现,预先存在的免疫力会降低病毒载量并阻断 传播,从而导致对病毒多样性的强烈选择。不同的组织施加不同的选择压力,上呼吸道有利于与人类受体高亲和力结合的病毒,而下呼吸道有利于抗体逃逸病毒。 [10.1002/advs.78843]。
两种 疫苗 均诱导 HI 反应,并在第 3-4 周达到峰值。rgH5N1 疫苗 引发针对 H5N8 的高交叉反应滴度 (9.2–9.4 log 2 ),而 rgH5N8 疫苗 引发针对 H5N1 的较低交叉反应滴度 (7.25 log 2 )。
该病毒引起 SPF 鸡的轻微临床疾病和 100% 存活率,但观察到显着的呼吸道组织病理学损伤。在 BALB/c 小鼠中,它表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明哺乳动物的适应潜力较低。 [10.1186/s13567-026-01862-3]。
疫苗 诱导显着的血清体液反应,在 H5N1 攻击后,它为大多数鸡提供保护并防止病毒脱落。 [10.3390/v18111285]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
The study found that pre-existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, leading to strong selection on viral diversity. [10.1002/advs.78843].
Both vaccines induced HI responses that peaked at weeks 3–4.
The virus caused mild clinical disease and 100% survival in SPF chickens, but significant respiratory tract histopathological damage was observed.
The vaccine induced a significant serum humoral response, and after the H5N1 challenge, it provided protection and prevented virus shedding in most of the chickens. [10.3390/v18111285].

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. The study found that pre-existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, leading to strong selection on viral diversity. [10.1002/advs.78843]. Both vaccines induced HI responses that peaked at weeks 3–4. The virus caused mild clinical disease and 100% survival in SPF chickens, but significant respiratory tract histopathological damage was observed. The vaccine induced a significant serum humoral response, and after the H5N1 challenge, it provided protection and prevented virus shedding in most of the chickens. [10.3390/v18111285].

news.headline_zh: 印度推出首个本土H5N1禽流感疫苗。
news.lead_zh: 印度计划于2026年11月20日推出首个针对家禽的本土H5N1禽流感疫苗,以应对持续的禽流感暴发。
key_findings_zh: 疫苗由ICAR-NIHSAD研发,针对H5N1进化枝2.3.2.1a,该毒株导致多数禽流感暴发。
疫苗预计可减少家禽死亡和病毒传播,但部分接种家禽仍可能传播病毒。
疫苗的推出标志着印度在禽流感防控方面的重要进展,但具体实施细节尚未公布。
自2006年以来,印度已报告超过500起H5N1和H5N8禽流感暴发,造成重大经济损失。
疫苗旨在提升印度家禽业的生物安全和疾病控制能力。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 禽流感病毒在印度持续传播,对家禽业和经济构成重大风险。
news.caveats_zh: 疫苗的具体实施细节和效果仍需进一步验证。
news.headline_en: India Unveils First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine for Poultry.
news.lead_en: India is set to unveil its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry on November 20, 2026, as reported by multiple sources.
key_findings_en: The vaccine, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, targets the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain, responsible for most outbreaks in the country.
While the vaccine aims to reduce poultry deaths and virus shedding, some vaccinated birds may still shed the virus.
The vaccine is a significant step in strengthening India's disease control and biosecurity measures.
Over 500 outbreaks involving H5N1 and H5N8 have been reported since 2006, causing substantial economic losses.
The vaccine is expected to be a milestone in India's self-reliance in veterinary vaccines.
news.trend_or_risk_en: The H5N1 virus continues to pose a significant risk to poultry and economic stability in India.
news.caveats_en: The vaccine's effectiveness and implementation details remain to be confirmed.
news.brief_en: India is set to unveil its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry on November 20, 2026, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD. The vaccine targets the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain, which has been responsible for most outbreaks in the country. While the vaccine aims to reduce poultry deaths and virus shedding, some vaccinated birds may still shed the virus. The development is a major milestone in India's efforts to combat avian influenza, but details on commercial availability, pricing, and deployment are not yet specified. The vaccine is expected to enhance preparedness against the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks, which have caused significant economic losses since 2006.

papers.title: Serologic Evidence of Avian Influenza Virus Exposure in Livestock, Egypt, 2024–2026
papers.abstract: Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%-4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt, driven by global concern over the spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Egypt between 2024 and 2026, focusing on domestic livestock to assess exposure to avian influenza viruses.
analysis.methods: The researchers tested livestock specimens for antibodies against specific avian influenza subtypes using serologic assays.
analysis.main_results: Influenza H9N2 antibodies were detected in 2.5% of tested animals, while H5N1 antibodies were found in 2.9%-4.5% of the tested population.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be circulating in livestock, highlighting the need for further investigation into the dynamics of host infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the importance of additional surveillance to better understand the transmission and infection dynamics of avian influenza viruses in livestock populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides moderate confidence in its findings, as it is based on serologic evidence and does not include detailed longitudinal or molecular data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential spillover of endemic avian influenza viruses into domestic livestock in Egypt between 2024 and 2026. Serologic testing revealed H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% of animals and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%-4.5% of the tested population. These findings suggest possible circulation of avian influenza viruses in livestock, emphasizing the need for further surveillance to understand host infection dynamics. The study's results provide moderate confidence in the presence of avian influenza exposure in livestock, though they lack detailed molecular or longitudinal data. The findings have implications for monitoring avian influenza in animal populations and assessing zoonotic risks, contributing to the broader understanding of influenza virus transmission dynamics.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Avian influenza A(H9N2) viruses pose a pandemic threat, having acquired preferential binding to human receptors and the ability to evade immunity in chickens. However, the selective forces driving these traits remain unclear. Here, we show how anatomical compartmentalization within chickens shapes hemagglutinin (HA) evolution. Using deep mutational scanning coupled with in vivo studies, we find that pre‐existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, thereby imposing strong selection on viral diversity. Distinct tissues exert divergent selection pressures in immunized chickens. The upper respiratory tract mainly enriches viruses with high‐affinity binding to human‐type receptors, whereas the lower respiratory tract preferentially favors antibody‐escape viruses. This functional difference was validated using variants carrying defined substitutions, which showed fitness aligned with their respective compartment. Our results demonstrate that tissue‐specific selection within an avian host can concurrently shape viral diversity toward human adaptation and immune evasion, providing a mechanism for the emergence of variants with pandemic potential in poultry.

papers.title: H9N2 avian influenza virus in Bangladesh: three genetically distinct co-circulating subgroups retain a largely conserved antigenic phenotype
papers.abstract: Abstract Low pathogenic avian influenza (LPAI) H9N2 viruses are endemic in poultry across Bangladesh, causing substantial economic losses and posing a persistent zoonotic risk. Although genetic surveillance has documented ongoing viral evolution, the relationship between genetic diversification and antigenic change remains poorly understood. This study investigated the genetic diversity, reassortment, and antigenic characteristics of contemporary H9N2 viruses circulating in Bangladesh. Phylogenetic analysis of 219 sampled sequences revealed three genetically distinct monophyletic haemagglutinin (HA) G-lineage sub-groups, each characterised by unique amino acid substitutions. In contrast, neuraminidase (NA) displayed similar genetic diversity without distinct phylogenetic clusters. A dual-metric analysis of paired HA and NA phylogenies identified 20 putative reassortant H9N2 viruses. Further analysis showed that genetic diversity was geographically structured; however, all three HA subgroups co-circulated across multiple regions, and some live bird markets contained representatives of all three groups simultaneously, suggesting that live bird markets may facilitate mixing between genetically distinct viruses, and create opportunities for reassortment among otherwise geographically separated strains. Despite substantial genetic diversity and reassortment, all viruses remained antigenically similar based on haemagglutination inhibition and virus neutralisation assays. However, a representative strain from one subgroup induced significantly lower homologous and heterologous antibody titres, suggesting reduced immunogenicity. Our findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between genetic evolution and antigenic change in Bangladeshi H9N2 viruses. While reassortment and genetic diversification continue to shape viral populations, antigenic properties remain largely conserved, supporting the continued relevance of current vaccine strategies while highlighting the importance of ongoing genetic and antigenic surveillance. Importance Low pathogenic avian influenza (LPAI) H9N2 viruses remain endemic in Bangladesh and continue to evolve through genetic diversification and reassortment. This study demonstrates that, despite the emergence of three distinct HA genetic subgroups and frequent reassortment events, contemporary Bangladeshi H9N2 viruses remain antigenically conserved. These findings reveal an important disconnect between genetic evolution and antigenic change, indicating that genetic divergence alone may not predict vaccine effectiveness. The co-circulation of multiple viral subgroups within live bird markets highlights their role as hubs for viral mixing and reassortment, emphasizing the need for targeted surveillance in these settings. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 低致病性 禽流感 (LPAI) H9N2 病毒在孟加拉国家禽中流行,造成重大经济损失并构成持续的人畜共患风险。尽管遗传监测已经记录了正在进行的病毒进化,但遗传多样性和抗原变化之间的关系仍然知之甚少。这项研究调查了孟加拉国流行的当代 H9N2 病毒的遗传多样性、重排和抗原特征。对 219 个采样序列的系统发育分析揭示了三个遗传上不同的单系血凝素 (HA) G 谱系亚群,每个亚群都以独特的氨基酸取代为特征。相比之下,神经氨酸酶(NA)表现出相似的遗传多样性,但没有明显的系统发育簇。对配对 HA 和 NA 系统发育的双度量分析确定了 20 种假定的重配 H9N2 病毒。进一步分析表明,遗传多样性具有地理结构;然而,所有三个HA亚群在多个地区共同流通,并且一些活禽市场同时包含所有三个亚群的代表,这表明活禽市场可能促进遗传上不同的病毒之间的混合,并为其他地理上分离的毒株之间的重配创造机会。尽管存在大量的遗传多样性和重配,但根据血凝抑制和病毒中和测定,所有病毒在抗原上仍然相似。然而,一个亚组的代表性菌株诱导的同源和异源抗体滴度显着降低,表明免疫原性降低。我们的研究结果表明,孟加拉国 H9N2 病毒的 进化 基因与抗原变化之间存在显着脱节。虽然重配和遗传多样化继续塑造病毒种群,但抗原特性在很大程度上仍然保守,支持当前 疫苗 策略的持续相关性,同时强调持续遗传和抗原 监测 的重要性。重要性 低致病性 禽流感 (LPAI) H9N2 病毒在孟加拉国仍然流行,并通过遗传多样化和重组继续进化。这项研究表明,尽管出现了三个不同的 HA 遗传亚群和频繁的重配事件,当代孟加拉国 H9N2 病毒仍然保持抗原保守性。这些发现揭示了遗传 进化 和抗原变化之间的重要脱节,表明仅遗传差异可能无法预测 疫苗 的有效性。活禽市场内多个病毒亚群的共同循环凸显了它们作为病毒混合和重组中心的作用,强调了在这些环境中需要有针对性的 监测。虽然目前的 疫苗 策略可能对流行菌株仍然有效,但免疫原性降低的亚组的鉴定强调了持续监测遗传和表型特征的重要性。总之,这些发现为支持孟加拉国及其他地区的风险评估、疫苗 评估和 禽流感 控制计划提供了关键证据。

papers.title: Protective and Cross-Protective Efficacies of Inactivated Recombinant H5N1 and H5N8 Vaccines Against Highly-Pathogenic Avian Influenza H5-Type Strains in Chickens
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Co-circulation of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 and H5N8 viruses (clade 2.3.4.4b) threatens poultry production and public health, so vaccines that protect against both viruses are needed. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-protective efficacy of inactivated recombinant (reverse genetics-derived) rgH5N1 and rgH5N8 vaccines (10 8.0 50% embryo infectious dose [EID 50 ]/dose) against homologous and heterologous HPAI H5-type challenge in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens. Vaccine strains were inactivated with 0.2% formalin and emulsified with Montanide ISA 71 VG adjuvant. SPF chickens (n = 10 per group) received rgH5N1 (G1), rgH5N8 (G2), or phosphate-buffered saline (G3, unvaccinated controls). Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers were measured at weeks 2, 3, and 4 post-vaccination. At week 4, birds were challenged intranasally with homologous or heterologous HPAI virus (10 6 EID 50 /0.1 mL) and monitored for 10 days for clinical signs and mortality; viral shedding was assessed by real-time RT-PCR. Both vaccines induced HI responses that peaked at weeks 3–4. The rgH5N1 vaccine elicited high cross-reactive titers against H5N8 (9.2–9.4 log 2 ), whereas the rgH5N8 vaccine elicited lower cross-reactive titers against H5N1 (7.25 log 2 ). Both vaccines conferred 100% survival and no detectable viral shedding (cycle threshold [Ct] > 38) after homologous and heterologous challenge. All unvaccinated controls died, with high viral loads detected from day 3. Both inactivated vaccines provided complete cross-protection against heterologous H5-type challenge under controlled conditions, preventing mortality and detectable viral shedding. This supports their potential for controlling co-circulating H5N1 and H5N8 viruses in poultry, although confirmation in larger groups under field conditions is needed.

papers.title: Characterization and vaccine-induced immunity of a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus with H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China
papers.abstract: Abstract In December 2025, an H6N2 avian influenza virus (A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, NL04) was isolated from a chicken outbreak in Henan, China with 15% field mortality and severe respiratory disease. Genome sequencing confirmed it is a novel reassortant possessing a waterfowl‐origin H6‐derived HA, H9N2‐derived NA, and the complete internal‐gene cassette of the H9N2 G57 genotype. Although NL04 caused only mild clinical disease and 100% survival in experimentally infected specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens, prominent respiratory‐tract histopathological damage was observed, revealing a marked phenotypic discrepancy between laboratory outcomes and severe field‐reported mortality that is likely driven by complex commercial‐farm risk factors. Tissue viral loads in SPF chickens peaked in nasal turbinates and the Harderian gland, confirming its predominant respiratory tropism. In BALB/c mice, NL04 exhibited limited nasal replication, indicating low mammalian‐adaptation potential. We further evaluated an inactivated vaccine candidate based on NL04. The vaccine induced robust humoral immunity, reduced viral shedding after homologous challenge, and elicited cross‐neutralizing antibodies against a heterologous H6N1 isolate. Our findings highlight the veterinary relevance of this unique H6N2 reassortant and stress the value of continuous genomic surveillance among poultry to prevent emerging avian‐influenza threats.

Genome sequencing confirmed it is a novel reassortant possessing a waterfowl‐origin H6‐derived HA, H9N2‐derived NA, and the complete internal‐gene cassette of the H9N2 G57 genotype. Although NL04 caused only mild clinical disease and 100% survival in experimentally infected specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens, prominent respiratory‐tract histopathological damage was observed, revealing a marked phenotypic discrepancy between laboratory outcomes and severe field‐reported mortality that is likely driven by complex commercial‐farm risk factors. Tissue viral loads in SPF chickens peaked in nasal turbinates and the Harderian gland, confirming its predominant respiratory tropism. In BALB/c mice, NL04 exhibited limited nasal replication, indicating low mammalian‐adaptation potential. We further evaluated an inactivated vaccine candidate based on NL04. The vaccine induced robust humoral immunity, reduced viral shedding after homologous challenge, and elicited cross‐neutralizing antibodies against a heterologous H6N1 isolate. Our findings highlight the veterinary relevance of this unique H6N2 reassortant and stress the value of continuous genomic surveillance among poultry to prevent emerging avian‐influenza threats.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus and assess its potential to induce immunity through vaccination, addressing the need to understand emerging avian influenza threats and their implications for poultry health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved isolating the H6N2 avian influenza virus from a chicken outbreak in Henan, China, and analyzing its characteristics in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens and BALB/c mice, with a focus on its pathogenicity and vaccine-induced immunity.
analysis.methods: Genome sequencing was used to confirm the viral composition, and SPF chickens were experimentally infected to evaluate clinical disease and histopathological damage. BALB/c mice were also tested for nasal replication to assess mammalian adaptation potential.
analysis.main_results: The virus caused mild clinical disease and 100% survival in SPF chickens, but significant respiratory tract histopathological damage was observed. In BALB/c mice, it showed limited nasal replication, suggesting low mammalian adaptation potential.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a phenotypic discrepancy between laboratory outcomes and field-reported severity, likely influenced by commercial farm risk factors, and highlight the importance of genomic surveillance for emerging avian influenza threats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the veterinary relevance of this H6N2 reassortant and emphasizes the need for continuous genomic monitoring in poultry to mitigate potential zoonotic risks and improve disease prevention strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus isolated from a chicken outbreak in Henan, China, which exhibits severe field mortality but causes mild disease in laboratory SPF chickens. The virus possesses a waterfowl-origin H6 HA, H9N2-derived NA, and internal genes from the H9N2 G57 genotype. Experimental infection in SPF chickens showed 100% survival but prominent respiratory tract damage, while BALB/c mice exhibited limited nasal replication, suggesting low mammalian adaptation potential. An inactivated vaccine candidate based on NL04 was evaluated, inducing robust humoral immunity and reducing viral shedding after homologous challenge. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in poultry to monitor emerging avian influenza threats and prevent zoonotic transmission. However, the findings are based on controlled laboratory conditions, and the phenotypic discrepancy between field and lab results may be influenced by commercial farm risk factors, limiting the generalizability of the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在表征一种新型 H6N2 禽流感 重配病毒,并评估其通过 疫苗接种 诱导免疫的潜力,满足了解新出现的 禽流感 威胁及其对家禽健康影响的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究从中国河南的一只鸡 暴发 中分离出 H6N2 禽流感 病毒,并分析其在无特定病原体 (SPF) 鸡和 BALB/c 小鼠中的特征,重点研究其致病性和 疫苗 诱导的免疫。
elements_zh.methods: 采用基因组测序确认病毒组成,并实验感染SPF鸡以评估临床疾病和组织病理学损伤。BALB/c 小鼠还接受了鼻复制测试,以评估哺乳动物的适应潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: 该病毒引起 SPF 鸡的轻微临床疾病和 100% 存活率,但观察到显着的呼吸道组织病理学损伤。在 BALB/c 小鼠中,它表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明哺乳动物的适应潜力较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果揭示了实验室结果与现场报告的严重程度之间的表型差异,可能受到商业农场风险因素的影响,并强调了 基因组监测 对于新兴 禽流感 威胁的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调了这种 H6N2 重配病毒的兽医相关性,并强调需要对家禽进行连续基因组监测,以减轻潜在的人畜共患病风险并改进疾病预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据仅限于实验室环境,观察到的表型差异可能受到实验中未控制的环境因素的影响,导致结论可信度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 2025 年 12 月,从中国河南的一只鸡 暴发 中分离到 H6N2 死亡率 病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04),该病毒具有 15% 的田 死亡率 并伴有严重呼吸道疾病。基因组 测序证实它是一种新型重配体,具有水禽来源的 H6 衍生的 HA、H9N2 衍生的 NA 和 H9N2 G57 基因型的完整内部基因盒。尽管 NL04 仅引起轻微的临床疾病,且实验感染的无特定病原体 (SPF) 鸡的存活率为 100%,但观察到显着的呼吸道组织病理学损伤,揭示实验室结果与现场报告的严重 死亡率 之间存在显着的表型差异,这可能是由复杂的商业农场风险因素驱动的。SPF 鸡的组织病毒载量在鼻甲和哈德氏腺中达到峰值,证实了其主要的呼吸道趋向性。在 BALB/c 小鼠中,NL04 表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明哺乳动物适应潜力较低。我们进一步评估了基于 NL04 的灭活 疫苗 候选药物。疫苗 诱导强大的体液免疫,减少同源攻击后的病毒脱落,并引发针对异源 H6N1 分离株的交叉中和抗体。我们的研究结果强调了这种独特的 H6N2 重配病毒的兽医相关性,并强调了在家禽中连续 基因组监测 预防新出现的禽流感威胁的价值。

papers.title: Genetic characterization of avian influenza H14 viruses in Guangdong, China: evidence of intercontinental transmission and reassortment in the East Asian-Australasian flyway.
papers.abstract: H14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. This study investigated the ecological origins and zoonotic potential of H14 viruses in southern China. The isolates were characterised by full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, together with assessment of avian- and human-type receptor binding, in vitro replication in avian, mammalian, and human cell lines, and in vivo pathogenicity in mice. Four H14 AIVs (one H14N6, two H14N7, and one H14N8) were isolated. We identified a novel H14 transmission network involving Mareca penelope and various shorebird species, indicating a multihost dispersal mechanism. Guangdong isolates formed a distinct subclade within the Eurasian lineage, closely related to Russian and Cambodian strains. The isolates (SZ3742/H14N6, ZJ3523/H14N7, SZ3536/H14N8) exhibited dual receptor-binding specificity for avian (α-2,3) and human (α-2,6) sialic acids. Strain-dependent replication in human A549 cells showed SZ3742/H14N6 peaked comparably to DF-1 cells but lower than MDCK cells, while the others had lower peak titres. All isolates replicated transiently at low titres in mouse lungs with limited pathogenicity. Molecular characterisation revealed mammalian adaptation markers and a typical HA cleavage site motif (PDKQTR↓GLF). This study presents the first evidence of H14 AIV circulation in Guangdong, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance in the East Asian -Australasian Flyway.

source_records.abstract: H14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. This study investigated the ecological origins and zoonotic potential of H14 viruses in southern China. The isolates were characterised by full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, together with assessment of avian- and human-type receptor binding, in vitro replication in avian, mammalian, and human cell lines, and in vivo pathogenicity in mice. Four H14 AIVs (one H14N6, two H14N7, and one H14N8) were isolated. We identified a novel H14 transmission network involving Mareca penelope and various shorebird species, indicating a multihost dispersal mechanism. Guangdong isolates formed a distinct subclade within the Eurasian lineage, closely related to Russian and Cambodian strains. The isolates (SZ3742/H14N6, ZJ3523/H14N7, SZ3536/H14N8) exhibited dual receptor-binding specificity for avian (α-2,3) and human (α-2,6) sialic acids. Strain-dependent replication in human A549 cells showed SZ3742/H14N6 peaked comparably to DF-1 cells but lower than MDCK cells, while the others had lower peak titres. All isolates replicated transiently at low titres in mouse lungs with limited pathogenicity. Molecular characterisation revealed mammalian adaptation markers and a typical HA cleavage site motif (PDKQTR↓GLF). This study presents the first evidence of H14 AIV circulation in Guangdong, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance in the East Asian -Australasian Flyway.

papers.title: Poultry and Livestock Disease Surveillance, Diagnosis, and Control
papers.abstract: Abstract Infectious diseases of poultry and ruminants limit production, disrupt trade and threaten human health. The last decade brought panzootic H5N1 avian influenza, its spillover into dairy cattle, and incursions of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), peste des petits ruminants (PPR) and lumpy skin disease into Europe. This critical review compares diagnostic, surveillance and prevention approaches for priority diseases of poultry (avian influenza, Newcastle disease, Marek's disease, coccidiosis, fowlpox) and ruminants (FMD, brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, PPR, lumpy skin disease, bluetongue) in literature published between 2015 and 2026, with global coverage and attention to low- and middle-income countries. Diseases were prioritised using five explicit criteria. The synthesis shows that test performance depends on purpose, specimen and prevalence, and that access and logistics limit diagnosis more often than assay chemistry. Vaccines can reshape pathogen populations, as leaky Marek's disease vaccines and FMD carrier animals illustrate, so vaccination needs matched monitoring. Economic estimates rest on incompatible methods, cross-species surveillance is needed after H5N1 emerged in cattle, and antimicrobial stewardship is essential in poultry. We propose a tiered surveillance–diagnostic–intervention workflow for resource-limited settings and list research priorities, including field validation of rapid and genomic tools and harmonised economic frameworks.

papers.title: An air of possibility: a systematic review of windborne transmission of avian influenza virus in poultry
papers.abstract: Abstract High pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) poses significant risks to poultry production, wildlife conservation, and public health. While direct contact primarily drives avian influenza virus (AIV) spread within infected flocks, introduction onto farms is more often attributed to indirect routes, including environmental contamination from wildlife reservoirs and transmission from other infected premises. Among plausible transmission pathways, the potential for windborne transmission remains a critical knowledge gap. We conducted a systematic review to assess current understanding of windborne AIV transmission in poultry. We searched two databases using terms related to influenza, poultry, and windborne transmission. Of 414 manuscripts identified, 47 met inclusion criteria. Most studies were conducted in the Netherlands ( n = 9) and the United States ( n = 9). Research primarily focused on high pathogenicity H5 strains ( n = 25) in commercial settings. The majority of studies ( n = 33) were published after 2014 following the emergence of HPAIV H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b. Findings suggest that environmental factors such as wind speed and direction may facilitate virus spread over several kilometers; however, findings were inconsistent across experimental studies, field investigations, and modelling analyses. Windborne transmission may contribute to outbreak dynamics, particularly in high-density production areas, but its relative importance remains uncertain. Several studies recommend incorporating wind parameters into outbreak investigations and strengthening biosecurity measures, such as air filtration and wind barriers. While windborne transmission of AIV is a plausible and potentially significant route of spread, further research is needed to improve detection methods, refine predictive models, and address gaps in real-time field data linking virus detection to actual transmission events. This will enhance our capacity to prevent and control AIV outbreaks, especially in high-risk regions.

papers.title: Optimizing Avian Influenza Viral RNA Enrichment from Water: A Comparison of Concentration Methods for Low-Volume Samples
papers.abstract: Abstract Feed-baited water bins may provide a complementary approach for avian influenza virus (AIV) surveillance in wild waterbird populations. In a previous study, water from these bins was sampled using swabs after exposure to visiting birds, but the low sample volume limited the detection and subsequent characterization of AIV RNA (F. Homeier-Bachmann, L. Globig, One Health 23:101548, 2026, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101548). Here, we compared five sample-processing methods for improving AIV RNA detection in small (40-mL) water samples (tap and brackish water) spiked with an AIV of the H4N6 subtype under simulated field conditions: swab sampling, polyethylene glycol precipitation, activated carbon capture, combined activated carbon capture and polyethylene glycol precipitation (AC/PEG), and electronegative membrane adsorption (EM). AC/PEG and EM showed the strongest overall performance based on RT-qPCR results, although their relative performance varied across experimental conditions. The qPCR-derived viral signal was generally higher in tap water than in brackish water, whereas wheat presence was associated with a lower signal, particularly for swab sampling. Subsequent testing was conducted to ascertain the most effective storage conditions with regard to temperature and duration. During storage, AIV RNA detection remained relatively stable at −20 °C for up to four weeks, with only minor increases in mean Ct values in both water matrices. Greater increases were observed at room temperature and 4 °C, with significantly higher Ct values at both temperatures than at −20 °C in both water matrices at Weeks 2 and 4 ( p < 0.05). These findings support the potential of AC/PEG and EM to facilitate the recovery, detection and subsequent characterization of AIV from low-volume water samples by improving viral RNA detection using RT-qPCR. Given its overall performance and lower cost compared with EM, AC/PEG may represent a practical option for field-based surveillance. Regarding storage, −20 °C provided the best conditions for maintaining AIV RNA detection, with relatively stable results for up to four weeks. Importance Environmental surveillance can complement conventional approaches for detecting avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation in wild waterbirds. Feed-baited water bins offer a non-invasive sampling strategy, but processing low-volume water samples may require viral enrichment to improve AIV RNA detection. Here, we show that combined activated carbon capture and polyethylene glycol precipitation (AC/PEG) is a promising, cost-effective method for improving AIV RNA detection in low-volume water samples. These findings highlight the potential of viral enrichment methods to support the use of simple, practical and non-invasive approaches for AIV surveillance.

papers.title: Pre-existing cross-subtype serological responses against H5Nx in health care workers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A rise in cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b in humans has been reported since 2023. Although influenza seasonal vaccination (H1N1/H3N2) was shown to be effective against cases of reinfection with endemic influenza A viruses (IAVs), its capacity to elicit cross-reactive antibodies against (H5N1) remains unclear. Here, we measured vaccine-elicited antibody responses against seasonal (H1N1/H3N2) and various avian subtypes A (H5Nx) using plasma samples from the CRCHUM Health Care Workers cohort in Montreal, Canada, during the 2024 influenza seasonal vaccination. The capacity of their plasma to recognize hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) antigens from ten influenza strains was measured. Their neutralizing activity, as well as their capacity to mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against cells stably expressing HA and NA, was measured. Overall, seasonal vaccination against H1N1/H3N2 elicited antibodies able to recognize several HA and NA, and in some individuals, this translated to increased neutralization and ADCC activity, including against H5Nx. This study provides insightful information on how vaccination shapes cross-reactive antibody responses against avian H5Nx. IMPORTANCE Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are endemic in the human population and responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths every year, occasionally leading to influenza pandemics. Since 2023, there has been a rise in avian IAV infections in humans, with some deaths reported, mostly related to the H5N1 subtype clade 2.3.4.4b. Seasonal vaccines against IAVs are effective, but their efficacy against avian IAVs is not well known. Here, following influenza seasonal vaccination in a cohort of adults, we report highly heterogeneous serological responses, possibly due to pre-existing immunity and HA sequence similarity. These findings provide insight into the breadth of pre-existing and vaccine-induced immunity against H5 influenza viruses and may inform the development of vaccination strategies aimed at providing broader protection against emerging influenza viruses.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 自 2023 年以来,据报道人类 高致病性禽流感 A (H5N1) 分支 2.3.4.4b 病例有所增加。尽管季节性流感 高致病性禽流感 (H1N1/H3N2) 被证明可有效对抗地方性甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 的再感染病例,但其引发针对 (H5N1) 交叉反应抗体的能力仍不清楚。在这里,我们使用 2024 年流感季节性 疫苗接种 期间加拿大蒙特利尔 CRCHUM 卫生保健工作者 队列研究 的血浆样本测量了 疫苗 引发的针对季节性 (H1N1/H3N2) 和各种禽类 A 亚型 (H5Nx) 的抗体反应。测量了它们的血浆识别十种流感病毒株的血凝素(HA)和神经氨酸酶(NA)抗原的能力。测量了它们的中和活性,以及​​它们介导针对稳定表达 HA 和 NA 的细胞的抗体依赖性细胞毒性 (ADCC) 的能力。总体而言,针对 H1N1/H3N2 的季节性 疫苗接种 引发了能够识别多种 HA 和 NA 的抗体,并且在某些个体中,这转化为中和和 ADCC 活性的增加,包括针对 H5Nx 的抗体。这项研究提供了有关 疫苗接种 如何形成针对禽类 H5Nx 的交叉反应抗体反应的深刻信息。重要性 甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 在人群中流行,每年导致数十万人死亡,有时还会导致流感大流行。自 2023 年以来,人类感染禽类 IAV 的数量有所增加,并报告了一些死亡病例,其中大部分与 H5N1 亚型分支 2.3.4.4b 有关。季节性 疫苗 对 IAV 有效,但其对禽 IAV 的功效尚不清楚。在这里,在成人 队列研究 中出现季节性流感 队列研究 后,我们报告了高度异质性的血清学反应,可能是由于预先存在的免疫力和 HA 序列相似性。这些发现提供了对预先存在的和 疫苗 诱导的针对 H5 流感病毒的免疫力的广度的深入了解,并可能为 疫苗接种 策略的开发提供信息,该策略旨在针对新出现的流感病毒提供更广泛的保护。

papers.title: Bovine myxovirus resistance protein (Mx)1, but not Mx2, mediates antiviral activity against human and avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The antiviral roles of bovine host defense factors, including myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2), remain relatively understudied. We examined bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessed their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Conversely, knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. Further, bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. Known mutations that reduce human MxA (hMxA) activity also impaired bMx1 function, and mutations in the viral nucleoprotein (NP) associated with resistance to hMxA also reduced virus sensitivity to bMx1. Furthermore, phylogenetic analysis showed that a small minority (>0.03%) of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry some of these NP mutations. These findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or opportunistic reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses have spilled over into dairy cows and have been circulating on dairy farms in the United States since 2024. The innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses have not been extensively studied. In this study, we focused on Mx proteins, a key part of the innate immune defense system toward viruses. We specifically looked at bovine Mx proteins and demonstrated antiviral activity toward different influenza viruses, including the highly pathogenic strains. We also showed that the mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein. Further, we found that a small minority of these avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins. Overall, this work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral roles of bovine Mx1 and Mx2 proteins against avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, which have recently infected dairy cows in the United States. The research focuses on understanding how these proteins mediate immune responses and their potential to inhibit viral replication. The study highlights the importance of bovine innate immune responses in controlling avian influenza viruses, which may have implications for surveillance and risk assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒最近感染了美国的奶牛,引起了对人类 跨物种溢出 的担忧。牛 宿主 防御因子(包括粘病毒抗性蛋白(bMx1 和 bMx2))的 抗病毒药物 作用仍相对未得到充分研究。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们检测了 HPAI H5N1 感染后分化牛细胞中 bMx1/bMx2 的诱导,并使用过表达、敲低和诱变方法评估了它们的 抗病毒药物 活性。bMx1 和 bMx2 在乳腺细胞中的诱导作用比在气管细胞中的诱导作用更强。
elements_zh.methods: 我们专门研究了牛 Mx 蛋白,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对不同流感病毒(包括高致病性毒株)的活性。已知的 突变 可以降低人类 MxA (hMxA) 活性,同时也会损害 bMx1 功能,而与 hMxA 抗性相关的病毒核蛋白 (NP) 中的 突变 也会降低病毒对 bMx1 的敏感性。
elements_zh.main_results: bMx1 而非 bMx2 的过表达可显着抑制季节性甲型流感病毒 (IAV)、低致病性和 高致病性禽流感 病毒,包括 H5N1 2.3.4.4b,但不能抑制乙型流感病毒。bMx1 的敲低导致 IAV 生长增强。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,虽然当前的 H5N1 病毒在很大程度上仍然对 bMx1 敏感,但病毒 进化 或机会性重配可能会导致 Mx 耐药性并增加大流行风险。此外,我们发现这些禽类病毒中的一小部分具有与牛 Mx1 和人 MxA 蛋白抗性相关的 突变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 总体而言,这项工作强调了高致病性流感病毒通过在牛(一种与人类关系密切的哺乳动物物种)中持续传播而增加的大流行风险。牛对流感病毒的先天性 抗病毒药物 免疫应答 尚未得到广泛研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据并未报告研究的局限性或证据强度。这些发现基于牛细胞的实验方法,表明对病毒耐药性和大流行风险的潜在影响。

papers.title: Efficacy of a Recombinant Newcastle Disease Virus Expressing H5N8 HA Against H5N1 Avian Influenza Virus (Clade 2.3.4.4b) in Broiler Chickens
papers.abstract: Background: Since November 2022, the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus subtype H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused high mortality among wild birds and poultry in Peru. Vaccines, such as recombinant Newcastle disease virus (rNDV)-vectored vaccines expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) antigen of avian influenza virus (AIV), are considered effective for preventing AI; however, the HA protein in the vaccine must be antigenically matched to the field virus to prevent mortality and virus shedding caused by AI. In this study, we developed a live rNDV-vectored vaccine expressing an HA protein with antigenic similarity to the HA of field-circulating AIV. Methods: The rNDV rLS1 strain (the parental virus) was used as a viral vector to develop the rLS1-HAOpti vaccine (an rNDV expressing the HA protein of H5N8 clade 2.3.4.4b) through reverse genetics. The immunogenicity and efficacy of the live vaccine against an HPAI H5N1 (clade 2.3.4.4b) challenge were evaluated in broiler chickens. Results: The vaccine induced a significant serum humoral response. After the H5N1 challenge, the vaccine provided protection and prevented virus shedding in most of the chickens. Conclusions: The rNDV vaccine candidate provided complete protection against mortality and clinical disease in broiler chickens challenged with H5N1 under the tested experimental conditions.

Vaccines, such as recombinant Newcastle disease virus (rNDV)-vectored vaccines expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) antigen of avian influenza virus (AIV), are considered effective for preventing AI; however, the HA protein in the vaccine must be antigenically matched to the field virus to prevent mortality and virus shedding caused by AI. In this study, we developed a live rNDV-vectored vaccine expressing an HA protein with antigenic similarity to the HA of field-circulating AIV. Methods: The rNDV rLS1 strain (the parental virus) was used as a viral vector to develop the rLS1-HAOpti vaccine (an rNDV expressing the HA protein of H5N8 clade 2.3.4.4b) through reverse genetics. The immunogenicity and efficacy of the live vaccine against an HPAI H5N1 (clade 2.3.4.4b) challenge were evaluated in broiler chickens. Results: The vaccine induced a significant serum humoral response. After the H5N1 challenge, the vaccine provided protection and prevented virus shedding in most of the chickens. Conclusions: The rNDV vaccine candidate provided complete protection against mortality and clinical disease in broiler chickens challenged with H5N1 under the tested experimental conditions.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:自 2022 年 11 月以来,高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 病毒亚型 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b 导致秘鲁 野生鸟类 和家禽中 死亡率 较高。疫苗,例如表达禽流感病毒(AIV)血凝素(HA)抗原的重组新城疫病毒(rNDV)载体疫苗,被认为可有效预防AI;然而,疫苗中的HA蛋白必须与野外病毒抗原匹配,以防止死亡率和AI引起的病毒脱落。在这项研究中,我们开发了一种活 rNDV 载体 疫苗,其表达的 HA 蛋白与外地循环 AIV 的 HA 具有抗原相似性。方法:以rNDV rLS1毒株(亲本病毒)为病毒媒介,通过反向遗传学开发rLS1-HAOpti 疫苗(表达H5N8进化枝2.3.4.4b的HA蛋白的rNDV)。在肉鸡中评估了活 疫苗 针对 HPAI H5N1(进化枝 2.3.4.4b)攻击的免疫原性和功效。结果:疫苗 诱导显着的血清体液反应。H5N1 攻击后,疫苗 为大多数鸡提供了保护并防止病毒传播。结论:在测试的实验条件下,rNDV 疫苗 候选药物为 H5N1 攻击的肉鸡提供了针对 死亡率 和临床疾病的完全保护。

papers.title: Inter-population connectivity of southern elephant seals and the likely intra-species transmission pathways of high pathogenicity avian influenza
papers.abstract: High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has spread beyond birds to affect seals across the Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic region, with southern elephant seals ( Mirounga leonina ) particularly devastated. The virus, likely introduced via spillover from infected migratory birds, has killed tens of thousands of adult seals and pups throughout most of their range. We used twenty years of elephant seal movement data from the southern Indian and Pacific oceans to assess whether seal-to-seal transmission could spread HPAI H5N1 between breeding colonies, despite the vast distances separating them (Marion Island, Iles Crozet, Iles Kerguelen, and Macquarie Island). There was substantial overlap in seals’ at-sea distributions during their winter post-moult trips, when seals travel for weeks at average speeds of 3.5 km/h. Two transmission pathways were examined: (1) terrestrial “stepping stone” routes, where infected seals could pass the virus between colonies during short intervals to remain infectious were feasible from Marion Island to Kerguelen but not from Kerguelen to Macquarie Island; and (2) at-sea encounters between seals, which occurred frequently enough to enable transmission. The findings suggest that once established at Macquarie Island, the virus could potentially spread further to New Zealand’s sub-Antarctic islands and mainland New Zealand. While seal-to-seal transmission appears possible, we conclude this is unlikely. Nonetheless, understanding at-sea contact rates enhances knowledge of H5N1 epidemiology and demonstrates the value of combining long-term population monitoring with movement data to understand wildlife disease dynamics.

We used twenty years of elephant seal movement data from the southern Indian and Pacific oceans to assess whether seal-to-seal transmission could spread HPAI H5N1 between breeding colonies, despite the vast distances separating them (Marion Island, Iles Crozet, Iles Kerguelen, and Macquarie Island). There was substantial overlap in seals’ at-sea distributions during their winter post-moult trips, when seals travel for weeks at average speeds of 3.5 km/h. Two transmission pathways were examined: (1) terrestrial “stepping stone” routes, where infected seals could pass the virus between colonies during short intervals to remain infectious were feasible from Marion Island to Kerguelen but not from Kerguelen to Macquarie Island; and (2) at-sea encounters between seals, which occurred frequently enough to enable transmission. The findings suggest that once established at Macquarie Island, the virus could potentially spread further to New Zealand’s sub-Antarctic islands and mainland New Zealand. While seal-to-seal transmission appears possible, we conclude this is unlikely. Nonetheless, understanding at-sea contact rates enhances knowledge of H5N1 epidemiology and demonstrates the value of combining long-term population monitoring with movement data to understand wildlife disease dynamics.

The research highlights the spread of the virus from migratory birds to seals, with significant mortality observed in adult seals and pups. papers.title: Infection and transmission dynamics of bovine and human influenza A H5N1 viruses in mouse and hamster models
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Here we investigated the pathogenesis and contact transmission of bovine- and human-derived highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b genotype B3.13 viruses in mammalian models. Using reverse genetics, we rescued three naturally occurring viruses, rTX2/24 (bovine-derived), rTexas/37, and rMichigan/90 (both human-derived), and compared their infection dynamics, replication, and pathogenicity with the wild-type bovine TX2/24 strain in vitro and in vivo . All four viruses demonstrated comparable replication kinetics in four mammalian cell lines. However, the rMichigan/90 strain exhibited smaller plaques in bovine and human cells. In vivo studies showed that mice infected with any of the viruses succumbed to infection within 4–5 days; however, mice infected with the rMichigan/90 virus exhibited slightly lower viral replication and shedding compared with the other strains. The hamster model showed a milder infection phenotype than mice in which all viruses induced body weight loss and oral shedding, with robust virus replication observed in tissues, but the rMichigan/90 virus presented reduced replication and shedding. Contact transmission studies in hamsters revealed limited transmissibility for these viruses, with only one out of four animals inoculated with the rMichigan/90 virus transmitting it to a naïve contact. These findings indicate that both bovine- and human-derived H5N1 genotype B3.13 viruses present high pathogenicity in rodent models, though the overall respiratory transmissibility remains low in the hamster model. IMPORTANCE Influenza A H5N1 virus spilled over from wild birds into dairy cattle in the United States in 2024. Since then, an increased number of human infections—with at least 71 confirmed cases—have been confirmed. In the present study, we evaluated and compared the pathogenicity and transmissibility of a bovine and two human H5N1 viruses of the genotype B3.13. Our results show that while all viruses are pathogenic in mouse and hamster models, the bovine isolate TX2/24 presents a broader tissue tropism than the human-derived viruses. Contact transmission studies revealed a limited ability of these viruses to transmit in the hamster contact transmission model. These findings highlight the high pathogenicity of H5N1 viruses in mammals and demonstrate that their respiratory transmissibility potential remains low in the hamster model.

papers.title_zh: 小鼠和仓鼠模型中牛和人甲型流感 H5N1 病毒的感染和 传播 动态
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Here we investigated the pathogenesis and contact transmission of bovine- and human-derived highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b genotype B3.13 viruses in mammalian models. Using reverse genetics, we rescued three naturally occurring viruses, rTX2/24 (bovine-derived), rTexas/37, and rMichigan/90 (both human-derived), and compared their infection dynamics, replication, and pathogenicity with the wild-type bovine TX2/24 strain in vitro and in vivo . All four viruses demonstrated comparable replication kinetics in four mammalian cell lines. However, the rMichigan/90 strain exhibited smaller plaques in bovine and human cells. In vivo studies showed that mice infected with any of the viruses succumbed to infection within 4–5 days; however, mice infected with the rMichigan/90 virus exhibited slightly lower viral replication and shedding compared with the other strains. The hamster model showed a milder infection phenotype than mice in which all viruses induced body weight loss and oral shedding, with robust virus replication observed in tissues, but the rMichigan/90 virus presented reduced replication and shedding. Contact transmission studies in hamsters revealed limited transmissibility for these viruses, with only one out of four animals inoculated with the rMichigan/90 virus transmitting it to a naïve contact. These findings indicate that both bovine- and human-derived H5N1 genotype B3.13 viruses present high pathogenicity in rodent models, though the overall respiratory transmissibility remains low in the hamster model. IMPORTANCE Influenza A H5N1 virus spilled over from wild birds into dairy cattle in the United States in 2024. Since then, an increased number of human infections—with at least 71 confirmed cases—have been confirmed. In the present study, we evaluated and compared the pathogenicity and transmissibility of a bovine and two human H5N1 viruses of the genotype B3.13. Our results show that while all viruses are pathogenic in mouse and hamster models, the bovine isolate TX2/24 presents a broader tissue tropism than the human-derived viruses. Contact transmission studies revealed a limited ability of these viruses to transmit in the hamster contact transmission model. These findings highlight the high pathogenicity of H5N1 viruses in mammals and demonstrate that their respiratory transmissibility potential remains low in the hamster model.

papers.title: Biosecurity Practices and Production Characteristics Associated with High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza in Québec Duck Farms: A 2022–2023 Case-Control Study
papers.abstract: The high-pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) epidemic that began in 2021 in Canada continues to affect poultry populations, resulting in the loss of millions of birds through 2026. To investigate farm-level risk factors associated with HPAI infection, a case–control study was conducted on 28 commercial duck farms in Québec, Canada. Farms completed an adapted Biocheck.Ugent questionnaire on biosecurity practices and production characteristics. Associations with HPAI status (case or control) were assessed using Fisher’s exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and multivariate patterns were explored using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) followed by hierarchical clustering on principal components (HCPC). Case farms had higher annual duck production and were more often part of an integrated production network than control farms. They also reported less frequent wildlife and structural inspections and more often purchased or produced ducks for force-feeding. MCA showed clear separation between case and control farms, driven by differences in biosecurity practices (e.g., hygiene practices, downtime) and farm characteristics (e.g., flock size, indoor housing type). HCPC identified three farm clusters, including one composed exclusively of case farms, characterized by force-feeding production and weaker between-barn hygiene. analysis.methods: Associations with HPAI status were assessed using Fisher’s exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and multivariate patterns were explored using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) followed by hierarchical clustering on principal components (HCPC).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated farm-level risk factors associated with high-pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) in Québec duck farms during 2022–2023. A case–control design was used, comparing 28 commercial duck farms with HPAI infection to those without. Farms completed a Biocheck.Ugent questionnaire on biosecurity practices and production characteristics. The analysis used Fisher’s exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, along with multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) and hierarchical clustering on principal components (HCPC) to identify patterns. Results showed that case farms had higher production, were more likely to be part of an integrated network, and reported less frequent inspections and more force-feeding practices. MCA revealed clear separation between case and control farms based on biosecurity and production differences. The study suggests that production structure and biosecurity profiles should be considered in identifying high-risk farms and developing prevention strategies. The findings are based on self-reported data and are of moderate evidence strength due to the abstract-only nature and potential for bias.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在确定与魁北克鸭场高致病性 禽流感 (HPAI) 感染相关的农场层面的风险因素,因为自 2021 年以来加拿大的 HPAI 流行已造成家禽数量大幅减少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022 年至 2023 年期间,对加拿大魁北克省的 28 个商业养鸭场进行了一项病例对照研究,以调查与 HPAI 感染相关的风险因素。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Fisher 精确检验和 Wilcoxon 秩和检验评估与 HPAI 状态的关联,并使用多重对应分析 (MCA) 和主成分分层聚类 (HCPC) 探索多变量模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 与对照农场相比,案例农场的鸭子年产量更高,并且更多地成为综合生产网络的一部分。他们还报告说,对野生动物和结构的检查频率较低,并且更频繁地购买或生产鸭子进行强制喂食。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在识别高致病性禽流感感染风险较高的农场并制定有针对性的预防和控制策略时,应考虑生产结构和生物安全状况。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为监测和鸭场HPAI风险评估策略提供参考,帮助设计更有效的生物安全措施和有针对性的干预措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象证据,研究结果基于农场的自我报告数据,这可能会引入偏差。证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 2021 年在加拿大开始的高致病性 禽流感 (HPAI) 流行病继续影响家禽种群,导致到 2026 年损失数百万只家禽。为了调查与 HPAI 感染相关的农场层面的风险因素,对加拿大魁北克省的 28 个商业养鸭场进行了病例对照研究。农场完成了一份关于生物安全实践和生产特征的改编 Biocheck.Ugent 调查问卷。使用 Fisher 精确检验和 Wilcoxon 秩和检验评估与 HPAI 状态(病例或对照)的关联,并使用多重对应分析 (MCA) 和主成分分层聚类 (HCPC) 探索多变量模式。与对照农场相比,案例农场的鸭子年产量更高,并且更多地成为综合生产网络的一部分。他们还报告说,对野生动物和结构的检查频率较低,并且更频繁地购买或生产鸭子进行强制喂食。MCA 显示病例农场和对照农场之间有明显的区别,这是由于生物安全实践(例如卫生习惯、停工时间)和农场特征(例如鸡群规模、室内鸡舍类型)的差异所致。HCPC 确定了三个农场集群,其中一个完全由案例农场组成,其特点是强制饲喂生产和畜舍间卫生状况较差。这些发现表明,在识别高致病性禽流感感染风险较高的农场并制定有针对性的预防和控制策略时,应考虑生产结构和生物安全状况。

papers.title: Avian influenza A virus polymerase gene leads to temperature-resistant genome replication
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza A viruses (IAV) pose a persistent pandemic threat. Successful cross-species transmission from waterfowl to mammals requires host adaptation for efficient replication and spread. Avian IAVs are adapted to the temperature of the avian gut, approximately 41°C, while human IAVs replicate at 33°C in the upper respiratory tract. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of avian-origin PB1 genes in enabling influenza A viruses (IAVs) to replicate at febrile temperatures, which is critical for cross-species transmission. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 流感A病毒(IAV)对人类健康构成持续的流行威胁。从水禽到哺乳动物的成功跨物种传播需要IAV进行适应性改变以实现高效的复制和传播。禽类IAV适应于禽类肠道的温度,约为41°C,而人类IAV则在上呼吸道的33°C温度下复制。PB1是病毒异三聚体RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RdRp)的催化核心,对于病毒RNA合成至关重要。三种大流行IAV株(1918年、1957年和1968年)携带了源自禽类的PB1基因,这表明其具有选择优势。发热是一种关键的免疫反应,会将体温升高至38°C或更高,并可能限制病毒复制。我们假设禽类PB1可能允许IAV在发热温度下复制。利用一种微型复制子系统,我们证明了季节性人类H1N1 IAV的聚合酶在40°C下无法高效复制病毒RNA,而将PB1替换为源自1918年、1957年和1968年大流行病毒或低致病性禽类H2N1病毒的PB1基因后,RNA合成得以恢复。在MDCK细胞中,表达禽类或1918年PB1的季节性人类H1N1病毒株可以在40°C下复制,而野生型H1N1病毒则不能。使用纯化的嵌合IAV聚合酶进行活性测定进一步表明,源自禽类的PB1可能在高温下内在性地增强聚合酶活性。这些数据表明,源自禽类的PB1基因使IAV能够在发热温度下复制,突显了其在人兽共患病出现和适应性改变中的作用。在哺乳动物中流行的IAV中,源自禽类的PB1基因的特征可能有助于识别具有大流行潜力的病毒株,并为开发应对措施提供信息。重要性 源自禽类的流感A病毒仍然是人类健康的一个持续威胁。1918年、1957年和1968年的大流行流感病毒都获得了源自禽类的PB1基因,但这些基因所带来的适应性优势仍不完全清楚。在这里,我们展示了源自禽类的PB1基因如何增强季节性人类流感病毒聚合酶在高温下的病毒RNA复制能力,并使人类流感病毒能够在40°C下复制,这一温度与禽类和人类发热疾病均相关。在基于细胞的聚合酶实验中,以及在纯化的聚合酶和真实病毒感染过程中均观察到了PB1依赖性效应。这些发现将温度耐受性复制识别为源自禽类PB1的潜在适应性特征,并表明获得禽类PB1可能有助于流感病毒在适应哺乳动物宿主时克服温度障碍。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感A病毒(IAV)对人类健康构成持续的流行威胁。从水禽到哺乳动物的成功跨物种传播需要IAV进行适应性改变以实现高效的复制和传播。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究调查了源自鸟类的 PB1 基因在哺乳动物 宿主 的 IAV 中的复制情况。三种大流行IAV毒株(1918年、1957年和1968年)携带禽源PB1基因,表明具有选择优势。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用微型复制子系统证明,季节性人类 H1N1 IAV 的聚合酶在 40°C 下无法有效复制病毒 RNA,而用 1918 年、1957 年和 1968 年大流行病毒或低致病性禽 H2N1 病毒的 PB1 替换,可以恢复 RNA 合成。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在MDCK细胞中,表达禽类或1918年PB1的季节性人类H1N1病毒株可以在40°C下复制,而野生型H1N1病毒则不能。纯化嵌合IAV聚合酶的活性测定进一步表明,源自禽类的PB1可能在高温下内在性地增强聚合酶活性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现将耐温 基因组 复制确定为禽源 PB1 的潜在适应特性,并表明获得禽类 PB1 可能有助于流感病毒克服在适应哺乳动物 宿主 过程中遇到的温度障碍。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在哺乳动物中流行的IAV中,源自禽类的PB1基因的特征可能有助于识别具有大流行潜力的病毒株,并为开发应对措施提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计或方法的具体限制。

papers.title: Why One Health Pays Off: Economic Evidence from Cameroon’s 2016 H5N1 Outbreak
papers.abstract: Abstract Cameroon experienced a major H5N1 epizootic in 2016, affecting poultry farms, markets, and production sites across several regions. Because the country had not previously undertaken an economic evaluation of its outbreak response, a cost analysis was conducted to document the financial and operational requirements of outbreak response and provide evidence to support preparedness planning and future economic evaluations. The study aimed to document the financial and operational costs associated with the outbreak response and identify key data and reporting gaps that may inform future economic evaluations and preparedness planning. The cost analysis used available data from laboratory testing, decontamination activities, destruction of infected poultry and materials, and field operations undertaken during the outbreak response. Information was provided by national laboratories, veterinary authorities, public health actors, and official reports. However, incomplete documentation and non-disaggregated financial records required several assumptions during cost reconstruction. The analysis documented the costs of implementing response measures, including laboratory testing, decontamination, destruction of infected poultry and materials, and field operations undertaken during the outbreak response. Findings indicate that the response involved substantial operational and financial costs, but the accuracy of results was constrained by limited data availability, lack of detailed financial reporting, and gaps in operational information. The assessment also highlighted important operational elements, including multi-laboratory sample handling and the extensive effort required for site decontamination. It also draws attention to broader poultry-sector effects considered in the source analysis, including production continuity and estimated value linked to meat, eggs, and manure. The study provides insight into the operational and financial requirements of multisectoral outbreak response, while highlighting important considerations for strengthening preparedness, documentation, and future economic assessment of One Health responses. Information © The Authors 2026

The cost analysis relied on data from laboratory testing, decontamination activities, destruction of infected poultry and materials, and field operations. papers.title_zh: 为什么一种健康会带来回报:来自喀麦隆 2016 年 H5N1 暴发 的经济证据
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Cameroon experienced a major H5N1 epizootic in 2016, affecting poultry farms, markets, and production sites across several regions. Because the country had not previously undertaken an economic evaluation of its outbreak response, a cost analysis was conducted to document the financial and operational requirements of outbreak response and provide evidence to support preparedness planning and future economic evaluations. The study aimed to document the financial and operational costs associated with the outbreak response and identify key data and reporting gaps that may inform future economic evaluations and preparedness planning. The cost analysis used available data from laboratory testing, decontamination activities, destruction of infected poultry and materials, and field operations undertaken during the outbreak response. Information was provided by national laboratories, veterinary authorities, public health actors, and official reports. However, incomplete documentation and non-disaggregated financial records required several assumptions during cost reconstruction. The analysis documented the costs of implementing response measures, including laboratory testing, decontamination, destruction of infected poultry and materials, and field operations undertaken during the outbreak response. Findings indicate that the response involved substantial operational and financial costs, but the accuracy of results was constrained by limited data availability, lack of detailed financial reporting, and gaps in operational information. The assessment also highlighted important operational elements, including multi-laboratory sample handling and the extensive effort required for site decontamination. It also draws attention to broader poultry-sector effects considered in the source analysis, including production continuity and estimated value linked to meat, eggs, and manure. The study provides insight into the operational and financial requirements of multisectoral outbreak response, while highlighting important considerations for strengthening preparedness, documentation, and future economic assessment of One Health responses. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 喀麦隆在 2016 年经历了一次 H5N1 禽流感大流行,影响了多个地区的家禽养殖场、市场和生产场所。由于该国此前未对其 暴发 应对措施进行经济评估,因此进行了成本分析,以记录 暴发 应对措施的财务和运营要求,并为支持准备计划和未来经济评估提供证据。该研究旨在记录与 暴发 响应相关的财务和运营成本,并确定可能为未来经济评估和准备规划提供信息的关键数据和报告差距。成本分析使用了实验室测试、净化活动、受感染家禽和材料的销毁以及 暴发 响应期间进行的现场操作的可用数据。信息由国家实验室、兽医当局、公共卫生参与者和官方报告提供。然而,不完整的文件记录和未分类的财务记录需要在成本重建期间做出一些假设。该分析记录了实施应对措施的成本,包括实验室检测、净化、销毁受感染的家禽和材料,以及 暴发 应对期间进行的现场操作。调查结果表明,应对措施涉及大量运营和财务成本,但结果的准确性受到可用数据有限、缺乏详细财务报告以及运营信息差距的限制。评估还强调了重要的操作要素,包括多实验室样本处理和现场净化所需的大量工作。它还提请人们注意来源分析中考虑的更广泛的家禽业影响,包括生产连续性和与肉、蛋和粪便相关的估计价值。该研究深入了解了多部门 暴发 应对措施的运营和财务要求,同时强调了加强“同一个健康”应对措施的准备、记录和未来经济评估的重要考虑因素。信息 © 作者 2026

papers.title: Linear DNA vaccine: a new approach to overcome the limitations of classical DNA vaccines, using avian influenza A/H5 prevention as an example
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses of the A/H5 subtype pose a serious threat to public health due to their high mortality rate (over 50 % among reported cases) and the potential risk of acquiring the ability to transmit between humans. Developing effective vaccine platforms, including DNA vaccines, is a priority task. The DoggyboneTM linear DNA vaccine technology overcomes the limitations of classical plasmid DNA vaccines (the presence of bacterial elements and antibiotic resistance genes) while retaining their advantages, such as high production speed that does not require using cell cultures or chicken embryos, temperature stability, and cost‐effectiveness. Developing a linear DNA vaccine encoding the haemagglutinin of the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus of the A/H5 subtype and evaluation its immunogenicity and protective efficacy in BALB/c mice. Materials and methods. The linear DNA vaccine db‐H5 was produced using the DoggyboneTM technology with φ29 DNA polymerase and TelN protelomerase. The functionality of db‐H5 in vitro was assessed by Western blot analysis. For the in vivo study, BALB/c mice were immunized with 1 μg of the DNA vaccine via jet injection. Immunogenicity was evaluated using ELISA, virus neutralization, and IFN‐γ ELISpot assays. Protective efficacy was tested by challenging the animals with the A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) virus. The resulting linear DNA ensured the expression of the target gene in transfected HEK293 cells. Mice immunized with the db‐H5 DNA vaccine showed high titres of haemagglutinin‐specific antibodies (1:72 900), neutralizing antibodies (median titre 1:40), and increased numbers of IFN‐γ‐producing splenocytes (48 SFUs/106). The survival rate of immunized mice after lethal challenge with 20MLD50 was 70 %, whereas all animals in the control group died. For the first time in Russian practice, we have demonstrated the feasibility of developing a linear DNA vaccine against diseases caused by highly pathogenic avian influenza A/H5 viruses using the DoggyboneTM technology. Two‐dose immunization of mice with an low dose (1 μg) provides protection against lethal infection, which justifies further development of this platform.

The DoggyboneTM linear DNA vaccine technology overcomes the limitations of classical plasmid DNA vaccines (the presence of bacterial elements and antibiotic resistance genes) while retaining their advantages, such as high production speed that does not require using cell cultures or chicken embryos, temperature stability, and cost‐effectiveness. Developing a linear DNA vaccine encoding the haemagglutinin of the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus of the A/H5 subtype and evaluation its immunogenicity and protective efficacy in BALB/c mice. Materials and methods. The linear DNA vaccine db‐H5 was produced using the DoggyboneTM technology with φ29 DNA polymerase and TelN protelomerase. The functionality of db‐H5 in vitro was assessed by Western blot analysis. For the in vivo study, BALB/c mice were immunized with 1 μg of the DNA vaccine via jet injection. Immunogenicity was evaluated using ELISA, virus neutralization, and IFN‐γ ELISpot assays. Protective efficacy was tested by challenging the animals with the A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) virus. The resulting linear DNA ensured the expression of the target gene in transfected HEK293 cells. Mice immunized with the db‐H5 DNA vaccine showed high titres of haemagglutinin‐specific antibodies (1:72 900), neutralizing antibodies (median titre 1:40), and increased numbers of IFN‐γ‐producing splenocytes (48 SFUs/106). The survival rate of immunized mice after lethal challenge with 20MLD50 was 70 %, whereas all animals in the control group died. For the first time in Russian practice, we have demonstrated the feasibility of developing a linear DNA vaccine against diseases caused by highly pathogenic avian influenza A/H5 viruses using the DoggyboneTM technology. Two‐dose immunization of mice with an low dose (1 μg) provides protection against lethal infection, which justifies further development of this platform.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a linear DNA vaccine against highly pathogenic avian influenza A/H5 viruses, addressing the limitations of classical DNA vaccines. The linear DNA vaccine db‐H5 was produced using the DoggyboneTM technology and tested in BALB/c mice. The vaccine induced high haemagglutinin-specific antibody titres, neutralizing antibodies, and increased IFN-γ-producing splenocytes. After a lethal challenge with A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8), 70% of immunized mice survived, while all control mice died. These results demonstrate the vaccine's effectiveness in an animal model and highlight its potential for future development. The study's findings are significant for vaccine development against avian influenza A/H5 viruses but are limited to in vivo testing in mice.

papers.full_text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1 bird flu) is the defining disease of our times, suggests Australian writer and journalist Michael Dulaney in his timely book Sentinels, on what happens when diseases spread between animals and humans. Now impacting mainland Australian wildlife, the disease, which reached us in June, epitomises our callous neglect of nature, despite us being embedded in and reliant on it. “Of all the pathogens I’ve learned about, this is the big one,” Dulaney writes. Review: Sentinels by Michael Dulaney (Scribe Publications) Over 700 bird flu events – which cover individual or multiple deaths of animals – have occurred in Australia so far. Greater crested terns, little penguins, common bottlenose dolphin, long-nosed fur seals, Australian sea lions, and many other bird and mammal species have all succumbed. It’s a sobering result of our missed chances to protect nature and prevent pathogens from jumping between non-human animals and people. In his book, which was longlisted for this year’s Walkley Book Award and published just a few months after bird flu reached Australia, Dulaney thoughtfully discusses our impacts on and connections with non-human life. We continue to exploit species and plunder nature at an alarming scale and rate. It’s estimated humans exploit as much as 300 times more species than non-human predators. The concept of a sentinel — the canary in the coal mine — draws from epidemiology, the study of disease. Dulaney’s thesis is that these sentinels are increasingly sickly, often dropping dead at disturbingly regular rates and in extraordinary numbers. It’s hard to dispute this. A recent grisly example is the estimated death of more than 13,000 elephant seal pups, more than 75% of all pups born, on the sub-Antarctic Heard Island last summer, as their remote, isolated location and shielding from H5N1 bird flu were inevitably breached. Humans are destroying nature and the spillover of diseases that jump between species – including to and from humans – is increasing. Dulaney writes: Researchers have counted around 200 new infectious diseases that have broken out more than 12,000 times over the past three decades On average, one new infectious disease jumps to humans every eight months. He suggests this threat should be considered in the same way as other globally significant and existential threats, including climate change. As a wildlife ecologist and conservation scientist, I echo his call to action. A joy to read Sentinels is composed of three parts and eight chapters. The first part is focused on wildlife, the second on agriculture and the third looks at the impacts of commerce, the wildlife trade and our treatment of fellow human beings. One chilling passage describes how in California’s bulging prison population, one of five of the state’s cases of Valley fever (a disease caused by pathogenic fungi) was found among its prisoners between 2007 and 2011. Dulaney’s writing is a joy. Easily consumed, complex ideas and information are made accessible to the reader. Sentinels is very well referenced too, including extensive peer-reviewed research. Case studies span China, the Andes, the Arctic, Indonesia, Australia and elsewhere. As a result, this book is undoubtedly globally relevant. Dulaney also takes his readers to the front lines. There are stories of ecologists studying flying foxes in forests, and about the relevance of Hendra virus, which causes severe, often fatal disease in both infected horses and humans. It can pass from bats to horses, and has killed people working with horses. Elsewhere, the book details people trying to protect endangered amphibians on Indonesian mountains, as Dulaney spends four days with Angga, a gifted wildlife tracker. “Sometimes, when Angga uncovers an exceptionally rare frog or snake species, his clients break down crying over finding something they have searched for their whole lives,” he writes. There’s even discussion of the potential links between pigs, East Germany and the fall of communism. The epilogue is perhaps the most powerful and vital section of the book. It brings together how what’s happening is not a case of misfortune, but a predictable, likely outcome of what we’re doing: the habitats we destroy, and the crowding of people and animals. The science is clear. Our actions are stressing wildlife populations and in some cases, they bring wildlife and their diseases closer to us and the animals we farm and eat. It’s a recipe for disaster. The increasing reliance of flying foxes on urban environments to find food – and the Hendra virus risk this poses – is because we’ve destroyed large areas of forests and woodlands these animals relied upon. Dulaney comes hard at capitalism, too, pointing to its commodification of nature. This will likely rankle some – but again, it’s hard to argue against. Even within the conservation community I’m part of, the value of species and ecosystems are often framed and described through the services they provide us, rather than their intrinsic value. The Australian government now has a Nature repair market, which includes the use of controversial offsets that allow for further environmental destruction. Dulaney is clear about his ecological grief. “In the days prior to handling ducks, I’d watched distressing video compilations filmed by carers around the world who could do nothing but witness these slow deaths,” he writes about bird flu. In the chapter devoted to it, he writes: I have come to believe that bird flu is the archetypal disease of this new age, the one that represents all of our failed efforts to address the growing threat of spillover – a disease that links farming, unrestrained industry, political intransigience, and environmental exploitation in a way that threatens hundreds of species, including our own. It scares me more than anything else. His honesty and authenticity mean Sentinels rises above many science-based books I’ve read, which clumsily attempt to hide the authors’ personal views and values. We are not impartial automatons: we all have skin in this game, which concerns our only home. Dulaney makes the case for urgent and substantial change. Hope, but no sugarcoating Much of the book is confronting; Dulaney does not sugarcoat our predicament. But he offers hope – and makes the important point that tackling disease will also help address other crises, such as climate change, which are inextricably linked. Sentinels covers a lot of ground. Given the complexities of disease ecology and the wicked problem of managing wildlife and societies to reduce our exposure to pandemics and better protect biodiversity, it’s unsurprising some issues aren’t covered in the depth I might desire. But in my view, this is more than compensated for by the broad knowledge and understanding readers will get from Dulaney’s book. Sentinels is a vital read. I hope it reaches a diverse audience, including our political leaders, who need to confront the challenges it so thoughtfully describes. To protect ourselves, we must protect our ecosystems and the species that sustain them.
