full_text_sections.full_text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1 bird flu) is the defining disease of our times, suggests Australian writer and journalist Michael Dulaney in his timely book Sentinels, on what happens when diseases spread between animals and humans. Now impacting mainland Australian wildlife, the disease, which reached us in June, epitomises our callous neglect of nature, despite us being embedded in and reliant on it. “Of all the pathogens I’ve learned about, this is the big one,” Dulaney writes. Review: Sentinels by Michael Dulaney (Scribe Publications) Over 700 bird flu events – which cover individual or multiple deaths of animals – have occurred in Australia so far. Greater crested terns, little penguins, common bottlenose dolphin, long-nosed fur seals, Australian sea lions, and many other bird and mammal species have all succumbed. It’s a sobering result of our missed chances to protect nature and prevent pathogens from jumping between non-human animals and people. In his book, which was longlisted for this year’s Walkley Book Award and published just a few months after bird flu reached Australia, Dulaney thoughtfully discusses our impacts on and connections with non-human life. We continue to exploit species and plunder nature at an alarming scale and rate. It’s estimated humans exploit as much as 300 times more species than non-human predators. The concept of a sentinel — the canary in the coal mine — draws from epidemiology, the study of disease. Dulaney’s thesis is that these sentinels are increasingly sickly, often dropping dead at disturbingly regular rates and in extraordinary numbers. It’s hard to dispute this. A recent grisly example is the estimated death of more than 13,000 elephant seal pups, more than 75% of all pups born, on the sub-Antarctic Heard Island last summer, as their remote, isolated location and shielding from H5N1 bird flu were inevitably breached. Humans are destroying nature and the spillover of diseases that jump between species – including to and from humans – is increasing. Dulaney writes: Researchers have counted around 200 new infectious diseases that have broken out more than 12,000 times over the past three decades On average, one new infectious disease jumps to humans every eight months. He suggests this threat should be considered in the same way as other globally significant and existential threats, including climate change. As a wildlife ecologist and conservation scientist, I echo his call to action. A joy to read Sentinels is composed of three parts and eight chapters. The first part is focused on wildlife, the second on agriculture and the third looks at the impacts of commerce, the wildlife trade and our treatment of fellow human beings. One chilling passage describes how in California’s bulging prison population, one of five of the state’s cases of Valley fever (a disease caused by pathogenic fungi) was found among its prisoners between 2007 and 2011. Dulaney’s writing is a joy. Easily consumed, complex ideas and information are made accessible to the reader. Sentinels is very well referenced too, including extensive peer-reviewed research. Case studies span China, the Andes, the Arctic, Indonesia, Australia and elsewhere. As a result, this book is undoubtedly globally relevant. Dulaney also takes his readers to the front lines. There are stories of ecologists studying flying foxes in forests, and about the relevance of Hendra virus, which causes severe, often fatal disease in both infected horses and humans. It can pass from bats to horses, and has killed people working with horses. Elsewhere, the book details people trying to protect endangered amphibians on Indonesian mountains, as Dulaney spends four days with Angga, a gifted wildlife tracker. “Sometimes, when Angga uncovers an exceptionally rare frog or snake species, his clients break down crying over finding something they have searched for their whole lives,” he writes. There’s even discussion of the potential links between pigs, East Germany and the fall of communism. The epilogue is perhaps the most powerful and vital section of the book. It brings together how what’s happening is not a case of misfortune, but a predictable, likely outcome of what we’re doing: the habitats we destroy, and the crowding of people and animals. The science is clear. Our actions are stressing wildlife populations and in some cases, they bring wildlife and their diseases closer to us and the animals we farm and eat. It’s a recipe for disaster. The increasing reliance of flying foxes on urban environments to find food – and the Hendra virus risk this poses – is because we’ve destroyed large areas of forests and woodlands these animals relied upon. Dulaney comes hard at capitalism, too, pointing to its commodification of nature. This will likely rankle some – but again, it’s hard to argue against. Even within the conservation community I’m part of, the value of species and ecosystems are often framed and described through the services they provide us, rather than their intrinsic value. The Australian government now has a Nature repair market, which includes the use of controversial offsets that allow for further environmental destruction. Dulaney is clear about his ecological grief. “In the days prior to handling ducks, I’d watched distressing video compilations filmed by carers around the world who could do nothing but witness these slow deaths,” he writes about bird flu. In the chapter devoted to it, he writes: I have come to believe that bird flu is the archetypal disease of this new age, the one that represents all of our failed efforts to address the growing threat of spillover – a disease that links farming, unrestrained industry, political intransigience, and environmental exploitation in a way that threatens hundreds of species, including our own. It scares me more than anything else. His honesty and authenticity mean Sentinels rises above many science-based books I’ve read, which clumsily attempt to hide the authors’ personal views and values. We are not impartial automatons: we all have skin in this game, which concerns our only home. Dulaney makes the case for urgent and substantial change. Hope, but no sugarcoating Much of the book is confronting; Dulaney does not sugarcoat our predicament. But he offers hope – and makes the important point that tackling disease will also help address other crises, such as climate change, which are inextricably linked. Sentinels covers a lot of ground. Given the complexities of disease ecology and the wicked problem of managing wildlife and societies to reduce our exposure to pandemics and better protect biodiversity, it’s unsurprising some issues aren’t covered in the depth I might desire. But in my view, this is more than compensated for by the broad knowledge and understanding readers will get from Dulaney’s book. Sentinels is a vital read. I hope it reaches a diverse audience, including our political leaders, who need to confront the challenges it so thoughtfully describes. To protect ourselves, we must protect our ecosystems and the species that sustain them. The ongoing demise of wildlife and the global rise of diseases and pandemics sound clarion calls we must urgently act upon. We must improve our relationship with nature.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the growing threat of avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1 bird flu, as a defining disease of our times, emphasizing the need to address the increasing spillover of pathogens between animals and humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of the book 'Sentinels' by Michael Dulaney, which examines the spread of avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1, across various ecosystems and species in Australia and globally, focusing on wildlife, agriculture, and human health impacts.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a narrative review of the book, analyzing case studies and examples of avian influenza A virus outbreaks, including H5N1, in different regions and species, and discussing the ecological and societal factors contributing to disease spillover.
analysis.main_results: The book reports over 700 bird flu events in Australia, with more than 13,000 elephant seal pups estimated to have died on Heard Island, and highlights the increasing frequency of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, with around 200 new infectious diseases jumping to humans over the past three decades.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dulaney interprets these findings as a predictable outcome of human activities that destroy habitats and bring wildlife and domestic animals closer to humans, suggesting that avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1, represent a broader crisis of spillover diseases and environmental exploitation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for better surveillance and protection of ecosystems to reduce the risk of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, emphasizing the interconnectedness of environmental health and public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a book review and does not include original data or statistical analysis, which limits its evidence strength. However, it provides a comprehensive overview of the ecological and societal context of avian influenza A virus spread.

analysis.summary_en: This analysis focuses on the growing threat of avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1 bird flu, as highlighted in Michael Dulaney's book 'Sentinels'. The study discusses the increasing frequency of zoonotic influenza outbreaks, with over 700 bird flu events reported in Australia and more than 13,000 elephant seal pups dying on Heard Island. Dulaney argues that these events are a predictable outcome of human activities that destroy habitats and increase contact between wildlife and humans. The findings underscore the importance of protecting ecosystems to mitigate the risk of disease spillover. However, the study is based on a book review and lacks original data, which limits its evidence strength. The book serves as a call to action for addressing the interconnected crises of environmental destruction and public health threats.

papers.title: Influenza Aviária A(H5N1) em Mamíferos e Humanos: Risco Pandêmico e Preparação dos Sistemas de Saúde
papers.abstract: A influenza aviária altamente patogênica A(H5N1) espalhou-se pelo mundo a partir de 2020 e provocou grande mortalidade de aves silvestres e domésticas, com registro de infecção em diversas espécies de mamíferos, incluindo mamíferos marinhos na América do Sul e, a partir de 2024, bovinos leiteiros nos Estados Unidos. Desde então, mais de 70 casos humanos foram confirmados naquele país, quase todos em trabalhadores expostos a animais infectados, em geral com quadro leve e conjuntivite. Não há evidência de transmissão sustentada entre pessoas, e as avaliações conjuntas da Organização Mundial da Saúde, da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura e da Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal consideram baixo o risco para a população geral e de baixo a moderado para pessoas com exposição ocupacional. No Brasil, o primeiro foco em granja comercial foi confirmado em 2025, com resposta rápida de contenção. A preparação dos sistemas de saúde envolve vigilância integrada humana, animal e ambiental, proteção dos trabalhadores expostos, diagnóstico e tratamento antiviral precoce dos casos suspeitos, planos de produção de vacinas e comunicação de risco. Este capítulo revisa a epidemiologia recente, as manifestações clínicas em humanos e as estratégias de vigilância e preparação, com atenção ao contexto brasileiro e à abordagem de Saúde Única.

analysis.summary_en: This chapter examines the global spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1), highlighting its impact on birds and mammals, including human cases. It emphasizes the low risk to the general population but moderate risk for those with occupational exposure. The study outlines the importance of integrated surveillance across human, animal, and environmental health, along with measures such as early antiviral treatment and vaccine production plans. The findings suggest that while the risk of sustained human-to-human transmission remains low, the need for preparedness and risk communication is critical. The evidence is based on reported outbreaks and official assessments, which provide a moderate level of confidence in the conclusions.

papers.abstract_zh: 甲型H5N1流感禽流感将成为2020年世界性的一个重大事件,对家禽和家禽造成巨大的死亡威胁,并登记了多种感染者的感染情况,包括感染者和海员南美洲,2024 年的一部分,是联合国国家的目标。据介绍,有 70 多个人的孔洞被确认为国家的孔洞,这些孔洞都是感染动物的,一般都是四级和结膜。没有证据表明可持续发展的重要性,并与世界组织、国家统一组织、食品和农业组织、世界动物组织、动物保护组织等相结合。总体而言,在职业展示方面,一切都是一个中庸之道。巴西将在 2025 年开始大规模商业化,并会快速回复内容。整个系统的准备工作包括人类综合警戒、动物和环境、工作人员的保护、诊断和抗病毒药物预防怀疑、疫苗生产计划和风险交流。本文修订了最近的流行病学,作为人类临床的宣言和警戒和准备策略,以巴西的情况和萨乌德乌尼卡的情况为背景。

papers.title: No Detection of Avian Influenza Virus Type A in Broods of Nestling Saker Falcons Falco cherrug at Artificial Nests in Mongolia
papers.abstract: Los recientes brotes del altamente patógeno virus de la influenza aviar han tenido efectos devastadores sobre las aves silvestres y de corral, habiendo facilitado las aves migratorias su propagación a escala mundial. En Mongolia, la migración primaveral de aves desde el sudeste asiático hacia las zonas de reproducción más septentrionales de regiones templadas y árticas probablemente constituye una vía importante de dispersión. En este país, la vigilancia de las infecciones provocadas por el virus de la influenza aviar (VIA) se ha centrado principalmente en las aves acuáticas. Aquí evaluamos las tasas de infección por el VIA de tipo A en nidadas de Falco cherrug, una especie que se captura y exporta anualmente en el marco del comercio regulado por la CITES, lo que supone una posible vía de transmisión de enfermedades, en particular hacia los países del Golfo. En nidos artificiales instalados en el centro y este de Mongolia, muestreamos 200 nidadas de Falco cherrug mediante hisopados orofaríngeos y muestras de pulpa de plumas. No detectamos ningún caso de infección por el VIA de tipo A mediante pruebas de reacción en cadena de la polimerasa con transcriptasa invsera, lo que indica que la tasa de infección es inferior al límite de detección del 6% de nuestro estudio. [Traducción del equipo editorial]

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the infection rates of avian influenza A viruses in nestling saker falcons Falco cherrug at artificial nests in Mongolia, given the potential for these birds to act as vectors for disease transmission, particularly to countries in the Gulf region. Recent outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza have had devastating effects on wild and domestic birds, facilitating the global spread of the virus through migratory birds.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Mongolia, focusing on 200 nestling saker falcons Falco cherrug at artificial nests in central and eastern Mongolia. Samples were collected through oropharyngeal swabs and feather pulp samples.
analysis.methods: Samples were tested for avian influenza A viruses using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
analysis.main_results: No avian influenza A virus was detected in any of the 200 nestling saker falcons sampled, indicating an infection rate below the 6% detection limit of the study.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that the saker falcons sampled did not serve as a significant vector for avian influenza A virus transmission, contributing to the understanding of the role of migratory birds in disease spread.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that saker falcons may not be a significant vector for avian influenza A virus transmission, which could inform surveillance and conservation efforts for these birds and their habitats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the small sample size and the use of artificial nests, which may not fully represent the natural nesting behavior of saker falcons. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the infection rates of avian influenza A viruses in nestling saker falcons at artificial nests in Mongolia. No virus was detected, indicating that these birds may not be significant vectors for disease transmission.

papers.title: A chicken interferon-stimulated gene screen reveals limited genes restricting influenza virus replication
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat. Not only does it cause significant economic losses to the agricultural industry, but it also presents a risk of spillover into the human population. However, several obstacles must be overcome for a successful cross-species transmission event to occur. One of these obstacles is the innate immunity of the host. While the innate immune response to IAV in humans has been well-studied, the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not as well understood. Here, we explore the interferon-induced immune response by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, and find that they are largely species-specific. Using this data, we performed a CRISPR knockout ISG screen against two strains of IAV, the mouse-adapted PR8, and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10. We find that for PR8, IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits with modest effects, consistent with previous work in mammals. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit; however, there were two additional hits absent for PR8, the HSP70 co-chaperone protein BAG5 and the deubiquitinase OTUD4. Overall, these findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system that can be used to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species. IMPORTANCE Wild birds, especially waterfowl and shorebirds, are the primary natural reservoir for influenza A viruses. These birds can transmit IAV to domestic poultry, where the spillover risk to humans increases. Chickens are the most common species of domestic poultry worldwide and frequently infected with avian influenza viruses. Despite this, relatively little is known about how their immune system responds to influenza infection. This lack of knowledge creates a barrier to finding ways of preventing or mitigating IAV infection in chicken flocks. In this study, we characterized the interferon-induced immune response to IAV in chickens and found that only a small subset of ISGs were responsible for restricting IAV in chicken cells.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat, not only causing significant economic losses to the agricultural industry but also presenting a risk of spillover into the human population. The study aimed to explore the interferon-induced immune response to IAV in birds, as this area is not as well understood as in humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using chicken, quail, and duck cells to identify interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) and assess their role in restricting IAV replication. It focused on two strains of IAV: the mouse-adapted PR8 and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10.
analysis.methods: A CRISPR knockout ISG screen was performed against two strains of IAV, PR8 and WF10, to identify genes that restrict viral replication. The study utilized chicken, quail, and duck cells to examine the interferon-induced immune response in avian species.
analysis.main_results: For PR8, IFITM3 was identified as the dominant restrictor of viral replication, with several additional hits showing modest effects. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit, but two additional genes, BAG5 and OTUD4, were found to restrict replication, which were absent in the PR8 results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and highlight the importance of species-specific ISGs in restricting IAV replication. This study establishes a screening system for identifying ISGs relevant to avian species.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the innate immune mechanisms of avian species against IAV, which can inform strategies for surveillance, prevention, and control of avian influenza in poultry populations, as well as understanding the potential for zoonotic transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level reporting and does not provide detailed statistical analyses or experimental validation. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of comprehensive data on the functional roles of the identified ISGs in avian species.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the interferon-induced immune response to avian influenza A virus (IAV) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, revealing that only a small subset of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) restrict IAV replication. The research highlights the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species, with IFITM3 being a dominant restrictor for both PR8 and WF10 strains. However, avian-specific IAV isolate WF10 also showed additional restrictors, BAG5 and OTUD4, not observed in PR8. These findings establish a screening system for identifying ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species, contributing to understanding the innate immune mechanisms of birds against IAV. The study is limited to abstract-level reporting and lacks detailed statistical analyses or experimental validation, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 病毒 (IAV) 是一种主要的全球健康威胁,不仅给农业造成重大经济损失,而且还给人类带来 跨物种溢出 的风险。该研究旨在探索干扰素在鸟类中诱导的 免疫应答 对 IAV 的影响,因为这一领域不像人类那样被充分了解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用鸡、鹌鹑和鸭细胞来鉴定干扰素刺激基因(ISG)并评估它们在限制 IAV 复制中的作用。它重点关注两种 IAV 毒株:小鼠适应性 PR8 和低致病性禽 IAV 分离株 WF10。
elements_zh.methods: 针对两种 IAV 毒株 PR8 和 WF10 进行了 CRISPR 敲除 ISG 筛选,以鉴定限制病毒复制的基因。该研究利用鸡、鹌鹑和鸭细胞来检测鸟类中干扰素诱导的 免疫应答。
elements_zh.main_results: 对于 PR8,IFITM3 被确定为病毒复制的主要限制因子,另外几次点击显示出适度的影响。对于禽类 WF10,IFITM3 也很受欢迎,但发现另外两个基因 BAG5 和 OTUD4 限制复制,而 PR8 结果中不存在这两个基因。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证实了物种间干扰素介导的免疫的差异,并强调了物种特异性 ISG 在限制 IAV 复制中的重要性。本研究建立了一个筛选系统来识别与鸟类相关的 ISG。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对禽类针对 IAV 的先天免疫机制的深入了解,这可以为 监测、家禽种群中 禽流感 的预防和控制策略提供信息,并了解人畜共患 传播 的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的报告,不提供详细的统计分析或实验验证。由于缺乏关于已确定的 ISG 在鸟类物种中的功能作用的全面数据,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感 病毒 (IAV) 是一种主要的全球健康威胁,不仅给农业造成重大经济损失,而且还给人类带来 跨物种溢出 的风险。该研究旨在探索干扰素在鸟类中诱导的 免疫应答 对 IAV 的影响,因为这一领域不像人类那样被充分了解。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用鸡、鹌鹑和鸭细胞来鉴定干扰素刺激基因(ISG)并评估它们在限制 IAV 复制中的作用。它重点关注两种 IAV 毒株:小鼠适应性 PR8 和低致病性禽 IAV 分离株 WF10。
analysis_zh.methods: 针对两种 IAV 毒株 PR8 和 WF10 进行了 CRISPR 敲除 ISG 筛选,以鉴定限制病毒复制的基因。该研究利用鸡、鹌鹑和鸭细胞来检测鸟类中干扰素诱导的 免疫应答。
analysis_zh.main_results: 对于 PR8,IFITM3 被确定为病毒复制的主要限制因子,另外几次点击显示出适度的影响。对于禽类 WF10,IFITM3 也很受欢迎,但发现另外两个基因 BAG5 和 OTUD4 限制复制,而 PR8 结果中不存在这两个基因。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证实了物种间干扰素介导的免疫的差异,并强调了物种特异性 ISG 在限制 IAV 复制中的重要性。本研究建立了一个筛选系统来识别与鸟类相关的 ISG。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对禽类针对 IAV 的先天免疫机制的深入了解,这可以为 监测、家禽种群中 禽流感 的预防和控制策略提供信息,并了解人畜共患 传播 的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的报告,不提供详细的统计分析或实验验证。由于缺乏关于已确定的 ISG 在鸟类物种中的功能作用的全面数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Mucosal vaccination with hemagglutinin stalk provides broad protection against influenza virus subtypes in mice
papers.abstract: Influenza viruses continually evolve through antigenic drift and shift, spreading via respiratory droplets and aerosols. Developing a universal nasal vaccine is essential for preventing seasonal and pandemic infections by inducing long-lasting immunity in the respiratory tract. The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) transfers IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier. This study investigates whether the i.n. delivery of the conserved Stalk antigen of HA, utilizing the FcRn, can stimulate protective immune responses against various influenza virus subtypes. We engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form. immunized with Stalk-Fc exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with groups of control mice. The immunized mice produced long-lasting HA Stalk–specific IgA and IgG Abs in nasal washes, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood, along with tissue-resident memory T cells in the lungs and long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow. This led to notably lower viral replication in the nasal turbinate and lungs. The Stalk-specific Abs demonstrated strong cross-reactivity against different influenza subtypes through neutralization, Ab- or complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, or phagocytosis. These results indicate that FcRn efficiently transports HA Stalk-Fc across the respiratory epithelial barrier, supporting the development of a universal influenza nasal vaccine.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the mucosal vaccination with the conserved Stalk antigen of hemagglutinin (HA) in mice, utilizing the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) to transfer IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier.
analysis.methods: The researchers engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form and immunized mice with this construct.
analysis.main_results: Immunized mice exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with control mice. papers.title_zh: 具有血凝素柄的粘膜 疫苗接种 为小鼠提供针对流感病毒亚型的广泛保护
papers.source_body_en: Influenza viruses continually evolve through antigenic drift and shift, spreading via respiratory droplets and aerosols. Developing a universal nasal vaccine is essential for preventing seasonal and pandemic infections by inducing long-lasting immunity in the respiratory tract. The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) transfers IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier. This study investigates whether the i.n. delivery of the conserved Stalk antigen of HA, utilizing the FcRn, can stimulate protective immune responses against various influenza virus subtypes. We engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form. immunized with Stalk-Fc exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with groups of control mice. The immunized mice produced long-lasting HA Stalk–specific IgA and IgG Abs in nasal washes, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood, along with tissue-resident memory T cells in the lungs and long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow. This led to notably lower viral replication in the nasal turbinate and lungs. The Stalk-specific Abs demonstrated strong cross-reactivity against different influenza subtypes through neutralization, Ab- or complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, or phagocytosis. These results indicate that FcRn efficiently transports HA Stalk-Fc across the respiratory epithelial barrier, supporting the development of a universal influenza nasal vaccine.

papers.title: Emergence of a distinct evolutionary cluster of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China during 2024-2025 with rapid evolution and antigenic divergence.
papers.abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterized 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterized by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.

papers.title_zh: 2024-2025 年期间,中国出现了具有快速 进化 和抗原分歧的 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒的独特进化簇。
papers.source_body_en: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. Here, we characterized 18 H5 viruses isolated through routine surveillance in China during 2024-2025, together with publicly available clade 2.3.4.4b H5 sequences collected since 2020. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these isolates formed a distinct evolutionary cluster within clade 2.3.4.4b, designated the G2-derived emerging cluster (G2-EC), which emerged around mid-2024 and exhibited clear genetic divergence from previously circulating H5N1 viruses. G2-EC viruses accumulated a characteristic set of hemagglutinin amino acid substitutions, most of which were located in antigenic regions. Across the clade 2.3.4.4b H5 virus population, the estimated mean HA evolutionary rate was higher during 2024-2025 than during preceding periods. These genetic changes were accompanied by marked antigenic divergence from the Re14 vaccine strain, with 4- to 32-fold reductions in HI titres. Genomic analysis revealed acquisition of PB1 segment from a distinct genetic background in G2-EC H5N1 viruses, followed by the emergence of H5N6 viruses sharing a highly similar genetic backbone but carrying a distinct NA segment, indicating sequential reassortment. Animal experiments showed that representative G2-EC viruses retained high pathogenicity and efficient direct-contact transmission in SPF chickens, while exhibiting relatively limited lethality in mice. Collectively, these findings document a recent evolutionary transition of clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses in China, characterized by genetic and antigenic divergence accompanied by sequential reassortment, underscoring the need for continued genomic and antigenic surveillance.
papers.abstract_zh: 进化枝2.3.4.4b H5病毒自在中国出现以来经历了连续的进化,但最近流行的病毒的遗传和抗原多样性程度仍不清楚。在这里,我们对 2024 年至 2025 年期间在中国通过常规 监测 分离的 18 种 H5 病毒进行了特征分析,以及自 2020 年以来收集的公开的进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5 序列。系统发育分析表明,这些分离株在进化枝 2.3.4.4b 内形成了一个独特的进化簇,称为 G2 衍生的新兴簇 (G2-EC),于 2024 年中期左右出现,与之前流行的 H5N1 病毒表现出明显的遗传差异。G2-EC病毒积累了一组特征性的血凝素氨基酸取代,其中大部分位于抗原区域。在分支 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒群体中,2024-2025 年期间估计的平均 HA 进化率高于之前时期。这些基因变化伴随着与 Re14 疫苗 菌株的显着抗原差异,HI 滴度降低了 4 至 32 倍。基因组分析显示,G2-EC H5N1 病毒从不同的遗传背景中获得了 PB1 片段,随后出现了共享高度相似的遗传主链但携带不同 NA 片段的 H5N6 病毒,这表明存在连续重配。动物实验表明,代表性的G2-EC病毒在SPF鸡中保留了高致病性和高效的直接接触传播,而在小鼠中表现出相对有限的致死率。总的来说,这些发现记录了中国分支 2.3.4.4b H5 病毒最近的进化转变,其特征是遗传和抗原分歧伴随着顺序重配,强调了持续基因组和抗原 监测 的需要。

papers.title: Cross-Protection against Influenza A(H5) Clade 2.3.4.4b Viruses after A(H1N1)pdm09 Infection.
papers.abstract: We challenged ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess cross-protection. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether prior infection with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. Ferrets previously infected with A(H1N1)pdm09 were challenged with these avian influenza subtypes to assess immune responses. Results indicated partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5, possibly due to the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. The findings suggest that immunity from A(H1N1)pdm09 infection may offer some cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, which could have implications for understanding immune responses to avian influenza subtypes. However, the study is limited to an animal model and relies on a single challenge experiment, which may not fully reflect human immunity. The evidence is moderate in strength.

papers.title: A Discrete Choice Experiment to Explore Drivers of Mask-Wearing
papers.abstract: A discrete choice experiment will examine how disease factors, policy, and social factors influence mask-wearing decisions during a hypothetical bird flu outbreak. Specifically, it will explore the influence of five different factors (infection rate, mortality rate, mask mandate, social norm, presence of vulnerable others) on individuals’ decision to wear a medical mask. Due to recent outbreaks of bird flu among livestock across the US, many health professionals are concerned about the potential of the bird flu virus to mutate leading to a large outbreak among humans. Therefore, we designed our study asking participants to report how likely they would be to wear a mask in different scenarios during such a hypothetical outbreak of bird flu.

papers.title: Global monitoring of wildlife mortality through participatory science in near‐real time
papers.abstract: Detection of wildlife mortality events is critical for timely conservation and natural resource management. We present an open‐source, web‐based, decision‐support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory‐science data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events worldwide. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using four case studies spanning taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales. In Canada and the US, high peaks of bird mortality coincided with zoonotic risk during avian influenza outbreaks. Across Africa, we detected 45 mortality events of threatened species in March 2026. In California, recorded mammal mortality was associated with human infrastructure, including proximity to roads, and to a lesser extent, the human footprint. Mortality of pumas ( Puma concolor ) was detected across 12 countries, highlighting the need for international cooperation to conserve mobile species. Our tool enables resource managers to flag emerging threats and empowers participatory scientists to monitor and integrate mortality records for conservation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a participatory science approach, utilizing data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events across different regions and species. It included four case studies covering various taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales.
analysis.methods: The authors created an open-source, web-based decision-support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory science data from iNaturalist. They used this tool to analyze mortality events in specific regions and species.
analysis.main_results: In Canada and the US, high peaks of bird mortality coincided with zoonotic risk during avian influenza outbreaks. Across Africa, 45 mortality events of threatened species were detected in March 2026.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the potential of participatory science in identifying patterns of wildlife mortality linked to zoonotic risks and the importance of monitoring threatened species. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform conservation strategies by identifying emerging threats and the need for international cooperation in protecting mobile species. They also contribute to understanding zoonotic risks associated with avian influenza outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on participatory science data, which may have biases or gaps. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on aggregated data from a single platform and does not include detailed laboratory or statistical analyses.

The findings highlight the potential of participatory science in identifying zoonotic risks and the importance of international cooperation for conserving mobile species. The study's reliance on aggregated data introduces limitations, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the absence of detailed laboratory or statistical analyses.

papers.source_body_en: Detection of wildlife mortality events is critical for timely conservation and natural resource management. We present an open‐source, web‐based, decision‐support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory‐science data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events worldwide. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using four case studies spanning taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales. In Canada and the US, high peaks of bird mortality coincided with zoonotic risk during avian influenza outbreaks. Across Africa, we detected 45 mortality events of threatened species in March 2026. In California, recorded mammal mortality was associated with human infrastructure, including proximity to roads, and to a lesser extent, the human footprint. Mortality of pumas ( Puma concolor ) was detected across 12 countries, highlighting the need for international cooperation to conserve mobile species. Our tool enables resource managers to flag emerging threats and empowers participatory scientists to monitor and integrate mortality records for conservation.

papers.title: Assessment of Biosecurity Measures in Live Poultry Markets in N’Djamena, Chad
papers.abstract: Background and Objective: Although, biosecurity is a primary means of disease prevention in livestock farming, implementing these measures remains challenging in live poultry supply chains. This study evaluated the implementation of biosecurity measures across four major commercial markets in N'Djamena, Chad: Al-Afia, Champs de Fil, Diguel and Dembé. Methodology: Between July and August 2023, a cross-sectional survey was conducted among 120 permanent live poultry vendors. A structured questionnaire was used to assess vendors' awareness of avian pathogens, knowledge of biosecurity standards and implementation of sanitary practices. Results: The results showed that 60.83% of vendors had low levels of biosecurity knowledge, 23.34% had moderate knowledge and 15.83% had good knowledge. Dembé market had the highest proportion of vendors with good biosecurity knowledge, with 6.67% of the total respondents classified in this category and a Mean±SD of 6.67±0.97%, significantly higher than the corresponding values for Al-Afia (2.50±0.31%) and Diguel (1.66±0.09%). Regarding compliance, 60% of vendors failed to implement biosecurity protocols, whereas only 5% adhered strictly to the recommended standards. Complete non-implementation was most prevalent at Diguel (17.50±4.28%) and Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%), compared with Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%). These deficiencies were associated with a lack of formal training, inadequate market infrastructure and low perceived immediate health risks. Conclusion: The findings indicate substantial gaps in biosecurity knowledge and compliance among live poultry vendors in N'Djamena. Given the potential role of live poultry markets in the transmission of avian influenza, Newcastle disease and other infectious diseases, targeted training programs, infrastructure improvements and strengthened regulatory frameworks are urgently needed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估乍得恩贾梅纳活家禽市场生物安全措施的实施情况,因为生物安全是畜牧业疾病预防的主要手段,但这些措施在活家禽供应链中仍然具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对乍得恩贾梅纳四个主要商业市场(Al-Afia、Champs de Fil、Diguel 和 Dembé)的 120 个固定活家禽供应商进行了横断面调查。
elements_zh.methods: 2023 年 7 月至 8 月期间,使用结构化调查问卷评估供应商对禽类病原体的认识、生物安全标准的了解以及卫生实践的实施情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,60.83%的商户生物安全知识水平较低,23.34%的商户生物安全知识水平一般,15.83%的商户生物安全知识水平较高。Dembé 市场拥有良好生物安全知识的供应商比例最高,占受访者总数的 6.67%,Mean±SD 为 6.67±0.97%,显着高于 Al-Afia(2.50±0.31%)和 Diguel(1.66±0.09%)的相应值。在合规性方面,60% 的供应商未能实施生物安全协议,而只有 5% 的供应商严格遵守建议的标准。与 Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%) 相比,完全不执行的情况在 Diguel (17.50±4.28%) 和 Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%) 最为普遍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 调查结果表明,恩贾梅纳的活家禽供应商在生物安全知识和合规性方面存在巨大差距,凸显了有针对性的培训计划、基础设施改进和强化监管框架的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究深入了解了活禽市场的生物安全实践,这对于预防 传播 和其他传染病至关重要,并强调了改进这些实践以保障公众健康的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。证据是温和的,因为它是基于调查结果而不是直接的生物学或临床测量。

A structured questionnaire was used to assess vendors' awareness of avian pathogens, knowledge of biosecurity standards and implementation of sanitary practices. Results: The results showed that 60.83% of vendors had low levels of biosecurity knowledge, 23.34% had moderate knowledge and 15.83% had good knowledge. Dembé market had the highest proportion of vendors with good biosecurity knowledge, with 6.67% of the total respondents classified in this category and a Mean±SD of 6.67±0.97%, significantly higher than the corresponding values for Al-Afia (2.50±0.31%) and Diguel (1.66±0.09%). Regarding compliance, 60% of vendors failed to implement biosecurity protocols, whereas only 5% adhered strictly to the recommended standards. Complete non-implementation was most prevalent at Diguel (17.50±4.28%) and Al-Afia (15.00±3.44%), compared with Champs de Fil (10.83±2.87%). These deficiencies were associated with a lack of formal training, inadequate market infrastructure and low perceived immediate health risks. Conclusion: The findings indicate substantial gaps in biosecurity knowledge and compliance among live poultry vendors in N'Djamena. Given the potential role of live poultry markets in the transmission of avian influenza, Newcastle disease and other infectious diseases, targeted training programs, infrastructure improvements and strengthened regulatory frameworks are urgently needed.

papers.title: Legal Approaches advancing One health
papers.abstract: This paper examines the development of the One Health approach at global and European Union (EU) levels, arguing that a regulatory perspective is essential for its effective implementation. Following a brief introduction, Paragraph II outlines the historical evolution of One Health, showing its progression from a predominantly sanitary concept to one that fully incorporates environmental dimensions. Paragraph III analyses the contribution of international organizations in promoting and operationalizing the approach. Paragraph IV discusses the role of legislation in institutionalizing One Health and reviews different legal pathways – ranging from its recognition as a general legal principle to its integration into sector specific legislation and the adoption of a comprehensive framework law – illustrated with examples from EU laws and policies. Paragraph V presents concrete instances of how One Health has been incorporated into legal systems, particularly in the areas of avian influenza, biodiversity conservation and agri-food systems, again drawing on EU regulation. The paper concludes that no single legal model can universally operationalize One Health; rather, the choice of regulatory approach must be adapted to the specific policy priorities and institutional context of each country or forum.

papers.abstract_zh: 本文探讨了“同一个健康”方法在全球和欧盟 (EU) 层面的发展,认为监管视角对于其有效实施至关重要。在简要介绍之后,第二段概述了 One Health 的历史 进化,展示了其从主要卫生概念到完全融入环境维度的概念的进展。第三段分析了国际组织在促进和实施该方法方面的贡献。第四段讨论了立法在“统一健康”制度化中的作用,并回顾了不同的法律途径——从将其视为一项一般法律原则到将其纳入具体部门的立法以及采用全面的框架法——并以欧盟法律和政策的例子进行说明。第五段介绍了如何将“同一个健康”纳入法律体系的具体实例,特别是在 禽流感、生物多样性保护和农业食品系统领域,再次借鉴欧盟法规。该文件的结论是,没有任何单一的法律模式可以普遍实施“同一个健康”;相反,监管方法的选择必须适应每个国家或论坛的具体政策优先事项和体制背景。

papers.title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices Regarding One Health and Zoonotic Diseases Among Undergraduate Medical Students at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background Zoonotic diseases are a major public health concern in Northeast India, and future physicians need One Health competencies to control them. We assessed One Health and zoonosis-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among MBBS students. Methodology This cross-sectional study (September 11 to October 11, 2026) used an attempted census of MBBS students across all three phases (Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III, the last comprising Part I and Part II) at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, Assam. A pilot-tested online questionnaire assessed knowledge (20 items), attitude, and practice (15 items each); scores ≥80% (modified Bloom’s cut-offs) indicated good knowledge, positive attitude, or good practice. Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square, and multivariable logistic regression were used for data analysis. analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 建议在所有阶段进行结构化的“同一个健康”教学,强调重点人畜共患疾病、与兽医学生的联合学习以及实地培训。大约三分之二(326 人,63.7%)支持将“同一个健康”纳入 MBBS 课程。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告与研究设计或数据分析相关的具体限制。由于研究的横截面性质以及自我报告数据的潜在偏差,置信度为中等。

papers.title: Rising biosecurity threats: Insights from Queensland’s approach to advancing response readiness
papers.abstract: Effective biosecurity is a growing global challenge, rapidly escalating in scale, complexity, cost, and consequence. Best-practice biosecurity seeks to protect people, animals, and the environment from exotic pests and diseases, yet ensuring a resilient response framework remains difficult, even in geographically remote countries such as Australia. Biosecurity incidents are an underappreciated security risk, increasing in both frequency and intensity within an era of polycrisis, where climate variability, natural disasters, geopolitical instability, disrupted supply chains, food insecurity, pandemics, and economic volatility interact and amplify impacts. Drawing on a government practitioner perspective, this paper argues that biosecurity must be understood as a disaster resilience issue rather than solely an agricultural one. Using examples including red imported fire ants and preparedness for highly pathogenic avian influenza, it highlights how biological threats increasingly intersect with public health, environmental management, emergency preparedness, and community resilience. The paper demonstrates the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement. Industries, governments, and communities all play critical roles in preventing, identifying, and responding to biosecurity threats. Advancing response readiness requires stronger partnerships, trusted networks, and governance arrangements capable of managing escalating biological risks in an increasingly complex, interconnected, and uncertain operating environment. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the growing global challenge of effective biosecurity, particularly in the context of avian influenza A viruses, avian-origin zoonotic infections, and their subtypes. The central question is how to enhance response readiness to these biological threats, considering their increasing frequency and intensity in an era of polycrisis. The scope includes examining biosecurity as a disaster resilience issue, not solely an agricultural one, and highlights the need for cross-sector coordination, early detection, and community engagement.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a government practitioner perspective, drawing on examples such as red imported fire ants and preparedness for highly pathogenic avian influenza. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria. The methods section emphasizes the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement as key components of a resilient biosecurity framework.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that biosecurity incidents are an underappreciated security risk, increasing in both frequency and intensity due to the interactions of multiple global crises. It highlights that biological threats increasingly intersect with public health, environmental management, emergency preparedness, and community resilience. The paper demonstrates the importance of early detection, cross-sector coordination, surge capability, institutional adaptability, and sustained community engagement in managing these risks.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a lack of emphasis on biosecurity as a disaster resilience issue rather than an agricultural one. It also notes that while the importance of early detection and cross-sector coordination is acknowledged, there is a gap in understanding how these strategies can be effectively implemented in an increasingly complex and interconnected operating environment. Additionally, the review does not provide detailed evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions or the extent of their application across different regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that advancing response readiness requires stronger partnerships, trusted networks, and governance arrangements capable of managing escalating biological risks. It highlights the need for sustained community engagement and institutional adaptability. Furthermore, it calls for a more integrated approach to biosecurity that considers its intersection with public health, environmental management, and emergency preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the growing global challenge of effective biosecurity, particularly in the context of avian influenza A viruses and related zoonotic infections. It argues that biosecurity must be understood as a disaster resilience issue, not solely an agricultural one, and highlights the need for cross-sector coordination, early detection, and community engagement. The paper demonstrates the importance of institutional adaptability and surge capability in managing escalating biological risks. While it provides general insights into the increasing frequency and intensity of biosecurity threats, it does not offer detailed evidence on the effectiveness of specific interventions. The review calls for stronger partnerships and governance arrangements to enhance response readiness in an increasingly complex and uncertain environment.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注有效生物安全方面日益严峻的全球挑战,特别是在 禽流感 A 病毒、禽源人畜共患感染及其亚型的背景下。核心问题是,考虑到在多重危机时代这些生物威胁的频率和强度不断增加,如何加强对这些生物威胁的应对准备。范围包括将生物安全视为一个抗灾问题,而不仅仅是农业问题,并强调跨部门协调、早期发现和社区参与的必要性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于政府从业者的角度,借鉴了红火蚁和 高致病性禽流感 的准备等例子。它不报告特定数据库、检索日期或资格标准。方法部分强调了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与作为弹性生物安全框架关键组成部分的重要性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,由于多种全球危机的相互作用,其频率和强度都在增加。它强调生物威胁日益与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力相互交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与在管理这些风险方面的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查指出,生物安全缺乏作为抗灾问题而不是农业问题的重视。报告还指出,虽然早期发现和跨部门协调的重要性已得到承认,但在理解如何在日益复杂和相互关联的运营环境中有效实施这些策略方面存在差距。此外,该审查没有提供具体干预措施的有效性或其在不同地区的应用程度的详细证据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、值得信赖的网络和能够管理不断升级的生物风险的治理安排。它强调了持续社区参与和机构适应性的必要性。此外,它呼吁采取更加综合的生物安全方法,考虑其与公共卫生、环境管理和应急准备的交叉点。

papers.abstract_zh: 有效的生物安全是一项日益严峻的全球挑战,其规模、复杂性、成本和后果迅速升级。最佳实践生物安全旨在保护人类、动物和环境免受外来病虫害的侵害,但确保有弹性的应对框架仍然很困难,即使在澳大利亚等地理位置偏远的国家也是如此。生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,在多重危机时代,其频率和强度都在增加,气候变化、自然灾害、地缘政治不稳定、供应链中断、粮食不安全、流行病和经济波动相互作用并放大影响。本文从政府从业者的角度出发,认为生物安全必须被理解为一个抗灾问题,而不仅仅是一个农业问题。它以红火蚁和 高致病性禽流感 的防备为例,强调了生物威胁如何与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力日益交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与的重要性。行业、政府和社区在预防、识别和应对生物安全威胁方面都发挥着关键作用。推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、可信网络和治理安排,以便能够在日益复杂、相互关联和不确定的运营环境中管理不断升级的生物风险。本文还包含在《商业与管理合集》中,可通过 https://hstalks.com/business/ 访问。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注有效生物安全方面日益严峻的全球挑战,特别是在 禽流感 A 病毒、禽源人畜共患感染及其亚型的背景下。核心问题是,考虑到在多重危机时代这些生物威胁的频率和强度不断增加,如何加强对这些生物威胁的应对准备。范围包括将生物安全视为一个抗灾问题,而不仅仅是农业问题,并强调跨部门协调、早期发现和社区参与的必要性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于政府从业者的角度,借鉴了红火蚁和 高致病性禽流感 的准备等例子。它不报告特定数据库、检索日期或资格标准。方法部分强调了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与作为弹性生物安全框架关键组成部分的重要性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,生物安全事件是一种被低估的安全风险,由于多种全球危机的相互作用,其频率和强度都在增加。它强调生物威胁日益与公共卫生、环境管理、应急准备和社区复原力相互交叉。该文件论证了早期发现、跨部门协调、激增能力、机构适应性和持续社区参与在管理这些风险方面的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查指出,生物安全缺乏作为抗灾问题而不是农业问题的重视。报告还指出,虽然早期发现和跨部门协调的重要性已得到承认,但在理解如何在日益复杂和相互关联的运营环境中有效实施这些策略方面存在差距。此外,该审查没有提供具体干预措施的有效性或其在不同地区的应用程度的详细证据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,推进应对准备工作需要更强有力的伙伴关系、值得信赖的网络和能够管理不断升级的生物风险的治理安排。它强调了持续社区参与和机构适应性的必要性。此外,它呼吁采取更加综合的生物安全方法,考虑其与公共卫生、环境管理和应急准备的交叉点。

Can India's new H5N1 chicken vaccine do more than prevent deaths? Discover how vaccine research is tackling bird flu, viral shedding and poultry protection. India is set to introduce its first indigenously developed vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza (bird flu) in chickens, marking an important step toward strengthening poultry disease control, reducing dependence on imported vaccines, and protecting the country's poultry industry from devastating outbreaks. The development comes at a time when highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), particularly H5N1, remains a major concern globally because of its ability to trigger severe outbreaks in poultry, cause high mortality, disrupt food production, and create significant economic losses for farmers. According to reports, India plans to launch the domestically developed H5N1 chicken vaccine on November 20, 2026, potentially adding a new tool to its bird flu prevention and control strategy.() Bird Flu Bird flu (avian influenza/avian flu) is a disease caused by an influenza virus (H5N1) that primarily affects birds but can infect humans also. How the Vaccine Could Strengthen India's Bird Flu Response The vaccine is an inactivated H5N1 vaccine targeting Clade 2.3.2.1a, () a strain associated with outbreaks in Indian poultry. It was developed by scientists at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal. The significance lies in developing a vaccine suited to virus strains circulating in India. Bird flu outbreaks can lead to large-scale poultry deaths, emergency culling, restrictions on movement and trade, and considerable financial losses for farmers. The Government of India says more than 500 combined H5N1 and H5N8 outbreaks have been reported in the country since 2006. The vaccine could provide an additional layer of protection for poultry, particularly in regions vulnerable to recurring outbreaks. However, the announcement of its development and dedication does not necessarily mean immediate nationwide vaccination. Deployment, regulatory approvals, vaccination strategy, monitoring and field effectiveness will determine how soon it can be used and how much impact it delivers. Bird Flu Outbreak Strikes Japan Poultry Farm, HPAI Confirmed Japan reports HPAI bird flu outbreak in Hokkaido poultry farm affecting 190,000 birds, reinforcing global monitoring of avian influenza and zoonotic risk. How Effective Are H5N1 Vaccines in Preventing Bird Flu in Chickens? Research published in 2026 highlights both the potential and the limitations of poultry vaccination. A September 2026 study examining six commercial H5 vaccines against newer H5N1 and H5N8 strains found that vaccination protected many chickens against death, but some vaccinated birds continued shedding virus. () The researchers emphasized that vaccine matching with circulating strains is critical to reducing transmission—not simply preventing mortality. This is particularly relevant to India's vaccine, which targets a specific H5N1 clade. Another study published in Vaccines in November 2026 reported that an enhanced inactivated H5N1 vaccine formulation improved immune responses and accelerated the reduction of viral shedding in experimentally vaccinated chickens. The findings reinforce the importance of vaccine design, immune response and transmission control when evaluating poultry vaccines. () These studies suggest that India's vaccine will need continued evaluation under field conditions to establish how effectively it prevents infection, reduces virus shedding and protects flocks against circulating viruses. Bird Flu Before Christmas: Should Turkey Lovers Be Worried? Bird flu has been confirmed at a Northumberland farm housing 32,000 free-range hens, raising concerns about further outbreaks and possible Christmas turkey supply disruptions. Can India's H5N1 Chicken Vaccine Help Reduce Bird Flu Risk to Humans? H5N1 is primarily an avian virus, but it can infect humans following exposure to infected birds or contaminated environments. Reducing infections in poultry could help lower the risk of human exposure, especially for poultry workers, farm owners, culling teams and people handling infected birds. The World Health Organization (WHO) says human infections are generally associated with exposure to infected animals, and sustained human-to-human transmission of currently circulating H5 viruses has not been demonstrated. () () A One Health approach involving animal, human and environmental surveillance remains essential. India's indigenous H5N1 vaccine is therefore more than a veterinary research achievement. It could become an important part of the country's strategy to protect poultry production, safeguard farmers' livelihoods and reduce the circulation of dangerous avian influenza viruses. Its success, however, will depend on how effectively vaccination is combined with surveillance, biosecurity, outbreak containment and scientific monitoring. analysis.brief_en: India is preparing to launch its first domestically developed vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza in chickens, as reported in a November 19, 2026, news article. The vaccine, developed by scientists at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), targets a specific H5N1 clade associated with outbreaks in the country. While the vaccine is expected to reduce poultry deaths and viral shedding, some studies suggest that vaccinated birds may still shed the virus, highlighting the need for continued evaluation. The government has reported over 500 combined H5N1 and H5N8 outbreaks since 2006, underscoring the importance of this new tool in controlling the disease. However, the vaccine's effectiveness and impact will depend on its implementation, regulatory approvals, and integration with surveillance and biosecurity measures. The World Health Organization (WHO) notes that human infections with H5N1 are generally linked to exposure to infected animals, and sustained human-to-human transmission has not been observed. This development is part of a broader strategy to protect poultry production, safeguard farmers' livelihoods, and reduce the circulation of dangerous avian influenza viruses.

news.content_zh: 据 2026 年 11 月 19 日的新闻文章报道,印度正准备在鸡中推出首个国内开发的针对 H5N1 禽流感 的 疫苗。疫苗 由印度农业研究委员会国家高安全动物疾病研究所 (ICAR-NIHSAD) 的科学家开发,针对该国与 暴发 相关的特定 H5N1 进化枝。虽然 疫苗 预计将减少家禽死亡和病毒传播,但一些研究表明,接种疫苗的家禽仍可能传播病毒,这凸显了继续评估的必要性。自 2006 年以来,政府已报告了 500 多例 H5N1 和 H5N8 暴发 混合病例,强调了这种新工具在控制该疾病方面的重要性。然而,疫苗 的有效性和影响将取决于其实施、监管批准以及与 监测 和生物安全措施的整合。世界卫生组织 (WHO) 指出,人类感染 H5N1 通常与接触受感染的动物有关,并且尚未观察到持续的人际 传播。这一发展是保护家禽生产、保障农民生计和减少危险 禽流感 病毒传播的更广泛战略的一部分。

news.excerpt: India is set to launch its first indigenously developed vaccine against the highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu virus, marking a significant step towards protecting the countrys poultry industry from ...

news.content_title: India to launch first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens tomorrow - The Tribune
news.content: India to launch first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens tomorrow Developed by ICAR scientists in Bhopal, vaccine targets strain responsible for most poultry outbreaks; over 500 bird flu outbreaks reported in India since 2006 India is set to launch its first indigenously developed vaccine against the highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu virus, marking a significant step towards protecting the country's poultry industry from recurring avian influenza outbreaks. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) vaccine for chickens to the nation on Thursday. Developed by scientists at the Bhopal-based ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), the vaccine is the first of its kind in India specifically targeting the H5N1 virus belonging to Clade 2.3.2.1a, a strain identified as responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens in the country. The development is significant as no specific commercial vaccine was previously available against this particular strain. "The indigenous formulation is expected to strengthen India's capacity to prevent and control outbreaks that have repeatedly resulted in mass culling of poultry, financial losses for farmers and disruptions in the poultry trade," an Agriculture Ministry official said. More than 500 bird flu outbreaks involving the H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported in India since the disease was first detected in the country in 2006, according to the ministry. Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu, is a severe infectious disease affecting poultry. Outbreaks can result in mortality approaching 100 per cent among infected birds, often forcing authorities to undertake large-scale culling and impose restrictions on the movement and trade of poultry products. However, the minister has not specified the vaccine's commercial availability, production arrangements, pricing, vaccination schedule or the scale and timeline of its deployment across poultry farms. Its effectiveness in protecting the poultry sector will ultimately depend on how widely and efficiently it is deployed, alongside disease surveillance, early diagnosis, farm-level biosecurity and coordinated outbreak-response measures. The development marks an important step towards strengthening India's indigenous veterinary vaccine research and reducing the vulnerability of its poultry industry to recurring outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza. Beyond its economic impact on poultry, H5N1 remains a significant global public health concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, had been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003

news.source_body_en: India is set to launch its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens on Thursday, November 19, 2026, developed by scientists at the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal. The vaccine targets the H5N1 strain, specifically Clade 2.3.2.1a, which has been responsible for most poultry outbreaks in the country since 2006. Over 500 bird flu outbreaks involving H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported, leading to mass culling, financial losses for farmers, and disruptions in the poultry trade. The vaccine is a significant development as no specific commercial vaccine was previously available against this strain. However, the minister has not provided details on its commercial availability, production arrangements, pricing, vaccination schedule, or deployment scale. The effectiveness of the vaccine in protecting the poultry sector will depend on its widespread use and coordination with disease surveillance, early diagnosis, and farm-level biosecurity measures. This marks an important step in strengthening India's indigenous veterinary vaccine research and reducing the vulnerability of its poultry industry to recurring outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza.

news.content: LOGINSIGNUP News Health Tech Pharma Hospitals & Providers Diagnostics Medical Devices Policy & Public Health Finance Precision Medicine Global View All News Podcast The Big Idea Bold Voices Compassionate Voices Visionary Healers Voices of Cardiology Legacy Labs Renal Icons Voice of Change Oncology Voices The Bone SIP From Awareness to Action Fem Series View All Podcast VOH Exclusives Insights Listicles Editorials Knowledge Hub Spotlight Stories View All VOH Exclusives VOH TV Daily Broadcast Expert Speaks View All VOH TV Web Stories Events Conferences & Summits Brand Solutions Health & Awareness View All Events VOH Products Newsletter Daily Weekly Monthly View All Newsletter Advisory LOGINSIGNUP News Podcast VOH Exclusives VOH TV Web Stories Events VOH Products Newsletter Advisory Home› News› Global› India Develops First Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine to Strengthen Bird Flu Prevention Global India Develops First Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine to Strengthen Bird Flu Prevention VOH Desk Published on:Nov 18, 2026 Avian Influenza VaccineH5N1 Bird FluICAR Developed by ICAR and NIHSAD, the inactivated vaccine targets the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain responsible for several poultry outbreaks in India, strengthening the country's preparedness against avian influenza. India has developed its first indigenously produced vaccine against the H5N1 avian influenza virus, marking an important step towards strengthening national preparedness against highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). The inactivated vaccine has been developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) to target the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain associated with multiple bird flu outbreaks in Indian poultry. The development addresses a critical gap in India's disease-control preparedness, as no specific commercially available vaccine currently provides protection against this particular strain in the country. The vaccine is expected to protect against circulating H5N1 strains belonging to the targeted clade. The virus poses significant challenges to poultry farming, with outbreaks potentially causing nearly 100% mortality among infected birds. Beyond livestock losses, bird flu can disrupt international trade, increase poultry product prices and affect farmers' livelihoods. The 2006 bird flu outbreak in India resulted in estimated direct and indirect economic losses of ₹2,200–3,000 crore. Upcoming Conferences and Events Physical EventNov 26th, 2026 Dental Excellence Awards 2026 The public health implications are also significant. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 1,003 human H5N1 infections, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. The targeted Clade 2.3.2.1a strain has been associated with outbreaks in poultry and has also been detected in other animal species, including mammals. Three human cases linked to infections with this strain have also been reported, highlighting the importance of controlling its spread across species. The indigenous vaccine represents a significant development in India's veterinary disease-control capabilities, with the potential to strengthen poultry health protection, reduce economic losses and support broader efforts to limit the transmission of avian influenza between animals and humans. news.title: India to get first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens on November 20
news.excerpt: India introduces its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, to protect poultry and prevent transmission.

news.content: Market Data Englishआवाज़ Stocks/ Latest News Market Stocks IPOs Commodities Personal Finance Mutual Funds BusinessEconomyIndiaWorldTechnologyPhotos More LifestyleCultureFood & DrinksHealthcare TravelVideosSportsEntertainmentUpcoming Events IPs & Events IPs & Events LIVE TV CNBC TV18CNBC TV18 PrimeCNBC AwaazCNBC Bajar Healthcare India to get first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens on November 20 By:CNBCTV18.com November 18, 2026 | 13:07 IST Edited bySudarsanan M Published OnNov 18, 2026 | 13:07 IST Last Updated OnNov 18, 2026 | 13:07 IST Twitter Whatsapp Facebook LinkedIn Copy Link Developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, the inactivated vaccine targets the H5N1 virus strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a. (Image AI generated) AI Summary India's first home-grown avian flu vaccine specifically targets the aggressive strain responsible for widespread poultry losses and severe economic shocks. By curbing infections among chickens, the immunization aims to safeguard vulnerable livestock populations and mitigate growing public health risks. Find out how authorities plan to roll out distribution across high-risk farming regions. +Follow on GoogleAdd as preferred source India is set to introduce its first indigenous vaccine against the H5N1 bird flu virus for chickens. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the vaccine to the nation on November 20, at ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal. Developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, the inactivated vaccine targets the H5N1 virus strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a. According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, it is the “first of its kind in India against the H5N1 HPAI virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a.” Why is the H5N1 vaccine important? Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), also called bird flu, is a severe viral infection that affects poultry. Outbreaks can cause mortality rates of nearly 100% among infected birds, resulting in heavy losses for poultry farmers due to bird culling and trade restrictions. India first detected the disease in 2006. Since then, more than 500 combined outbreaks involving H5N1 and H5N8 strains have been reported in the country. The ministry said a major bird flu outbreak could put more than 20% of India's poultry population at risk and reduce the country's GDP growth by up to 1.5%. The 2006 outbreak alone caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200–3,000 crore. H5N1 strain poses wider concerns According to the ministry, the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. In recent years, infections involving this strain have also been detected in other animal species, including mammals, as well as in three human cases. The disease is also a public health concern. The ministry cited World Health Organisation data showing that 1,003 human cases of H5N1 infection, including 479 deaths, had been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. How the indigenous vaccine will help The ministry said no specific commercial vaccine was available against the H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain. The indigenous vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD is intended to provide protection against strains of the virus circulating in India. "This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans," the ministry said. Agency News National Shivraj Singh Chouhan to dedicate India’s first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry to nation today By IANS - November 20, 2026 Spread the love Tweet Shivraj Singh Chouhan to dedicate India’s first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry to nation today New Delhi: Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, will dedicate India’s first “indigenous inactivated H5N1 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus vaccine” for poultry to the nation on Friday. Bhopal-based ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) has developed a vaccine against the deadly animal disease ‘Bird Flu’, also known as Avian Influenza, officials said. The vaccine will be unveiled at the institute and marks a major step toward strengthening disease control in the country’s poultry sector. Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), widely known as bird flu, poses a grave risk to chickens and other avian species, with outbreaks often resulting in total flock mortality rates. In addition to necessitating mass culling and trade bans, bird flu disrupts international markets, drives up poultry product prices, and inflicts heavy financial losses on farmers. Since the first reported case in India in 2006, the country has experienced over 500 outbreaks involving the H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes. Official estimates indicate that a major outbreak could reduce India’s GDP growth by 1.5 per cent and put more than 20 per cent of the nation’s poultry population at risk. Past outbreaks have already demonstrated this financial vulnerability: the 2006 outbreak resulted in estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore, while a separate outbreak in Manipur caused losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the state’s GDP. In addition to agricultural losses, H5N1 carries serious public health implications. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza — resulting in 479 deaths — have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. Virological studies show that the “H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain” has been responsible for most outbreaks in chickens, with recent infections also detected in mammals alongside three reported human cases. Until now, no specific commercial vaccine was available to protect poultry against the circulating Clade 2.3.2.1a strain. ICAR-NIHSAD’s indigenous vaccine fills this critical void by helping to protect poultry from the circulating strain, reducing economic losses for farmers, and limiting the virus’s transmission from chickens to other animals and humans. news.title: India to unveil indigenous H5N1 poultry vaccine
news.excerpt: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, to the nation on Friday.
news.rss_summary_html: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, to the nation on Friday.

news.content: Friday, Nov 20, 2026 Search Hyderabad Telangana AP News India World Entertainment Sport Science and Tech Business Rewind ... NRI View Point cartoon My Space Education Today Reviews Property Lifestyle E-Paper NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | India | India S First Indigenous H5n1 Bird Flu Vaccine For Poultry A0ce014b India to unveil indigenous H5N1 poultry vaccine Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, to the nation on Friday. By Telangana Today Desk Published Date - 20 November 2026, 07:22 AM Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry to the nation at ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, today. ICAR-NIHSAD developed indigenous vaccine New Delhi: Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first “indigenous inactivated H5N1 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus vaccine” for poultry to the nation on Friday. The Bhopal-based Indian Council of Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) developed the vaccine against bird flu, also known as avian influenza, officials said. The vaccine will be unveiled at the institute and marks a major step towards strengthening disease control in the country’s poultry sector, officials said. Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), widely known as bird flu, poses a risk to chickens and other avian species, with outbreaks often resulting in total flock mortality. Bird flu also necessitates mass culling and trade bans, disrupts international markets, raises poultry product prices and causes financial losses to farmers. Since the first reported case in India in 2006, the country has recorded over 500 outbreaks involving the H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes. Official estimates indicate that a major outbreak could reduce India’s GDP growth by 1.5 per cent and put more than 20 per cent of the nation’s poultry population at risk. The 2006 outbreak resulted in estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore, while a separate outbreak in Manipur caused losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the State’s GDP. H5N1 also has public health implications. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, resulting in 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. Virological studies show that the “H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain” has been responsible for most outbreaks in chickens, with recent infections also detected in mammals alongside three reported human cases. Until now, no specific commercial vaccine was available to protect poultry against the circulating Clade 2.3.2.1a strain. ICAR-NIHSAD’s indigenous vaccine will help protect poultry from the circulating strain, reduce economic losses for farmers and limit the virus’s transmission from chickens to other animals and humans, officials said. In short India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza vaccine for poultry will be dedicated to the nation on Friday. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases developed the vaccine in Bhopal. Officials said the vaccine will protect poultry against the circulating strain and reduce losses to farmers. news.title_zh: 印度将推出本土 H5N1 家禽 疫苗
news.source_body_en: India is set to unveil its first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry on Friday, November 20, 2026, at ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal. The vaccine, developed by the institute, aims to protect poultry against the circulating H5N1 strain, reduce economic losses for farmers, and limit the virus’s transmission to other animals and humans. Since its first reported case in 2006, H5N1 has caused over 500 outbreaks in India, with potential risks to more than 20% of the poultry population and estimated GDP losses of 1.5%. The virus, known as Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), can lead to total flock mortality, mass culling, and trade bans, disrupting international markets and raising poultry product prices. The vaccine marks a significant step in disease control and is part of the government’s efforts to address the threat posed by H5N1.
