Go Ad Lite Homehealthhealthcare India unveils 1st homegrown H5N1 vaccine to combat bird flu amid rising outbreaks The impact of bird flu is not limited to poultry farms. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses. Moreover, it also affects global trade, prices of poultry products and the livelihoods of farmers. DH Online Last Updated : 18 November 2026, 16:51 IST Join Us Prefer 0 A representational image Credit: iStock In an effort to strengthen India’s preparedness for controlling outbreaks caused by highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), the country is launching its first indigenously developed vaccine against the H5N1 bird flu virus. ANYTIME, ANYWHERE. Experience a more refined e-paper today Read E-Paper Story continues below. Go Ad Lite Story continues below. Go Ad Lite Developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), the inactivated vaccine will target the H5N1 virus belonging to Clade 2.3.2.1a. This strain is linked to several bird flu outbreaks in chickens in India. In recent times, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, along with three human cases. This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans. The vaccine is expected to protect against H5N1 strains of this clade circulating in India. At present, there is no specific commercially available vaccine in India providing protection against the Clade 2.3.2.1a H5N1 virus strain. Therefore, this discovery is crucial for the ountry. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses. Moreover, it also affects global trade, prices of poultry products and the livelihoods of farmers. For instance, the 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs. 2,200–3,000 crore. The disease is also a public health concern. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. Studies have shown that the H5N1 strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. Recently, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in other animal species, including mammals, as well as three human cases. The vaccine is expected to address the circulating H5N1 strains in the country, enhancing preparedness against the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks.

The vaccine, developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), targets the H5N1 virus responsible for nearly 100 per cent mortality in infected birds, causing major financial losses for poultry farmers. The strain has also been detected in mammals and three human cases, raising public health concerns. Currently, there is no specific vaccine available in India for this strain, making the new development essential for controlling the spread and protecting both animal and human populations. The vaccine is expected to address the circulating H5N1 strains in the country, enhancing preparedness against the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks.

Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the vaccine to the nation at the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal on November 20. Advertisement × PLAYSTREAM 00:00 StayNext 00:00 Ad will close in:click to close Developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, the inactivated vaccine targets the H5N1 virus of clade 2.3.2.1a, which has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. According to the statement, a single dose provides protection for up to six months, making it suitable for layer and breeder chickens. Bird flu outbreaks The development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks in parts of the country, including Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, which have reported bird deaths and culling as part of containment measures. Also read: H5N1 bird flu alert in India: crows, poultry die across states In Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore district, H5N1 infection was confirmed in November following sudden bird deaths at poultry farms. As of November 13, 35,647 birds had died in the affected zone. Authorities initiated culling within a one-kilometre radius of the affected premises, with around 40,000 chickens subsequently reported to have been culled. Poultry movement was also restricted. Andhra Pradesh reported an outbreak in October in Anantapur district, including Siddarampuram village in Bukkarayasamudram mandal. The state government declared infected and surveillance zones and imposed restrictions on poultry movement. H5N1 strain Bird flu, or highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), can cause severe disease and high mortality among poultry. Outbreaks often lead to large-scale culling, movement restrictions and trade disruptions, causing substantial losses to farmers. Since the disease was first detected in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of the H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported. Also read: Avian flu confirmed in Kerala's Alappuzha; nearly 6,000 birds to be culled The government says the H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1a strain has also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, as well as in three human cases. The World Health Organization has reported 1,003 human cases of H5N1, including 479 deaths, across 25 countries since 2003. Until now, no specific commercial vaccine has been available against the H5N1 virus of clade 2.3.2.1a. The indigenous vaccine is expected to add another tool to India’s efforts to control outbreaks, alongside surveillance, testing, biosecurity and culling. bird flu virusVaccines Comments X Please login to post a comment Login Leave a comment undefined Post Newest Oldest Popular Attachments Newest Newest Oldest Popular Attachments No attachments Drop files here Next Story X

analysis.time: The vaccine development was announced on 18 Nov 2026, with the H5N1 outbreak in Tamil Nadu confirmed in November and the 35,647 bird deaths reported as of November 13.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreaks were reported in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, specifically in Cuddalore district and Anantapur district, affecting poultry and leading to culling and movement restrictions.
analysis.event: India has developed its first indigenous vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza, which targets the H5N1 virus of clade 2.3.2.1a, responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. The development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks and culling measures.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of November 13, 35,647 birds had died in the affected zone, and around 40,000 chickens were culled. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The vaccine is expected to add another tool to India’s efforts to control outbreaks, alongside surveillance, testing, biosecurity, and culling. The Union Agriculture Minister will dedicate the vaccine to the nation on November 20.

analysis.brief_en: India has developed its first indigenous vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza, targeting the clade 2.3.2.1a strain, which has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. The vaccine, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, provides protection for up to six months and is suitable for layer and breeder chickens. This development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, where 35,647 birds had died as of November 13, and around 40,000 chickens were culled. Authorities have imposed movement restrictions and declared infected and surveillance zones. The H5N1 strain has also been detected in mammals and three human cases, with the World Health Organization reporting 1,003 human cases and 479 deaths globally since 2003. The vaccine is expected to enhance India’s preparedness for outbreaks, alongside existing measures such as surveillance, testing, biosecurity, and culling. The Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the vaccine to the nation on November 20.
analysis.summary_en: India has developed its first indigenous vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza, targeting the clade 2.3.2.1a strain, which has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. The vaccine, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, provides protection for up to six months and is suitable for layer and breeder chickens. This development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, where 35,647 birds had died as of November 13, and around 40,000 chickens were culled. Authorities have imposed movement restrictions and declared infected and surveillance zones. The H5N1 strain has also been detected in mammals and three human cases, with the World Health Organization reporting 1,003 human cases and 479 deaths globally since 2003. The vaccine is expected to enhance India’s preparedness for outbreaks, alongside existing measures such as surveillance, testing, biosecurity, and culling. The Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the vaccine to the nation on November 20.

news.source_body_en: India has developed its first indigenous vaccine against H5N1 avian influenza, targeting the clade 2.3.2.1a strain, which has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. The vaccine, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, provides protection for up to six months and is suitable for layer and breeder chickens. This development comes amid fresh bird flu outbreaks in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, where 35,647 birds had died as of November 13, and around 40,000 chickens were culled. Authorities have imposed movement restrictions and declared infected and surveillance zones. The H5N1 strain has also been detected in mammals and three human cases, with the World Health Organization reporting 1,003 human cases and 479 deaths globally since 2003. The vaccine is expected to enhance India’s preparedness for outbreaks, alongside existing measures such as surveillance, testing, biosecurity, and culling. The Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate the vaccine to the nation on November 20.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Ginsenoside Rg1 Adjuvant Boosts Immune Protection Against H9N2 Avian Influenza in Chickens by November 14, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Ginsenoside Rg1 Adjuvant Boosts Immune Protection Against H9N2 Avian Influenza in Chickens Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers investigating novel poultry immunization strategies have demonstrated that supplementing an inactivated H9N2 avian influenza vaccine with ginsenoside Rg1 substantially enhances immune responses and protective efficacy in young chickens. In a controlled trial conducted using one-day-old non-immunized Arbor Acres broiler chicks, administering ginsenoside Rg1 alongside the standard inactivated H9N2 vaccine generated significantly higher levels of specific immunoglobulins and hemagglutination inhibition titers compared to vaccination alone. Following an experimental intranasal viral challenge with live avian influenza, birds that received the adjuvant regimen exhibited marked reductions in oropharyngeal and cloacal viral shedding, alongside lower viral loads within critical respiratory and renal tissues. These findings indicate that ginsenoside Rg1 holds strong potential as an effective natural adjuvant for avian influenza vaccination programs. The global poultry sector faces persistent operational and economic setbacks driven by the continuous circulation of the H9N2 subtype, which represents the most widespread form of low pathogenic avian influenza found in domestic bird populations. More critically, ongoing genomic monitoring reveals that circulating H9N2 lineages continuously undergo antigenic variation and genetic reassortment within agricultural reservoirs. Through these evolutionary shifts, H9N2 strains frequently donate essential internal genetic segments to emerging highly pathogenic avian influenza variants, including lethal subtypes such as H5N1 and H7N9. This genetic exchange significantly amplifies the risk of interspecies transmission and poses ongoing zoonotic threats to human public health. To counteract widespread circulation, agricultural operations in numerous countries, including China, South Korea, and Egypt, routinely administer oil-adjuvanted inactivated vaccines to poultry flocks. Nevertheless, recurrent field outbreaks persist even among heavily vaccinated bird populations, exposing critical shortcomings in current immunization programs that largely stem from the limited antigenic breadth and suboptimal immunogenicity of existing formulations. Vaccine effectiveness depends fundamentally not only on target antigen selection but also on the pharmacological properties of the adjuvant used to stimulate the host immune system. While commercial animal vaccines commonly incorporate adjuvants such as Matrix-M, CpG1018, MF59, or traditional aluminum salts, these agents present notable practical limitations. Many conventional formulations fail to generate adequate cellular immune activation, carry potential risks of adverse reactions, or induce pronounced local tissue irritation at injection sites. These recognized biological drawbacks highlight an urgent need in veterinary medicine to identify safe, non-toxic adjuvants capable of enhancing cellular and humoral protection without compromising animal welfare. Discover more Check Symptoms Vaccine vaccine vaccines Find Vaccines In the search for safer alternatives, natural pharmacological compounds derived from traditional botanical medicine have attracted growing scientific attention due to their low intrinsic toxicity, high biocompatibility, and diverse immunomodulatory capabilities. Previous immunological studies have established that ginsenoside Rg1 possesses the capacity to stimulate balanced T helper type 1 and T helper type 2 immune responses in multiple animal species. Scientific literature has documented its adjuvant efficacy in experimental vaccination models against several major animal and human viral pathogens, including hepatitis B virus, infectious bursal disease virus, influenza, and porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus. However, despite these encouraging demonstrations in other disease contexts, the functional capacity of ginsenoside Rg1 to bolster protective immunity against avian H9N2 influenza in commercial poultry had remained entirely unexplored prior to this comprehensive study. To rigorously evaluate the adjuvant capabilities of the compound, the research team procured high-grade ginsenoside Rg1 possessing a verified chemical purity exceeding 98 percent from a specialized biochemical supplier in Chengdu, China. Recognizing that bacterial endotoxin contamination can confound immunological evaluations by introducing uncontrolled inflammatory artifacts, the investigators processed the saponin solution through a dedicated gel endotoxin-removal column, successfully verifying that residual endotoxin concentrations remained strictly below 0.5 endotoxin units per milliliter. The viral component utilized throughout the immunization and challenge trials was the low pathogenic avian influenza serotype strain designated A/Chicken/Jilin/DH109/2012, which was propagated and adapted in nine-day-old specific-pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs. Commercial inactivated H9N2 vaccines were acquired from Harbin Pharmaceutical Group Biological Vaccine Company. The experimental cohort comprised 150 one-day-old non-immunized Arbor Acres chicks obtained from a certified commercial hatchery, which were randomly divided into three identical treatment groups of 50 chicks each to establish rigorous comparative baselines under approved institutional animal care protocols. Discover more Book Acupuncture Identify Plants Try Herbs The experimental protocol evaluated three distinct cohorts: an unadjuvanted vaccine group, an Rg1-supplemented vaccine group, and an unvaccinated control group receiving sterile phosphate-buffered saline. Birds in both vaccinated groups were administered 200 microliters of the inactivated H9N2 vaccine by intramuscular injection on three occasions spaced exactly two weeks apart, on days 0, 14, and 28. Concurrently with the initial immunization, the adjuvant group received ginsenoside Rg1 dissolved in drinking water at a calculated dosage of 1 milligram per kilogram of body weight daily for seven consecutive days. Within each 50-bird group, specific biological replicates were systematically assigned to pre-planned investigative endpoints: ten live chickens were monitored longitudinally for blood serum antibodies and mucosal swabs; 18 were sampled across scheduled intervals for splenic lymphocyte proliferation assays; five were evaluated for immune organ weights; five underwent hepatic and renal histopathological examination; nine were assessed for organ viral loads; and 13 were observed continuously for clinical health signs, body weight development, and survival. Humoral immune responses were tracked by collecting serum samples on days 14, 28, and 42 following the initial vaccination to measure specific immunoglobulin G concentrations and hemagglutination inhibition titers. Enzymatic analysis revealed that while the standard vaccine induced detectable antibodies above control levels, the addition of ginsenoside Rg1 produced a marked enhancement in antibody production. By days 28 and 42, specific serum immunoglobulin G levels were significantly elevated in the Rg1 combination group relative to birds receiving the unadjuvanted vaccine (p < 0.05). Furthermore, hemagglutination inhibition titers in the adjuvant group displayed a sustained, statistically significant rise throughout the 42-day observation window. Because a hemagglutination inhibition titer of at least 4 log2 is widely recognized as the definitive benchmark required for neutralizing viral particles, preventing hemagglutinin-receptor binding, and blocking viral transmission, the robust titers achieved in the Rg1 cohort underscore the compound’s capacity to amplify protective neutralizing antibody synthesis. Beyond antibody production, the researchers assessed cell-mediated immunity, which plays a pivotal role in clearing intracellular viral infections and establishing durable immunological memory. Splenic lymphocytes harvested on days 14, 28, and 42 post-immunization were tested using Cell Counting Kit-8 colorimetric assays to evaluate proliferation dynamics. At days 28 and 42, lymphocytes isolated from chicks receiving ginsenoside Rg1 exhibited significantly higher proliferative responses compared to the vaccine-only group (p < 0.05). Complementary multi-parameter flow cytometry revealed that the proportions of both CD3+CD4+ helper T cells and CD3+CD8+ cytotoxic T cells were markedly expanded in the Rg1 group relative to controls. In parallel, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays showed that the adjuvant regimen significantly enhanced serum concentrations of key regulatory cytokines, including interferon-gamma, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-4, and interleukin-6. This coordinated upregulation demonstrates that ginsenoside Rg1 simultaneously potentiates cytotoxic CD8+ cellular effector pathways and promotes Th2-associated cytokine production responsible for directing optimal B-cell maturation. The investigation also confirmed that ginsenoside Rg1 supplementation supported healthy lymphoid organ development without inducing systemic organ toxicity. On day 28 post-inoculation, chickens in the adjuvant cohort exhibited significantly increased weight indices for the spleen, thymus, and bursa of Fabricius compared to those receiving vaccine alone. Biochemical screening of serum alkaline phosphatase and lactate dehydrogenase revealed no abnormal deviations, while histopathological examination of liver and kidney sections demonstrated normal tissue architecture without pathological lesions across all vaccinated groups. Fourteen days following the final immunization, birds were challenged intranasally with 100 microliters containing 10^7 median egg infectious doses of the live H9N2 strain. Swab sampling assessed by quantitative real-time PCR revealed that while unvaccinated controls exhibited 90 percent shedding rates at day 14 and vaccine-only birds shed virus through day 10, the Rg1 group completely cleared oropharyngeal and cloacal shedding by day 10. Moreover, tissue viral load assessments confirmed that live virus was undetectable in the lungs and kidneys of Rg1-treated chickens by day 10 post-challenge. In evaluating the overall outcomes, the authors noted that combining oral ginsenoside Rg1 with an inactivated H9N2 vaccine successfully stimulated both branches of the avian adaptive immune system, resulting in accelerated viral clearance and superior tissue protection. The botanical adjuvant enhanced the production of protective neutralizing antibodies, expanded functional T-cell subsets, and bolstered key cytokine networks while maintaining an excellent biosafety profile. Nonetheless, the researchers explicitly acknowledged two important methodological limitations in their experimental design. First, the toxicological screening was restricted to targeted liver and kidney biochemistry and histopathology, rather than an exhaustive safety assessment adhering strictly to international World Health Organization or European Medicines Agency regulatory standards. Second, the study did not incorporate an isolated control cohort receiving ginsenoside Rg1 monotherapy without vaccination, precluding direct observation of the adjuvant’s baseline physiological effects in unimmunized animals. Nevertheless, recurrent field outbreaks persist even among heavily vaccinated bird populations, exposing critical shortcomings in current immunization programs that largely stem from the limited antigenic breadth and suboptimal immunogenicity of existing formulations. Vaccine effectiveness depends fundamentally not only on target antigen selection but also on the pharmacological properties of the adjuvant used to stimulate the host immune system. While commercial animal vaccines commonly incorporate adjuvants such as Matrix-M, CpG1018, MF59, or traditional aluminum salts, these agents present notable practical limitations. Many conventional formulations fail to generate adequate cellular immune activation, carry potential risks of adverse reactions, or induce pronounced local tissue irritation at injection sites. These recognized biological drawbacks highlight an urgent need in veterinary medicine to identify safe, non-toxic adjuvants capable of enhancing cellular and humoral protection without compromising animal welfare. Discover more Check Symptoms Vaccine vaccine vaccines Find Vaccines In the search for safer alternatives, natural pharmacological compounds derived from traditional botanical medicine have attracted growing scientific attention due to their low intrinsic toxicity, high biocompatibility, and diverse immunomodulatory capabilities. Previous immunological studies have established that ginsenoside Rg1 possesses the capacity to stimulate balanced T helper type 1 and T helper type 2 immune responses in multiple animal species. Scientific literature has documented its adjuvant efficacy in experimental vaccination models against several major animal and human viral pathogens, including hepatitis B virus, infectious bursal disease virus, influenza, and porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus. However, despite these encouraging demonstrations in other disease contexts, the functional capacity of ginsenoside Rg1 to bolster protective immunity against avian H9N2 influenza in commercial poultry had remained entirely unexplored prior to this comprehensive study. To rigorously evaluate the adjuvant capabilities of the compound, the research team procured high-grade ginsenoside Rg1 possessing a verified chemical purity exceeding 98 percent from a specialized biochemical supplier in Chengdu, China. Recognizing that bacterial endotoxin contamination can confound immunological evaluations by introducing uncontrolled inflammatory artifacts, the investigators processed the saponin solution through a dedicated gel endotoxin-removal column, successfully verifying that residual endotoxin concentrations remained strictly below 0.5 endotoxin units per milliliter. The viral component utilized throughout the immunization and challenge trials was the low pathogenic avian influenza serotype strain designated A/Chicken/Jilin/DH109/2012, which was propagated and adapted in nine-day-old specific-pathogen-free embryonated chicken eggs. Commercial inactivated H9N2 vaccines were acquired from Harbin Pharmaceutical Group Biological Vaccine Company. The experimental cohort comprised 150 one-day-old non-immunized Arbor Acres chicks obtained from a certified commercial hatchery, which were randomly divided into three identical treatment groups of 50 chicks each to establish rigorous comparative baselines under approved institutional animal care protocols. Discover more Book Acupuncture Identify Plants Try Herbs The experimental protocol evaluated three distinct cohorts: an unadjuvanted vaccine group, an Rg1-supplemented vaccine group, and an unvaccinated control group receiving sterile phosphate-buffered saline. Birds in both vaccinated groups were administered 200 microliters of the inactivated H9N2 vaccine by intramuscular injection on three occasions spaced exactly two weeks apart, on days 0, 14, and 28. Concurrently with the initial immunization, the adjuvant group received ginsenoside Rg1 dissolved in drinking water at a calculated dosage of 1 milligram per kilogram of body weight daily for seven consecutive days. Within each 50-bird group, specific biological replicates were systematically assigned to pre-planned investigative endpoints: ten live chickens were monitored longitudinally for blood serum antibodies and mucosal swabs; 18 were sampled across scheduled intervals for splenic lymphocyte proliferation assays; five were evaluated for immune organ weights; five underwent hepatic and renal histopathological examination; nine were assessed for organ viral loads; and 13 were observed continuously for clinical health signs, body weight development, and survival. Humoral immune responses were tracked by collecting serum samples on days 14, 28, and 42 following the initial vaccination to measure specific immunoglobulin G concentrations and hemagglutination inhibition titers. Enzymatic analysis revealed that while the standard vaccine induced detectable antibodies above control levels, the addition of ginsenoside Rg1 produced a marked enhancement in antibody production. By days 28 and 42, specific serum immunoglobulin G levels were significantly elevated in the Rg1 combination group relative to birds receiving the unadjuvanted vaccine (p < 0.05). Furthermore, hemagglutination inhibition titers in the adjuvant group displayed a sustained, statistically significant rise throughout the 42-day observation window. Because a hemagglutination inhibition titer of at least 4 log2 is widely recognized as the definitive benchmark required for neutralizing viral particles, preventing hemagglutinin-receptor binding, and blocking viral transmission, the robust titers achieved in the Rg1 cohort underscore the compound’s capacity to amplify protective neutralizing antibody synthesis. Beyond antibody production, the researchers assessed cell-mediated immunity, which plays a pivotal role in clearing intracellular viral infections and establishing durable immunological memory. Splenic lymphocytes harvested on days 14, 28, and 42 post-immunization were tested using Cell Counting Kit-8 colorimetric assays to evaluate proliferation dynamics. At days 28 and 42, lymphocytes isolated from chicks receiving ginsenoside Rg1 exhibited significantly higher proliferative responses compared to the vaccine-only group (p < 0.05). Complementary multi-parameter flow cytometry revealed that the proportions of both CD3+CD4+ helper T cells and CD3+CD8+ cytotoxic T cells were markedly expanded in the Rg1 group relative to controls. In parallel, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays showed that the adjuvant regimen significantly enhanced serum concentrations of key regulatory cytokines, including interferon-gamma, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-4, and interleukin-6. This coordinated upregulation demonstrates that ginsenoside Rg1 simultaneously potentiates cytotoxic CD8+ cellular effector pathways and promotes Th2-associated cytokine production responsible for directing optimal B-cell maturation. The investigation also confirmed that ginsenoside Rg1 supplementation supported healthy lymphoid organ development without inducing systemic organ toxicity. On day 28 post-inoculation, chickens in the adjuvant cohort exhibited significantly increased weight indices for the spleen, thymus, and bursa of Fabricius compared to those receiving vaccine alone. Biochemical screening of serum alkaline phosphatase and lactate dehydrogenase revealed no abnormal deviations, while histopathological examination of liver and kidney sections demonstrated normal tissue architecture without pathological lesions across all vaccinated groups. Fourteen days following the final immunization, birds were challenged intranasally with 100 microliters containing 10^7 median egg infectious doses of the live H9N2 strain. Swab sampling assessed by quantitative real-time PCR revealed that while unvaccinated controls exhibited 90 percent shedding rates at day 14 and vaccine-only birds shed virus through day 10, the Rg1 group completely cleared oropharyngeal and cloacal shedding by day 10. Moreover, tissue viral load assessments confirmed that live virus was undetectable in the lungs and kidneys of Rg1-treated chickens by day 10 post-challenge. In evaluating the overall outcomes, the authors noted that combining oral ginsenoside Rg1 with an inactivated H9N2 vaccine successfully stimulated both branches of the avian adaptive immune system, resulting in accelerated viral clearance and superior tissue protection. The botanical adjuvant enhanced the production of protective neutralizing antibodies, expanded functional T-cell subsets, and bolstered key cytokine networks while maintaining an excellent biosafety profile. Nonetheless, the researchers explicitly acknowledged two important methodological limitations in their experimental design. First, the toxicological screening was restricted to targeted liver and kidney biochemistry and histopathology, rather than an exhaustive safety assessment adhering strictly to international World Health Organization or European Medicines Agency regulatory standards. Second, the study did not incorporate an isolated control cohort receiving ginsenoside Rg1 monotherapy without vaccination, precluding direct observation of the adjuvant’s baseline physiological effects in unimmunized animals. news.content_title: India develops first home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens
news.content: India India develops first home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens This results in substantial financial losses for poultry farmers due to large-scale culling of birds and trade restrictions. NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough after years of research and trials, India is set to launch its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, raising hopes within the poultry industry of preventing recurring bird flu outbreaks. The vaccine, based on indigenously developed technology, is an Inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) formulation that protects against the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus strain circulating in the country. Of late, this dangerous strain has also spilled over in various animal species, including mammals, along with three recent human cases. Between 2006 and 2021, India experienced 341 outbreaks of bird flu across 24 states. Of these, 284 cases were attributed to the H5N1 virus and 57 to H5N8. While there is a vaccine available for lower-risk pathogens, there is currently no specific vaccine against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. The vaccine was developed by scientists at the Indian Council for Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal. “This marks a major milestone in safeguarding poultry health, strengthening farm resilience, and advancing Atmanirbharta (self-reliance) in veterinary biologicals,” Aniket Sanyal, Director of ICAR-NIHSAD, told this daily. The development of this vaccine represents a significant achievement for Indian science in combating Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu. HPAI is a severe disease, and outbreaks can lead to nearly 100% mortality among infected birds. This results in substantial financial losses for poultry farmers due to large-scale culling of birds and trade restrictions. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also disrupt global trade, inflate prices of poultry products, and threaten the livelihoods of farmers. PAI has a near 100% mortality among infected birds. A significant outbreak of bird flu could reduce India’s GDP growth by up to 1.5%, with more than 20% of the country’s poultry population at risk if the disease spreads unchecked. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses between Rs 2,200 crore and Rs 3,000 crore

selected_identity.page_title: India develops first home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens

news.content_original: India India develops first home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens This results in substantial financial losses for poultry farmers due to large-scale culling of birds and trade restrictions. NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough after years of research and trials, India is set to launch its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, raising hopes within the poultry industry of preventing recurring bird flu outbreaks. The vaccine, based on indigenously developed technology, is an Inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) formulation that protects against the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus strain circulating in the country. Of late, this dangerous strain has also spilled over in various animal species, including mammals, along with three recent human cases. Between 2006 and 2021, India experienced 341 outbreaks of bird flu across 24 states. Of these, 284 cases were attributed to the H5N1 virus and 57 to H5N8. While there is a vaccine available for lower-risk pathogens, there is currently no specific vaccine against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. The vaccine was developed by scientists at the Indian Council for Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal. “This marks a major milestone in safeguarding poultry health, strengthening farm resilience, and advancing Atmanirbharta (self-reliance) in veterinary biologicals,” Aniket Sanyal, Director of ICAR-NIHSAD, told this daily. The development of this vaccine represents a significant achievement for Indian science in combating Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu. HPAI is a severe disease, and outbreaks can lead to nearly 100% mortality among infected birds. This results in substantial financial losses for poultry farmers due to large-scale culling of birds and trade restrictions. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also disrupt global trade, inflate prices of poultry products, and threaten the livelihoods of farmers. PAI has a near 100% mortality among infected birds. A significant outbreak of bird flu could reduce India’s GDP growth by up to 1.5%, with more than 20% of the country’s poultry population at risk if the disease spreads unchecked. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses between Rs 2,200 crore and Rs 3,000 crore

12:39 PM | Updated On 19 Nov 2026 12:39 PM Overview India is preparing to launch its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, developed by scientists at the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal. The inactivated vaccine targets the highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus, Clade 2.3.2.1a, circulating in the country. Between 2006 and 2021, India recorded 341 bird flu outbreaks across 24 states, including 284 caused by H5N1 and 57 by H5N8. The vaccine is expected to strengthen poultry disease prevention and reduce the economic burden of recurring outbreaks. Highly pathogenic avian influenza can cause mortality approaching 100% among infected poultry, resulting in large-scale culling, trade restrictions and substantial financial losses. The 2006 outbreak alone reportedly caused losses estimated between Rs 2,200 crore and Rs 3,000 crore. ICAR-NIHSAD Director Aniket Sanyal described the development as an important milestone in strengthening poultry health and India's self-reliance in veterinary vaccines. The vaccine is intended for poultry, not human use, according to the New Indian Express report. news.content: BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat England Regions Lincolnshire Restrictions in place after another bird flu case Image caption, Birds at the site near Coningsby will be humanely killed, Defra says ByStuart Harratt East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire Published 19 November 2026 Another case of bird flu has been confirmed in Lincolnshire. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said an outbreak of the avian influenza H5N1 was found in commercial poultry near Coningsby in East Lindsey. A 1.9 miles (3km) protection zone and 6.2 miles (10km) surveillance zone have been declared around the site and all birds will be humanely culled, Defra said. It is the fourth outbreak reported in East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire this month, with cases reported in the Brigg, Pocklington and Market Rasen areas. Last week, the UK's Chief Veterinary Officer introduced a national order directing all poultry owners with more than 50 birds to ensure they are housed indoors. Bird flu, also known as avian influenza, is an infectious disease affecting birds and can be spread through saliva, faeces or contaminated environments. news.content_original: BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat England Regions Lincolnshire Restrictions in place after another bird flu case Image caption, Birds at the site near Coningsby will be humanely killed, Defra says ByStuart Harratt East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire Published 19 November 2026 Another case of bird flu has been confirmed in Lincolnshire. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said an outbreak of the avian influenza H5N1 was found in commercial poultry near Coningsby in East Lindsey. A 1.9 miles (3km) protection zone and 6.2 miles (10km) surveillance zone have been declared around the site and all birds will be humanely culled, Defra said. It is the fourth outbreak reported in East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire this month, with cases reported in the Brigg, Pocklington and Market Rasen areas. Last week, the UK's Chief Veterinary Officer introduced a national order directing all poultry owners with more than 50 birds to ensure they are housed indoors. Bird flu, also known as avian influenza, is an infectious disease affecting birds and can be spread through saliva, faeces or contaminated environments. news.excerpt: A person in Oregon was diagnosed with highly pathogenic avian influenza Nov. 19, marking the state's first human case in 2026.

news.content_title: Human contracts bird flu at Morrow County dairy farm in Oregon
news.content: The Oregon Health Authority on Nov. 19 confirmed the state's first human case this year of highly pathogenic avian influenza linked to a cattle outbreak at a Morrow County dairy farm. The person was treated with an antiviral medicine, oseltamivir, after they developed mild symptoms of HPAI, OHA said in a news release. They were not hospitalized. The virus is not known to spread from human to human. The risk to the public is "extremely low," OHA said. Epidemiologists at OHA received confirmation of the case from the Oregon State Public Health Laboratory on Nov. 18. Oregon public health officials monitored more than 300 people exposed to sick animals since 2022, including one human case of bird flu identified in 2024 in connection with a commercial poultry outbreak, OHA said. Epidemiologists are working with the Oregon Department of Agriculture, which provides personal protection equipment and training to the affected farm workers, and Morrow County Public Health, who are monitoring those exposed to the virus, OHA said. Public health officials offered oseltamivir to those in the person's household out of caution, OHA said. "This is not cause for alarm. Rather, it is evidence that the surveillance and response system we have in place is working," Melissa Sutton, medical director for respiratory viral pathogens at OHA, said. "Our goal is to ensure that all symptomatic farm workers receive prompt testing and treatment to prevent severe disease." The seasonal flu vaccine does not protect against HPAI. Getting the vaccine can help reduce the risk of getting sick with human influenza viruses, which can reduce the risk of coinfection with both human and seasonal virus and an avian virus, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. news.title_zh: 俄勒冈州确认今年首例人感染禽流感病例
news.source_body_en: Oregon has confirmed its first human case of bird flu this year, linked to an outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in dairy cattle at a Morrow County farm. The affected individual, who has not been identified, developed mild symptoms and was treated promptly, with members of their household also receiving precautionary treatment. No hospitalizations were required, and the risk to the public is described as "extremely low" by Oregon Health Authority officials. There have been no cases of human-to-human transmission, and pasteurized milk and dairy products remain safe for consumption. The confirmation highlights the effectiveness of the surveillance system, though the exact connection between the case and the HPAI outbreak is still under investigation. Officials emphasize the importance of monitoring and treating symptomatic farm workers to prevent severe disease.

Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search Support Menu New case of H9N2 reported in China as more US dairy herds hit with avian flu News brief November 18, 2026 Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) Share Capturas E / iStock China has reported a new case of H9N2 avian flu to the World Health Organization (WHO) in the Western Pacific Region. The patient is a child in Hunan province who was exposed to the virus via backyard poultry. The child has recovered. Since 2015, a total of 190 human infections with H9N2 avian flu, including two deaths (both in people with underlying conditions), have been reported to the WHO in the Western Pacific. Of these, 187 were in China, two in Cambodia, and one in Vietnam, the WHO said. More US cows affected In US avian flu news, dairy herds in Oklahoma and Oregon were hit with the virus this past week. Washington state still has the most recent activity, with 35 of the 46 detections noted in the past 30 days by the US Department of Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Infection Service (APHIS). In Worcester County, Maryland, 218,400 birds were hit at a commercial broiler producer this week, APHIS noted. In the past 30 days, avian flu has been confirmed in 35 flocks, including 14 commercial flocks and 21 backyard flocks. A total of 2.96 million birds have been affected by avian flu in that span. WHO: Ebola case count has more than doubled in 3 months News brief November 18, 2026 Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Ebola WHO / Christopher Black Ebola cases have more than doubled in 3 months, according to the director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO), Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, PhD. As of today, 11,536 confirmed Ebola cases, including 5,635 confirmed deaths, have been reported since the outbreak was declared on May 15. In opening remarks to the third meeting of the WHO’s emergency committee on the Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic, Tedros said the DRC is still seeing 400 to 500 new cases each week. Children in particular are “paying a terrible price” for the uncontrolled outbreak, which is now entering its seventh month. Children have accounted for roughly 30% of all deaths in this outbreak. More Ebola laboratories open Some progress has been made, Tedros said, but it has been uneven. “At the start of the outbreak, two laboratories could test for the virus. Today there are more than two dozen. Close to 2,000 treatment beds are now available, and about 3,000 people have recovered,” he said. Tedros also said 900 people in the DRC are now enrolled in clinical trials of therapeutics, including a vaccine trial using Ervebo, the Ebola vaccine approved for the Zaire strain of the virus. And Tedros said two candidate vaccines developed specifically against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus will be added to an ongoing vaccine trial in the coming weeks. White House pulls Heidi Overton’s nomination for FDA chief News brief November 18, 2026 Liz Szabo, MA Topics Public Health Heidi Overton, MD, watches President Trump sign an executive order calling for children to be vaccinated against fewer diseases. Credit: The White House The White House has withdrawn the nomination of Heidi Overton, MD, one of President Trump’s senior domestic policy advisers, for commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Sen. Bill Cassidy, MD, a Louisiana Republican, wrote on X last night that he was disappointed in that decision. A Senate health committee was scheduled to vote on her nomination today. “The White House abandoned a viable confirmation path for Dr. Overton,” wrote Cassidy, who will leave the Senate after losing the Republican primary last spring. The White House “said that this was because she did not have the votes to pass,” Cassidy wrote. “This was odd as I was having productive conversations with members. I believe she would have had the votes to pass out of committee and pass the full Senate. My conversations with her convinced me she would follow the science and push back against decisions that put Americans’ health at risk.” Kyle Diamantas, JD, has been serving as the acting FDA commissioner since early May, when Marty Makary, MD, MPH, resigned from the position. Makary served in the role for just over a year. Opposition from abortion opponents, MAHA leaders In his post, Cassidy said that some senators wanted the White House to commit more strongly to anti-abortion policies. “Pro-life Senators sought final assurances from the Administration regarding the Administration’s commitment to life issues,” Cassidy wrote. “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments. Unfortunately, with the limited time left, confirming a permanent FDA Commissioner will fall to Senate Democrats.” Some leaders of the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, which includes critics of childhood vaccinations and chemical additives in food, have been critical of Overton. In a post on X, the advocacy group MAHA Action wrote, “The White House clearly recognizes that we have a once in a lifetime opportunity to change the D.C. status quo, and that the next FDA commissioner must be aligned with the MAHA agenda.” In case you missed it Previous Next Study suggests screening for chlamydia, gonorrhea increases with electronic intervention Policy changes in Listen (2 mins) Save Share Largest US egg producer to cull 1.8 million birds after bird flu outbreak on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google The largest egg producer in the US will cull 2.7 percent of its flock [File: Jeenah Moon/Reuters] By Andy Hirschfeld Published On 18 Nov 202618 Nov 2026 Cal-Maine Foods, the largest egg producer in the United States, has said it would cull 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its facilities in Florida. On Wednesday, the company said the 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 young hens being culled account for 2.7 percent of its flock. Production at the facility will be temporarily halted. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom list 2 of 4US urges China to honour Busan trade deal commitments list 3 of 4Australia warns H5N1 likely to spread after first mass mortality episode list 4 of 4Australia pledges action on H5N1 after bird flu case confirmed end of list Cal-Maine said in a statement that it would coordinate with other production and distribution facilities to minimise disruption across the company. The risk bird flu poses to human health is low. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), there have been 74 human cases since February 2024, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission. However, the virus continues to pose a significant challenge to the US poultry and egg industries. Some 21.5 million birds have been affected this year, following a historic surge in outbreaks in late 2024 and early 2025 that sharply reduced the number of egg-laying hens. Approximately 50.7 million laying hens were lost between mid-October 2024 and early March 2025, when egg prices in the US reached a record high of $6.23 per dozen. The current average retail price of eggs is $2.32 per dozen, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Despite the announcement that production at the Florida facility would be temporarily halted, Cal-Maine’s stock rose 5.3 percent in early trading. 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Advertisement Your browser does not support the audio element

news.source_body_en: Cal-Maine Foods, the largest US egg producer, has announced the culling of 1.8 million birds following the detection of avian influenza at its Florida facility. This action accounts for 2.7 percent of its total flock. The company stated that production at the affected site will be temporarily halted, and it will coordinate with other facilities to minimize disruption. The CDC notes that there have been 74 human cases of avian influenza since February 2024, but no evidence of human-to-human transmission, indicating a low risk to human health. The outbreak has caused significant challenges for the US poultry and egg industries, with 21.5 million birds affected this year. Despite the culling, Cal-Maine's stock rose 5.3 percent in early trading, suggesting market confidence. The decision to cull is based on confirmed avian influenza detection, and the company is taking measures to manage the impact on its operations.

news.content: Direct access to content Direct access to research Direct access to menu Menu Search en fr es Codes and Manuals Publications Documentary Portal Training Platform ANIMUSE TRUVET PVSIS WildEpi The Animal Echo Bookshop Cart My account en fr es The State of the World’s Animal Health Animal Diseases Antimicrobial resistance Search Who we areToggle submenu Back to menu Who we are We are the global authority on animal health. Founded in 1924 as the Office International des Epizooties (OIE), in May 2003 we adopted the common name World Organisation for Animal Health. An intergovernmental organisation, we focus on transparently disseminating information on animal diseases, improving animal health globally and thus build a safer, healthier and more sustainable world Mission Advocacy Strategy Structure and GovernanceToggle submenu Back to menu World Assembly Council Director General Governance Review Committee Organisation’s Framework Members How WOAH is funded What we doToggle submenu Back to menu What we do We work to improve animal health and welfare across the globe. By collecting, analysing and disseminating veterinary scientific information, we encourage international solidarity in the control of animal health risks. Furthermore, we work across borders to foster a One Health approach, recognising that the health of animals, humans and the environment are interdependent. Animal Health and WelfareToggle submenu Back to menu Animal Diseases Disease Data Collection Animal Welfare Wildlife Health Official Disease Status StandardsToggle submenu Back to menu Codes and Manuals Standard-Setting Process Observatory Global InitiativesToggle submenu Back to menu Disease Eradication Antimicrobial resistance One Health Biological threat reduction Food Safety Publications What we offerToggle submenu Back to menu What we offer We oversee various programmes, both cross-sectoral ones and those focused on specific needs, to improve the capacities of Veterinary Services and Aquatic Animal Health Services. These programmes are designed to empower and guide countries in the development and implementation of sustainable national plans which go well beyond purely veterinary matters. World AMR Awareness Week 2026: “One Health, One action: Prevent AMR now” Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites no longer respond to medicines used to treat the infections they cause. AMR is no longer a future challenge; it is a global threat. Held every 18 to 24 November, World AMR Awareness Week raises awareness and understanding of AMR and promotes global action to help prevent the spread of drug-resistant infections. Nipah and Hendra virus diseases Working across borders to foster a One Health approach to global health. The health of animals and the environment strongly depend on human activities. See more One Health The “One Health” approach summarises a concept that has been known for more than a century; that human, animal and plant health are interdependent and bound to the health of the ecosystems in which they exist. We envisage and implement it as a collaborative, whole of society, whole of government approach to understanding, anticipating and addressing risks to global health. Founded in 1924 as the Office International des Epizooties (OIE), in May 2003 we adopted the common name World Organisation for Animal Health. analysis.brief_en: The World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) has issued a call for heightened vigilance as reported avian influenza outbreaks increase globally. Published on November 16, 2026, this statement highlights the growing concern over avian influenza A viruses and their potential impact on animal health and welfare. WOAH emphasizes the importance of international collaboration and a One Health approach, which recognizes the interconnectedness of animal, human, and environmental health. The organization is actively involved in collecting, analyzing, and disseminating veterinary scientific information to encourage global solidarity in managing animal health risks. While the specific scale and impact of the outbreaks are not detailed in the evidence, WOAH's focus on transparency and trust aims to improve acceptance of disease zones by trade partners. The statement underscores the need for continued efforts in disease surveillance, prevention, and control to address the challenges posed by avian influenza.

H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Veterinary Research 3.8 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 中国河南家禽来源H9N2来源NA及内部基因H6N2新型禽流感重排病毒的表征与疫苗诱导免疫 2025年12月,研究人员从中国河南省一次造成15%田间死亡率并伴随严重呼吸道疾病的鸡群疫情中分离到一株H6N2禽流感(AIV)病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04)。全基因组测序证实该病毒为新型重排体,其携带水禽源H6亚型血凝素(HA, hemagglutinin)基因、H9N2亚型神经氨酸酶(NA, neuraminidase)基因以及H9N2 G57基因型的完整内部基因盒(internal-gene cassette)。尽管NL04在实验感染无特定病原体(SPF, specific-pathogen-free)鸡后仅引起轻度临床症状并表现出100%存活率,但研究人员观察到其呼吸道组织存在显著的组织病理学损伤,揭示了实验室结局与田间严重报告的死亡率之间存在明显的表型差异,而这种差异可能由商业化农场的复杂风险因素所驱动。SPF鸡的组织病毒载量在鼻甲(nasal turbinates)和哈德氏腺(Harderian I(ST339-like),NA基因属于H9N2 Y280-like lineage,六个内部基因均来源于鸡源H9N2 G57基因型,证实为完整种间重排事件。尽管PB2和M基因的最近缘序列在基本局部比对搜索工具(BLAST, Basic Local Alignment Search Tool)中来自H3N3/H3N8病毒,但系统进化树将其归入H9N2 G57-like lineage。病毒滴度达107.78 EID 50 /0.1 mL。 Molecular characteristics NL04的HA裂解位点为PQIETR↓G,无连续碱性氨基酸,未检测到Q226L和G228S。NA stalk区缺失并检测到K368N。PB2携带A588V、T598I和A676T;PB1的I368V与雪貂传播性相关;PA的K356R与哺乳动物复制及致病性增加有关;M1中T215A为物种特异性标志,N30D与毒力增强有关;M2的S31N赋予金刚烷胺(amantadine)耐药性;NS1携带P42S、E172K、N205S和P212S。 Study in SPF chicken 以106.00 mL。体外复制显示,NL04在MDCK和CEF细胞中有效增殖,CEF细胞在12至48小时支持更高产量,峰值分别出现在36至48小时和60小时。 Temporal trends, host range, and subtype diversity of H6Ny viruses 基于GISAID数据库5029条H6Ny序列(1963–2025),H6Ny病毒于1990年代末急剧上升,2014年达约440株峰值。禽类占91.7%,环境样本占6.4%,哺乳动物与人极为罕见。H6N2占30.98%,H6N6占28.08%。H6N2已显著溢出到家鸡(145株)。 Discussion 研究人员指出,NL04的重排模式有别于既往仅获得单一H9N2片段的H6N2病毒,其HA、NA及内部基因的差异提示H6与H9N2已发生深度基因交流。H9N2内部基因骨架可能通过改善聚合酶功能兼容性提高禽类复制效率,解释了NL04在鸡胚和CEF中的高滴度增殖,并提示其可作为疫苗候选种子病毒。SPF鸡实验显示,大体病变缺失并不等同于组织损伤轻微,病理检查更为敏感。NL04在SPF鸡中的轻度表型与商业鸡群15%死亡率差异显著,商业化环境中的高密度饲养应激及大肠杆菌(Escherichia coli)、支原体(Mycoplasma)等继发感染可能是田间严重表现的重要原因,凸显了SPF模型推演至真实农场的固有局限。疫苗方面,免疫鸡高HI抗体水平可能归因于H9N2内部基因盒的高抗原载荷及水禽源HA的强免疫原性;免疫鸡攻毒后排毒期缩短,血清可中和异源H6N1毒株,表明疫苗可诱导交叉中和活性,但攻毒后组织指标未测定。小鼠模型中NL04复制有限,提示哺乳动物适应潜力低,虽携带PB2-V588、PA-R356及NA stalk缺失等非典型替换,但在NL04背景下尚不足以赋予robust的哺乳动物复制,实际功能有待反向遗传学验证。全球数据表明H6人感染极为罕见,当前条件下NL04的人畜共患溢出风险较低。研究人员总结认为,该病毒成功建立提示多种A型流感病毒共循环,H6重排病毒的临床影响可能被H9N2地方流行所掩盖,但频繁重排强化了对水禽、野鸟及商业家禽开展增强型纵向监测的价值。 Limitations 未开展体外受体结合实验;未包含气溶胶(aerosol)传播实验;仅依赖单一分离株;未在商业化鸡群中攻毒;未测定肠道病毒滴度。 Conclusions NL04为新型重排病毒,其特征为水禽源H6 HA、H9N2 Y280-like with H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Veterinary Research 3.8 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 中国河南家禽来源H9N2来源NA及内部基因H6N2新型禽流感重排病毒的表征与疫苗诱导免疫 2025年12月,研究人员从中国河南省一次造成15%田间死亡率并伴随严重呼吸道疾病的鸡群疫情中分离到一株H6N2禽流感(AIV)病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04)。全基因组测序证实该病毒为新型重排体,其携带水禽源H6亚型血凝素(HA, hemagglutinin)基因、H9N2亚型神经氨酸酶(NA, neuraminidase)基因以及H9N2 G57基因型的完整内部基因盒(internal-gene cassette)。尽管NL04在实验感染无特定病原体(SPF, specific-pathogen-free)鸡后仅引起轻度临床症状并表现出100%存活率,但研究人员观察到其呼吸道组织存在显著的组织病理学损伤,揭示了实验室结局与田间严重报告的死亡率之间存在明显的表型差异,而这种差异可能由商业化农场的复杂风险因素所驱动。SPF鸡的组织病毒载量在鼻甲(nasal turbinates)和哈德氏腺(Harderian gland)中达到峰值,证实该病毒具有显著的呼吸道嗜性。在BALB/c小鼠中,NL04表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明其哺乳动物适应(mammalian-adaptation)潜力较低。研究人员进一步评估了以NL04为基础的灭活疫苗候选株。该疫苗诱导了强效的体液免疫(humoral immunity),在减少同源攻毒(homologous challenge)后病毒排毒方面表现出效果,并可诱导针对异源H6N1分离株的交叉中和抗体(cross-neutralizing antibodies)。研究结果凸显了这一独特H6N2重排体的兽医意义,并强调了对家禽开展持续基因组监测(genomic surveillance)的价值,以防范新出现的禽流感威胁。 禽流感病毒(AIV, avian influenza virus)是对全球家禽产业的重大威胁。低致病性禽流感(LPAIV, low-pathogenic avian influenza virus)H6亚型自1965年分离以来,已在欧亚大陆广泛循环,尤其在中国水禽、鸡及活禽市场流行。尽管H6在实验感染禽类中常仅引起轻微疾病,但田间感染常伴随产蛋下降、生长减缓及继发细菌易感性升高。H9N2亚型在中国呈地方性流行,是H7N9、H3N8等人畜共患病毒内部基因盒的重要供体。在中国鸡场中,H6与H9N2频繁共循环,为重排创造了条件。获得H9N2内部基因的重排H6病毒值得特别关注。基于此,研究人员从河南鸡群中分离并表征一株H6N2禽流感重排病毒,系统评估其基因特征、致病性、组织嗜性及疫苗免疫效力,以支撑监测与防控策略制定。 义翘神州通用型Whitlow 218 Linker兔单抗,高效助力CAR流式检测,欢迎索取详细资料>> 领 取 2025年12月,研究人员从中国河南省商丘市某54周龄鸡群中分离到一株H6N2禽流感病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04),鸡群死亡率达15%。通过全基因组测序、细胞感染、SPF鸡与BALB/c小鼠实验、组织病理学、免疫组织化学及疫苗评价等技术,系统评估了病毒的遗传演化、复制特性、宿主嗜性与免疫原性。核心结论如下:NL04为新型重排病毒,HA来源于水禽源H6 ST339-like谱系(group I),NA来源于H9N2 Y280-like谱系,六个内部基因全部来源于鸡源H9N2 G57基因型。在SPF鸡中,NL04呈低致病性,100%存活,但可引起严重呼吸道组织病理学损伤,病毒在鼻甲与哈德氏腺(Harderian gland)高效复制,呈显著呼吸道嗜性。在BALB/c小鼠中,NL04仅有限鼻内复制,未引起死亡或体重下降,提示哺乳动物适应(mammalian adaptation)潜力较低。以NL04为基础的灭活疫苗可诱导强效血凝抑制(HI, hemagglutination inhibition)抗体,免疫鸡同源攻毒后排毒期缩短,并可产生针对异源H6N1毒株的交叉中和抗体。研究表明,NL04在实验室条件下维持低致病性,但其高效复制与强免疫原性提示应对商业鸡群保持警惕,凸显了持续禽流感基因组监测的价值。 研究人员综合运用了以下关键技术方法:对采集自河南商丘鸡场的组织样本进行聚合酶链式反应(PCR, polymerase chain reaction)鉴定与鸡胚分离,采用Sanger测序完成全基因组测序,利用MEGA 7.0构建系统进化树解析基因来源与重排模式。在细胞水平利用Madin-Darby犬肾(MDCK, Madin-Darby Canine Kidney)和鸡胚成纤维(CEF, chicken embryo fibroblast)细胞评估病毒复制动力学。通过动物感染实验解析生物学特性:以106.0 EID 50 剂量经眼鼻途径感染2周龄SPF鸡,采集组织及拭子进行病毒滴定与组织病理学/免疫组织化学分析;以同剂量经鼻感染6周龄BALB/c小鼠。将NL04经β-丙内酯(β-BPL, β-propiolactone)灭活后与Montanide ISA 78 VG佐剂乳化,通过测定HI抗体、同源攻毒后口咽与泄殖腔排毒动态及中和实验评价疫苗免疫原性。此外,基于GISAID数据库5029条H6Ny序列,采用时空与宿主分布分析揭示流行病学特征。 Identification, phylogenetic analysis 研究人员从鸡场组织中分离到一株H6N2病毒,全基因组测序命名为NL04。系统进化分析显示,其HA基因属于水禽源H6 group I(ST339-like),NA基因属于H9N2 Y280-like lineage,六个内部基因均来源于鸡源H9N2 G57基因型,证实为完整种间重排事件。尽管PB2和M基因的最近缘序列在基本局部比对搜索工具(BLAST, Basic Local Alignment Search Tool)中来自H3N3/H3N8病毒,但系统进化树将其归入H9N2 G57-like lineage。病毒滴度达107.78 EID 50 /0.1 mL。 Molecular characteristics NL04的HA裂解位点为PQIETR↓G,无连续碱性氨基酸,未检测到Q226L和G228S。NA stalk区缺失并检测到K368N。PB2携带A588V、T598I和A676T;PB1的I368V与雪貂传播性相关;PA的K356R与哺乳动物复制及致病性增加有关;M1中T215A为物种特异性标志,N30D与毒力增强有关;M2的S31N赋予金刚烷胺(amantadine)耐药性;NS1携带P42S、E172K、N205S和P212S。 Study in SPF chicken 以106.00 EID 50 NL04感染SPF鸡后全部存活,大体剖检见哈德氏腺出血及法氏囊轻度肿胀。组织病理学显示气管严重纤毛脱落、肺泡萎缩伴炎症细胞浸润、肾脏肾小球核固缩;免疫组织化学(IHC, immunohistochemistry)证实肺泡上皮细胞存在病毒NP抗原。病变以肺和气管最严重。组织病毒滴度在鼻甲(105.56 EID 50 /0.1 mL)和哈德氏腺(104.23 EID 50 /0.1 mL)最高,气管和支气管均为101.82 EID 50 /0.1 mL。 Study in mouse and replication kinetics NL04感染BALB/c小鼠后未引起死亡或显著体重下降,仅肺部轻度炎症及肺泡上皮细胞病毒抗原阳性。组织病毒滴度在鼻甲为103.25 EID 50 /0.1 mL,肺为101.56 EID 50 /0.1 reaction)鉴定与鸡胚分离,采用Sanger测序完成全基因组测序,利用MEGA 7.0构建系统进化树解析基因来源与重排模式。在细胞水平利用Madin-Darby犬肾(MDCK, Madin-Darby Canine Kidney)和鸡胚成纤维(CEF, chicken embryo fibroblast)细胞评估病毒复制动力学。通过动物感染实验解析生物学特性:以10EID剂量经眼鼻途径感染2周龄SPF鸡,采集组织及拭子进行病毒滴定与组织病理学/免疫组织化学分析;以同剂量经鼻感染6周龄BALB/c小鼠。将NL04经β-丙内酯(β-BPL, β-propiolactone)灭活后与Montanide ISA 78 VG佐剂乳化,通过测定HI抗体、同源攻毒后口咽与泄殖腔排毒动态及中和实验评价疫苗免疫原性。此外,基于GISAID数据库5029条H6Ny序列,采用时空与宿主分布分析揭示流行病学特征。Identification, phylogenetic analysis研究人员从鸡场组织中分离到一株H6N2病毒,全基因组测序命名为NL04。系统进化分析显示,其HA基因属于水禽源H6 group I(ST339-like),NA基因属于H9N2 Y280-like lineage,六个内部基因均来源于鸡源H9N2 G57基因型,证实为完整种间重排事件。尽管PB2和M基因的最近缘序列在基本局部比对搜索工具(BLAST, Basic Local Alignment Search Tool)中来自H3N3/H3N8病毒,但系统进化树将其归入H9N2 G57-like lineage。病毒滴度达10EID/0.1 mL。Molecular characteristicsNL04的HA裂解位点为PQIETR↓G,无连续碱性氨基酸,未检测到Q226L和G228S。NA stalk区缺失并检测到K368N。PB2携带A588V、T598I和A676T;PB1的I368V与雪貂传播性相关;PA的K356R与哺乳动物复制及致病性增加有关;M1中T215A为物种特异性标志,N30D与毒力增强有关;M2的S31N赋予金刚烷胺(amantadine)耐药性;NS1携带P42S、E172K、N205S和P212S。Study in SPF chicken以10EIDNL04感染SPF鸡后全部存活,大体剖检见哈德氏腺出血及法氏囊轻度肿胀。组织病理学显示气管严重纤毛脱落、肺泡萎缩伴炎症细胞浸润、肾脏肾小球核固缩;免疫组织化学(IHC, immunohistochemistry)证实肺泡上皮细胞存在病毒NP抗原。病变以肺和气管最严重。组织病毒滴度在鼻甲(10EID/0.1 mL)和哈德氏腺(10EID/0.1 mL)最高,气管和支气管均为10EID/0.1 mL。Study in mouse and replication kineticsNL04感染BALB/c小鼠后未引起死亡或显著体重下降,仅肺部轻度炎症及肺泡上皮细胞病毒抗原阳性。组织病毒滴度在鼻甲为10EID/0.1 mL,肺为10EID/0.1 mL。体外复制显示,NL04在MDCK和CEF细胞中有效增殖,CEF细胞在12至48小时支持更高产量,峰值分别出现在36至48小时和60小时。Temporal trends, host range, and subtype diversity of H6Ny viruses基于GISAID数据库5029条H6Ny序列(1963–2025),H6Ny病毒于1990年代末急剧上升,2014年达约440株峰值。禽类占91.7%,环境样本占6.4%,哺乳动物与人极为罕见。H6N2占30.98%,H6N6占28.08%。H6N2已显著溢出到家鸡(145株)。Discussion研究人员指出,NL04的重排模式有别于既往仅获得单一H9N2片段的H6N2病毒,其HA、NA及内部基因的差异提示H6与H9N2已发生深度基因交流。H9N2内部基因骨架可能通过改善聚合酶功能兼容性提高禽类复制效率,解释了NL04在鸡胚和CEF中的高滴度增殖,并提示其可作为疫苗候选种子病毒。SPF鸡实验显示,大体病变缺失并不等同于组织损伤轻微,病理检查更为敏感。NL04在SPF鸡中的轻度表型与商业鸡群15%死亡率差异显著,商业化环境中的高密度饲养应激及大肠杆菌(Escherichia coli)、支原体(Mycoplasma)等继发感染可能是田间严重表现的重要原因,凸显了SPF模型推演至真实农场的固有局限。疫苗方面,免疫鸡高HI抗体水平可能归因于H9N2内部基因盒的高抗原载荷及水禽源HA的强免疫原性;免疫鸡攻毒后排毒期缩短,血清可中和异源H6N1毒株,表明疫苗可诱导交叉中和活性,但攻毒后组织指标未测定。小鼠模型中NL04复制有限,提示哺乳动物适应潜力低,虽携带PB2-V588、PA-R356及NA stalk缺失等非典型替换,但在NL04背景下尚不足以赋予robust的哺乳动物复制,实际功能有待反向遗传学验证。全球数据表明H6人感染极为罕见,当前条件下NL04的人畜共患溢出风险较低。研究人员总结认为,该病毒成功建立提示多种A型流感病毒共循环,H6重排病毒的临床影响可能被H9N2地方流行所掩盖,但频繁重排强化了对水禽、野鸟及商业家禽开展增强型纵向监测的价值。Limitations未开展体外受体结合实验;未包含气溶胶(aerosol)传播实验;仅依赖单一分离株;未在商业化鸡群中攻毒;未测定肠道病毒滴度。ConclusionsNL04为新型重排病毒,其特征为水禽源H6 HA、H9N2 Y280-like NA及G57基因型六个内部基因。本研究首次对该特定基因型在禽类及哺乳动物宿主中进行了全面表型评估。结果表明,NL04在SPF鸡中维持低致病性,但其高效复制及强免疫原性提示应对商业鸡群密切监测。研究强化了对禽群开展持续流感病毒基因组监测的价值,以追踪新发重排病毒的进化与出现。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 source_language_evidence.time: “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 中国河南家禽来源H9N2来源NA及内部基因H6N2新型禽流感重排病毒的表征与疫苗诱导免疫 2025年12月,研究人员从中国河南省一次造成15%田间死亡率并伴随严重呼吸道疾病的鸡群疫情中分离到一株H6N2禽流感(AIV)病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04)。全基因组测序证实该病毒为新型重排体,其携带水禽源H6亚型血凝素(HA, hemagglutinin)基因、H9N2亚型神经氨酸酶(NA, neuraminidase)基因以及H9N2 G57基因型的完整内部基因盒(internal-gene cassette)。尽管NL04在实验感染无特定病原体(SPF, specific-pathogen-free)鸡后仅引起轻度临床症状并表现出100%存活率,但研究人员观察到其呼吸道组织存在显著的组织病理学损伤,揭示了实验室结局与田间严重报告的死亡率之间存在明显的表型差异,而这种差异可能由商业化农场的复杂风险因素所驱动。SPF鸡的组织病毒载量在鼻甲(nasal turbinates)和哈德氏腺(Harderian gland)中达到峰值,证实该病毒具有显著的呼吸道嗜性。在BALB/c小鼠中,NL04表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明其哺乳动物适应(mammalian-adaptation)潜力较低。研究人员进一步评估了以NL04为基础的灭活疫苗候选株。该疫苗诱导了强效的体液免疫(humoral immunity),在减少同源攻毒(homologous challenge)后病毒排毒方面表现出效果,并可诱导针对异源H6N1分离株的交叉中和抗体(cross-neutralizing antibodies)。研究结果凸显了这一独特H6N2重排体的兽医意义,并强调了对家禽开展持续基因组监测(genomic surveillance)的价值,以防范新出现的禽流感威胁。

source_language_evidence.brief_en: 来源于中国河南家禽的H9N2来源NA及内部基因H6N2新型重排禽流感病毒的鉴定、致病特性与灭活疫苗免疫原性研究 《Veterinary Research》:Characterization and vaccine-induced immunity of a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus with H9N2-derived NA and internal genes from poultry in Henan, China 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Veterinary Research 3.8 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 中国河南家禽来源H9N2来源NA及内部基因H6N2新型禽流感重排病毒的表征与疫苗诱导免疫 2025年12月,研究人员从中国河南省一次造成15%田间死亡率并伴随严重呼吸道疾病的鸡群疫情中分离到一株H6N2禽流感(AIV)病毒(A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025,NL04)。全基因组测序证实该病毒为新型重排体,其携带水禽源H6亚型血凝素(HA, hemagglutinin)基因、H9N2亚型神经氨酸酶(NA, neuraminidase)基因以及H9N2 G57基因型的完整内部基因盒(internal-gene cassette)。尽管NL04在实验感染无特定病原体(SPF, specific-pathogen-free)鸡后仅引起轻度临床症状并表现出100%存活率,但研究人员观察到其呼吸道组织存在显著的组织病理学损伤,揭示了实验室结局与田间严重报告的死亡率之间存在明显的表型差异,而这种差异可能由商业化农场的复杂风险因素所驱动。SPF鸡的组织病毒载量在鼻甲(nasal turbinates)和哈德氏腺(Harderian gland)中达到峰值,证实该病毒具有显著的呼吸道嗜性。在BALB/c小鼠中,NL04表现出有限的鼻腔复制,表明其哺乳动物适应(mammalian-adaptation)潜力较低。研究人员进一步评估了以NL04为基础的灭活疫苗候选株。该疫苗诱导了强效的体液免疫(humoral immunity),在减少同源攻毒(homologous challenge)后病毒排毒方面表现出效果,并可诱导针对异源H6N1分离株的交叉中和抗体(cross-neutralizing antibodies)。研究结果凸显了这一独特H6N2重排体的兽医意义,并强调了对家禽开展持续基因组监测(genomic surveillance)的价值,以防范新出现的禽流感威胁。 禽流感病毒(AIV, avian influ。

news.source_body_en: New bird flu cases have been reported in California's dairy herds, prompting state agricultural and veterinary officials to seek urgent vaccine measures. The article highlights the emergence of avian-origin zoonotic infections and the potential risk they pose. While the exact number of cases, deaths, or exposures is not specified, the situation has raised concerns about the spread of the virus and the need for immediate action. Officials are emphasizing the importance of vaccination to mitigate the impact on both animal and human populations. The article does not provide detailed information on the current status of the investigation or any confirmed results, leaving some uncertainty about the full extent of the outbreak and its implications for public health and the dairy industry.
news.content_zh: 加州奶牛场报告了新的禽流感病例,促使该州农业和兽医官员寻求紧急 疫苗 措施。这篇文章强调了禽源人畜共患感染的出现及其带来的潜在风险。虽然没有具体说明病例、死亡或接触的确切数量,但这种情况引起了人们对病毒传播的担忧,并需要立即采取行动。官员们强调 疫苗接种 对于减轻对动物和人类影响的重要性。该文章没有提供有关调查现状或任何已确认结果的详细信息,因此对 暴发 的全面范围及其对公共卫生和乳制品行业的影响存在一些不确定性。

news.content: 2025—2026年南非2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感分子流行病学研究:欧洲基因型EA-2024-DI.2引入、沿海海鸟传播与逆向迁移机制 《Transboundary and Emerging Diseases》:Molecular Epidemiology of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza in South Africa, 2025–2026 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Transboundary and Emerging Diseases 2.6 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article Open Access Goose/Guangdong(Gs/GD,鹅/广东)谱系2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感(High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza,HPAI)病毒对大流行家禽产业和野生动物保护构成严重威胁。继2017年至2023年间南半球两次重大动物疫情之后,2.3.4.4b分支H5N1 HPAI的一种新分支于2025年6月在南非出现。为建立进化和传播动态,研究人员对商业家禽和多种野生鸟类群体的代表性病毒进行了测序和分析,采用最大似然法(Maximum Likelihood,ML)和时标贝叶斯最大分支可信度(Time-scaled Maximum Clade Credibility,MCC)系统发育树来确定亚基因型并追踪病毒扩散。特定遗传标记得到了评估。对125个新基因组序列的系统发育分析揭示了一种来自欧洲的EA-2024-DI.2基因型的独特引入。商业家禽病例显著低于此前波次,但沿海群居海鸟出现了大规模暴发。一种特定的沿海海鸟谱系在整个夏季持续存在,并沿海岸向北传播至纳米比亚,与过去的动物疫情相似。研究结果表明,北半球入侵呈现出新兴的4年周期性趋势。此外,气候驱动的野生鸭载体水资源可利用性可能触发了从未有过的从南部沿海区域返回南非北部内陆的反向病毒迁移。这些发现为未来流行病学风险评估提供了重要基线,并强调了区域协调野生鸟类监测与针对性疫苗接种策略的紧迫性。 Goose/Guangdong(Gs/GD,鹅/广东)谱系2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感(High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza,HPAI)病毒持续对全球家禽产业和野生动物保护构成严峻威胁。2000年代中期,该谱系病毒通过回溢事件在迁徙水禽中建立自然储存库,随后H5Nx HPAI后代病毒持续重配与多样化,在北半球水禽繁殖地定殖并沿季节性迁徙路线跨洲传播。2017年至2023年间,南半球先后经历两次重大疫情:2017—2019年为H5N8基因型EA-2020-A疫情,2021—2023年为H5N1基因型EA-2020-C疫情,导致南非遭受数亿美元直接损失、控制措施成本与贸易禁令,并造成非洲企鹅(Spheniscus demersus)和南非鸬鹚(Phalacrocorax capensis)等濒危物种种群大规模死亡。2024年4月前南非仅偶见沿海海鸟病例,此后至2025年6月下旬未再检出。2025年6月21日,东部姆普马兰加省Piet Retief肉种鸡场暴发疫情,6月25日西北省Boischpoort另一肉种鸡场疫情,此后南开普省沿海海鸟死亡激增。纳米比亚与博茨瓦纳也相继报告病例。为厘清此次新暴发的病毒起源、传播动态及遗传驱动因素,研究人员开展了系统性分子流行病学研究,旨在为区域风险评估与防控策略提供关键基线。 欢迎索取10x Genomics的《单细胞基因表达样本制备指南》>> 领 取 在技术方法上,研究人员主要采用最大似然法(Maximum Likelihood,ML)和时标贝叶斯最大分支可信度(Time-scaled Maximum Clade Credibility,MCC)系统发育推断。研究纳入2025年6月至2026年5月间南非及周边地区商业家禽、野生鸟类(含海鸟、水禽及猛禽)及海豹的代表性样本,经实时逆转录聚合酶链式反应(Real-time Reverse Transcription PCR,rRT-PCR)筛选并富集全部8个基因组节段后,利用Ion Torrent技术完成测序与基因组组装。ML树在IQ-Tree中以GTR模型和1000次超快速Bootstrap构建;MCC树则基于BEAST v.2软件,采用HKY替代模型、Coalescent Bayesian Skyline模型及Relaxed Lognormal分子钟运行4000万次马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛(Markov Chain Monte Carlo,MCMC)迭代。氨基酸突变通过FluMutGUI v3.2.0鉴定,病毒基因型通过Genin2分配,系统发育分析整合了GISAID EpiFlu与GenBank数据库中的参考序列。 研究结果显示,基于全基因组系统发育分析,此次疫情由2024年源于欧洲的基因型EA-2024-DI.2引入,最接近参考株为2024年12月乌干达粉嘴巨鸥(Gelochelidon nilotica)携带病毒(EPI_ISL_20349270)。在Origins, Distribution, and Characteristics of Sub-Genotypes部分,研究人员共识别出8种亚基因型。亚基因型1对应初始鸡场疫情,局限于姆普马兰加省东部;亚基因型2的最近共同祖先(Most Recent Common Ancestor,MRCA)追溯至2025年4月中旬,提示早在缺乏主动监测时已引入,Delmas地区两鸡场疫情虽空间邻近却呈现较长分支,且携带PA-T97I、NP-M105V、NP-N319K及M 2 -S31N等毒力相关突变,表明7至8月期间该地区鸡群可能存在隐性循环。亚基因型3主要感染普通燕鸥(Sterna hirundo)、白额燕鸥和非洲企鹅,沿海岸线向东扩散至东伦敦;亚基因型4以南非鸥(Hartlaub's gull)为主,局限于西开普省开普敦都会区,42%病毒含HA-D94N突变(与α 2–6 唾液酸结合偏好相关)。亚基因型5局限于南开普本地出现,见于鸡、埃及雁(Alopochen aegyptiaca)和盔珠鸡(Numida meleagris);亚基因型6分布广泛,从林波波省延伸至西南海岸并影响企鹅,其中企鹅最后测序病例携带PA-P190S和NS 1 -D92E突变。亚基因型7主要见于普通燕鸥,局限于开普敦地区,多数含HA-T188I突变;亚基因型8由亚基因型7经遗传漂变进化而来,在普通燕鸥等群居海鸟中持续存在,传播至纳米比亚。值得注意的是,2026年5月北西省Brits地区惩教所鸡场疫情并非欧洲新亚系EA-2024-DI.2.1,而是本地亚基因型8毒株,其MRCA与西开普省样本追溯至2026年2月初。结合西开普省2025年冬季降水显著偏少与北部内陆2026年异常洪涝,研究人员推测气候驱动的鸭类水资源变化可能介导了从沿海向内陆的反向传播。 在Impact on Coastal Seabird Populations部分,依托南非林业、渔业和环境事务部海洋与海岸信息系统(Oceans and Coastal Information Management System,OCIMS)鸟禽流感报告工具与SANCCOB康复中心数据,2025年7月4日至2026年8月29日共记录39种2728例疑似或确诊HPAI病例。普通燕鸥(n=1031)与南非鸥(n=963)受影响最严重,其次为白额燕鸥(n=188)、银鸥(n=157)和北极燕鸥(n=96)。非洲企鹅确诊45例且19例完成测序,证实存在多来源再感染。本次疫情影响物种数与既往相似,但总病例数最低,且首次出现海鸟繁殖群落严重死亡。在Lower Poultry Case Burden Compared to Past Epizootics部分,官方报告仅确认12起商业家禽与9起后院/小型鸡群疫情,远低于2017—2018年的45起商业疫情与8起后院疫情及2021—2023年的68起商业疫情与34起后院疫情;商用鸵鸟未确认病例,尽管血清学检测到H5特异性抗体,RT-PCR未检出H5病毒RNA。家禽病例锐减的原因尚不明确,可能与病毒表型变化、生产者生物安全干预或环境与生物安全因素共同相关。 在讨论与结论部分,研究人员指出本次疫情与2017年及2021年疫情存在相似流行病学特征:病毒于南半球初夏(约4至5月)以遗传多样性变体形式传入,冬季在野生鸟类与家禽中升级,春季随气温升高消退。然而,本次疫情呈现到达南开普的病毒遗传多样性更高、家禽溢出显著减少,以及沿海海鸟谱系向内陆逆向传播等显著差异。在两次既往疫情中,仅有一个亚基因型在首波抵达南开普,而本次则有多种亚基因型共存并迅速引发沿海海鸟感染。研究人员提出,2017、2021、2025年三次疫情间隔约4年,提示亚热带地区可能因鸭群聚集密度较低及高温环境不利于病毒长期存活而不易形成HPAI地方化,但约4年的进化窗口可能使循环病毒积累足够的抗原性修饰或适应性性状,以突破非洲热带鸭群免疫屏障并引发疫情。若该周期持续,下一次Gs/GD 2.3.4.4b H5Nx HPAI传入预计于2029年秋季出现。研究结论强调,基因组测序对追踪起源、传播动态、重配事件及宿主适应性突变不可或缺;此次新增的125条序列极大扩展了对非洲大陆尤其是亚热带生态系统病毒流行病学的理解。鉴于非洲基因组数据持续匮乏,研究人员呼吁建立协调的亚区域主动野生鸟类监测计划,评估对受威胁野生鸟类及当地家禽实施针对性疫苗接种的必要性,并警惕气候变化对未来病毒扩散模式的深远影响。欧亚大陆HPAI的地方化状态已构成经由南迁飞行路线传入南半球的永久威胁,该风险将随区域家禽产业发展而上升;同时,来自亚南极地区经远洋海鸟传入的可能性亦不能排除。 HPAI后代病毒持续重配与多样化,在北半球水禽繁殖地定殖并沿季节性迁徙路线跨洲传播。2017年至2023年间,南半球先后经历两次重大疫情:2017—2019年为H5N8基因型EA-2020-A疫情,2021—2023年为H5N1基因型EA-2020-C疫情,导致南非遭受数亿美元直接损失、控制措施成本与贸易禁令,并造成非洲企鹅(Spheniscus demersus)和南非鸬鹚(Phalacrocorax capensis)等濒危物种种群大规模死亡。2024年4月前南非仅偶见沿海海鸟病例,此后至2025年6月下旬未再检出。2025年6月21日,东部姆普马兰加省Piet Retief肉种鸡场暴发疫情,6月25日西北省Boischpoort另一肉种鸡场疫情,此后南开普省沿海海鸟死亡激增。纳米比亚与博茨瓦纳也相继报告病例。为厘清此次新暴发的病毒起源、传播动态及遗传驱动因素,研究人员开展了系统性分子流行病学研究,旨在为区域风险评估与防控策略提供关键基线。 欢迎索取10x Genomics的《单细胞基因表达样本制备指南》>> 领 取 在技术方法上,研究人员主要采用最大似然法(Maximum Likelihood,ML)和时标贝叶斯最大分支可信度(Time-scaled Maximum Clade Credibility,MCC)系统发育推断。研究纳入2025年6月至2026年5月间南非及周边地区商业家禽、野生鸟类(含海鸟、水禽及猛禽)及海豹的代表性样本,经实时逆转录聚合酶链式反应(Real-time Reverse Transcription PCR,rRT-PCR)筛选并富集全部8个基因组节段后,利用Ion Torrent技术完成测序与基因组组装。ML树在IQ-Tree中以GTR模型和1000次超快速Bootstrap构建;MCC树则基于BEAST v.2软件,采用HKY替代模型、Coalescent Bayesian Skyline模型及Relaxed 研究结果显示,基于全基因组系统发育分析,此次疫情由2024年源于欧洲的基因型EA-2024-DI.2引入,最接近参考株为2024年12月乌干达粉嘴巨鸥(Gelochelidon nilotica)携带病毒(EPI_ISL_20349270)。在Origins, Distribution, and Characteristics of Sub-Genotypes部分,研究人员共识别出8种亚基因型。亚基因型1对应初始鸡场疫情,局限于姆普马兰加省东部;亚基因型2的最近共同祖先(Most Recent Common Ancestor,MRCA)追溯至2025年4月中旬,提示早在缺乏主动监测时已引入,Delmas地区两鸡场疫情虽空间邻近却呈现较长分支,且携带PA-T97I、NP-M105V、NP-N319K及M 2 -S31N等毒力相关突变,表明7至8月期间该地区鸡群可能存在隐性循环。亚基因型3主要感染普通燕鸥(Sterna hirundo)、白额燕鸥和非洲企鹅,沿海岸线向东扩散至东伦敦;亚基因型4以南非鸥(Hartlaub's gull)为主,局限于西开普省开普敦都会区,42%病毒含HA-D94N突变(与α 2–6 唾液酸结合偏好相关)。亚基因型5局限于南开普本地出现,见于鸡、埃及雁(Alopochen 在Impact on Coastal Seabird Populations部分,依托南非林业、渔业和环境事务部海洋与海岸信息系统(Oceans and Coastal Information Management Poultry Case Burden Compared to Past Epizootics部分,官方报告仅确认12起商业家禽与9起后院/小型鸡群疫情,远低于2017—2018年的45起商业疫情与8起后院疫情及2021—2023年的68起商业疫情与34起后院疫情;商用鸵鸟未确认病例,尽管血清学检测到H5特异性抗体,RT-PCR未检出H5病毒RNA。家禽病例锐减的原因尚不明确,可能与病毒表型变化、生产者生物安全干预或环境与生物安全因素共同相关。 2.3.4.4b H5Nx HPAI传入预计于2029年秋季出现。研究结论强调,基因组测序对追踪起源、传播动态、重配事件及宿主适应性突变不可或缺;此次新增的125条序列极大扩展了对非洲大陆尤其是亚热带生态系统病毒流行病学的理解。鉴于非洲基因组数据持续匮乏,研究人员呼吁建立协调的亚区域主动野生鸟类监测计划,评估对受威胁野生鸟类及当地家禽实施针对性疫苗接种的必要性,并警惕气候变化对未来病毒扩散模式的深远影响。欧亚大陆HPAI的地方化状态已构成经由南迁飞行路线传入南半球的永久威胁,该风险将随区域家禽产业发展而上升;同时,来自亚南极地区经远洋海鸟传入的可能性亦不能排除。 source_language_evidence.time: “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article Open Access Goose/Guangdong(Gs/GD,鹅/广东)谱系2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感(High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza,HPAI)病毒对大流行家禽产业和野生动物保护构成严重威胁。继2017年至2023年间南半球两次重大动物疫情之后,2.3.4.4b分支H5N1 HPAI的一种新分支于2025年6月在南非出现。为建立进化和传播动态,研究人员对商业家禽和多种野生鸟类群体的代表性病毒进行了测序和分析,采用最大似然法(Maximum Likelihood,ML)和时标贝叶斯最大分支可信度(Time-scaled Maximum Clade Credibility,MCC)系统发育树来确定亚基因型并追踪病毒扩散。特定遗传标记得到了评估。对125个新基因组序列的系统发育分析揭示了一种来自欧洲的EA-2024-DI.2基因型的独特引入。商业家禽病例显著低于此前波次,但沿海群居海鸟出现了大规模暴发。一种特定的沿海海鸟谱系在整个夏季持续存在,并沿海岸向北传播至纳米比亚,与过去的动物疫情相似。研究结果表明,北半球入侵呈现出新兴的4年周期性趋势。此外,气候驱动的野生鸭载体水资源可利用性可能触发了从未有过的从南部沿海区域返回南非北部内陆的反向病毒迁移。这些发现为未来流行病学风险评估提供了重要基线,并强调了区域协调野生鸟类监测与针对性疫苗接种策略的紧迫性。
source_language_evidence.location_and_population: 2025—2026年南非2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感分子流行病学研究:欧洲基因型EA-2024-DI.2引入、沿海海鸟传播与逆向迁移机制 《Transboundary and Emerging Diseases》:Molecular Epidemiology of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza in South Africa, 2025–2026 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Transboundary and Emerging Diseases 2.6 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送!
source_language_evidence.event: 在Impact on Coastal Seabird Populations部分,依托南非林业、渔业和环境事务部海洋与海岸信息系统(Oceans and Coastal Information Management System,OCIMS)鸟禽流感报告工具与SANCCOB康复中心数据,2025年7月4日至2026年8月29日共记录39种2728例疑似或确诊HPAI病例。普通燕鸥(n=1031)与南非鸥(n=963)受影响最严重,其次为白额燕鸥(n=188)、银鸥(n=157)和北极燕鸥(n=96)。非洲企鹅确诊45例且19例完成测序,证实存在多来源再感染。本次疫情影响物种数与既往相似,但总病例数最低,且首次出现海鸟繁殖群落严重死亡。在Lower Poultry Case Burden Compared to Past Epizootics部分,官方报告仅确认12起商业家禽与9起后院/小型鸡群疫情,远低于2017—2018年的45起商业疫情与8起后院疫情及2021—2023年的68起商业疫情与34起后院疫情;商用鸵鸟未确认病例,尽管血清学检测到H5特异性抗体,RT-PCR未检出H5病毒RNA。家禽病例锐减的原因尚不明确,可能与病毒表型变化、生产者生物安全干预或环境与生物安全因素共同相关。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: 在讨论与结论部分,研究人员指出本次疫情与2017年及2021年疫情存在相似流行病学特征:病毒于南半球初夏(约4至5月)以遗传多样性变体形式传入,冬季在野生鸟类与家禽中升级,春季随气温升高消退。然而,本次疫情呈现到达南开普的病毒遗传多样性更高、家禽溢出显著减少,以及沿海海鸟谱系向内陆逆向传播等显著差异。在两次既往疫情中,仅有一个亚基因型在首波抵达南开普,而本次则有多种亚基因型共存并迅速引发沿海海鸟感染。研究人员提出,2017、2021、2025年三次疫情间隔约4年,提示亚热带地区可能因鸭群聚集密度较低及高温环境不利于病毒长期存活而不易形成HPAI地方化,但约4年的进化窗口可能使循环病毒积累足够的抗原性修饰或适应性性状,以突破非洲热带鸭群免疫屏障并引发疫情。若该周期持续,下一次Gs/GD 2.3.4.4b H5Nx HPAI传入预计于2029年秋季出现。研究结论强调,基因组测序对追踪起源、传播动态、重配事件及宿主适应性突变不可或缺;此次新增的125条序列极大扩展了对非洲大陆尤其是亚热带生态系统病毒流行病学的理解。鉴于非洲基因组数据持续匮乏,研究人员呼吁建立协调的亚区域主动野生鸟类监测计划,评估对受威胁野生鸟类及当地家禽实施针对性疫苗接种的必要性,并警惕气候变化对未来病毒扩散模式的深远影响。欧亚大陆HPAI的地方化状态已构成经由南迁飞行路线传入南半球的永久威胁,该风险将随区域家禽产业发展而上升;同时,来自亚南极地区经远洋海鸟传入的可能性亦不能排除。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 2025—2026年南非2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感分子流行病学研究:欧洲基因型EA-2024-DI.2引入、沿海海鸟传播与逆向迁移机制 《Transboundary and Emerging Diseases》:Molecular Epidemiology of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza in South Africa, 2025–2026 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Transboundary and Emerging Diseases 2.6 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article Open Access Goose/Guangdong(Gs/GD,鹅/广东)谱系2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感(High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza,HPAI)病毒对大流行家禽产业和野生动物保护构成严重威胁。继2017年至2023年间南半球两次重大动物疫情之后,2.3.4.4b分支H5N1 HPAI的一种新分支于2025年6月在南非出现。为建立进化和传播动态,研究人员对商业家禽和多种野生鸟类群体的代表性病毒进行了测序和分析,采用最大似然法(Maximum Likelihood,ML)和时标贝叶斯最大分支可信度(Time-scaled Maximum Clade Credibility,MCC)系统发育树来确定亚基因型并追踪病毒扩散。特定遗传标记得到了评估。对125个新基因组序列的系统发育分析揭示了一种来自欧洲的EA-2024-DI.2基因型的独特引入。商业家禽病例显著低于此前波次,但沿海群居海鸟出现了大规模暴发。一种特定的沿海海鸟谱系在整个夏季持续存在,并沿海岸向北传播至纳米比亚,与过去的动物疫情相似。研究结果表明,北半球入侵呈现出新兴的4年周期性趋势。此外,气候驱动的野生鸭载体水资源可利用性可能触发了从未有过的从南部沿海区域返回南非北部内陆的反向病毒迁移。这些发现为未来流行病学风险评估提供了重要基线,并强调了区域协调野生鸟类监测与针对性疫苗接种策略的紧迫性。 Goose/Guangdong(Gs/GD,鹅/广东)谱系2.3.4.4b分支H5N1高致病性禽流感(High-Pathogenicity Avian Influenza,HPAI)病毒持续对全球家禽产业和野生动物保护构成严峻威胁。2000年代中期,该谱系病毒通过回溢事件在迁徙水禽中建立自然储存库,随后H5Nx HPAI后代病毒持续重配与多样化,在北半球水禽繁殖地定殖并沿季节性迁徙路线跨洲传播。2017年至2023年间,南半球先后。

analysis.brief_en: The Oregon Health Authority (OHA) confirmed the state’s first human case of avian influenza in 2026, as reported by newportnewstimes.com. This marks a significant development in the state's public health monitoring, highlighting the potential for avian influenza to spread to humans. The confirmation was made on November 19, 2026, and the event is tied to Oregon, United States. No specific case count, death count, or exposure count was reported in the evidence. The OHA has acknowledged the case, but no further details on investigation, testing, or response measures were provided. This event is part of the broader surveillance for avian influenza A viruses, which are of particular concern due to their zoonotic potential. The confirmation underscores the importance of continued monitoring and preparedness for such infections, especially in regions where avian influenza outbreaks have been reported in animals.
